functions.name: animcurve_channel_evaluate
functions.description: This function gets the value at a specific point in time from a channel struct.

params.name: channel_struct
params.description: The struct pointer for the channel to evaluate.

params.name: posx

functions.name: animcurve_channel_new
functions.description: This function creates a new animation curve channel struct.

functions.name: animcurve_create
functions.description: This function creates an empty animation curve struct, ready for you to populate with channel data.

functions.name: animcurve_destroy
functions.description: This function destroys an animation curve previously created with the function animcurve_create().

params.name: curve_struct
params.description: The pointer to the curve struct to destroy.

functions.name: animcurve_get
functions.description: This function returns a struct containing all the data for the given animation curve.

params.name: curve_id
params.description: The asset ID (index) of the animation curve to get.

functions.name: animcurve_get_channel
functions.description: This function returns the struct containing the channel data for the channel specified in an animation curve asset or struct (as returned by animcurve_get()).

params.name: curve_struct_or_id
params.description: The ID or struct pointer of the animation curve to target

params.name: channel_name_or_index
params.description: The channel name (a string) or the channel index (an integer)

functions.name: animcurve_get_channel_index
functions.description: This function returns the index value for any given animation curve channel. Note that if the curve or channel does not exist then you will get an error.

params.name: curve_struct_or_id
params.description: The ID or struct pointer of the animation curve to target

params.name: channel_name
params.description: The channel name.

functions.name: animcurve_point_new
functions.description: This function creates a new points struct (posx, value) to be added to an animation curve channel.

functions.name: asset_add_tags
functions.description: This function adds one or more tag strings to any asset from the Asset Browser. You supply either the asset name (as a string) or its asset index, as well as either a single tag string or an array where each item is a single tag string.

params.name: name_or_index
params.description: The name of the asset (a string) or its index value (an integer).

params.name: tags
params.description: A single asset tag string or an array with various asset tags.

params.name: asset_type
params.description: OPTIONAL! The type of asset to set the tags on, only used when supplying an index for the first argument.

functions.name: asset_clear_tags
functions.description: This function clears all tags present on the given asset from the Asset Browser and returns whether any tags were removed. You supply either the asset name (as a string) or its asset index, and if you supply an asset index value, then you will need to supply the optional asset type argument (a constant), as assets of different types can have the same index, even though they cannot have the same name.

params.name: name_or_index
params.description: The name of the asset (a string) or its index value (an integer).

params.name: asset_type
params.description: OPTIONAL! The type of asset to clear the tags from, only used when supplying an index for the first argument.

functions.name: asset_get_index
functions.description: This function gets the handle for a game asset from its name. If the asset is not found, the function will return a value of -1, otherwise it will return the handle for the asset being checked.

params.name: name
params.description: The name of the game asset to get the index of (a string).

functions.name: asset_get_tags
functions.description: This function retrieves all tags assigned to an asset from the Asset Browser. You supply either the asset name (as a string) or its asset index, and the function will return an array of tags for that asset. If no tags are found or there is an error (i.e.: the name string given doesn't exist) then the returned array will be empty.

params.name: name_or_index
params.description: The name of the asset (a string) or its index value (an integer).

params.name: asset_type
params.description: OPTIONAL! The type of asset to get the tags for, only used when supplying an index for the first argument.

functions.name: asset_get_type
functions.description: This function gets the type of asset being referenced from its name.

params.name: name_or_ref
params.description: The name of or a reference to the game asset to get the type of.

functions.name: asset_get_ids
functions.description: This function returns an array containing IDs of all existing assets of given type.

params.name: asset_type
params.description: The type of assets to retrieve an array of.

functions.name: asset_has_tags
functions.description: This function checks if one or more tag strings is assigned to the given asset from the Asset Browser. You supply either the asset name (as a string) or its asset index, as well as either a single tag string or an array where each item is a single tag string.

params.name: name_or_index
params.description: The name of the asset (a string) or its index value (an integer).

params.name: tags
params.description: A single asset tag string or an array with various asset tags.

params.name: asset_type
params.description: OPTIONAL! The type of asset to check the tags for, only used when supplying an index for the first argument.

functions.name: asset_remove_tags
functions.description: This function removes one or more tag strings to any asset from the Asset Browser. You supply either the asset name (as a string) or its asset index, as well as either a single tag string or an array where each item is a single tag string.

params.name: name_or_index
params.description: The name of the asset (a string) or its index value (an integer).

params.name: tags
params.description: A single asset tag string or an array with various asset tags.

params.name: asset_type
params.description: OPTIONAL! The type of asset to remove the tags from, only used when supplying an index for the first argument.

functions.name: tag_get_assets
functions.description: This function retrieves the names of all assets that have been assigned the given tag or tags. You supply either a single tag string or an array, where each item in the array is a tag string.

params.name: tags
params.description: A single asset tag string or an array with various asset tags.

functions.name: tag_get_asset_ids
functions.description: This function gets all the assets of a given type that have the given tags assigned to them. You supply either a single tag (as a string) or an array, where each item in the array is a tag (as a string), as well as the type of asset to check.

params.name: tags
params.description: A single asset tag string or an array with various asset tags.

params.name: asset_type
params.description: An asset type constant (listed above)

functions.name: audio_channel_num
functions.description: With this function you can set how many audio channels are available for playing audio in GameMaker.

params.name: num
params.description: Number of available audio channels (default is 128).

functions.name: audio_create_stream
functions.description: With this function you can create a new sound index which can then be used in the regular audio functions to stream audio directly from an external OGG file source.

params.name: filename
params.description: The file (OGG only) to stream the audio from.

functions.name: audio_debug
functions.description: This function can be used to display debug information about the audio system, with true switching it on and false to switch it off. Enabling this will display the Audio window of The Debug Overlay.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable (set to true) or disable (false) audio debugging.

functions.name: audio_throw_on_error
functions.description: This function can be used to toggle whether errors returned from the audio engine should throw runtime errors which abort the game.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable or disable throwing.

functions.name: audio_destroy_stream
functions.description: This function destroys a previously created audio stream from memory. Any further calls to the sound after it has been destroyed will give an error.

params.name: sound
params.description: The sound asset, as returned by audio_create_stream.

functions.name: audio_exists
functions.description: This function returns whether a Sound Asset exists. The sound to check can either be a single instance of a sound (the index for individual sounds being played can be stored in a variable when using the audio_play_sound or audio_play_sound_at functions) or a sound asset.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to check the existence of.

functions.name: audio_falloff_set_model
functions.description: This function sets the audio falloff model used in your game.

params.name: model
params.description: The constant used to set the falloff model.

functions.name: audio_get_master_gain
functions.description: With this function you can get the absolute value for the global volume of all sounds and music for a specific listener.

params.name: listenerindex
params.description: The index of the listener to get the gain of.

functions.name: audio_get_name
functions.description: This function will return the name of a given audio asset as a string.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to check.

functions.name: audio_get_type
functions.description: This function returns the type of the given sound asset, which can be either streamed (1) or in memory (0).

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to check.

functions.name: audio_is_paused
functions.description: This function will check the given sound to see if it is currently paused.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to check.

functions.name: audio_is_playing
functions.description: This function will check the given sound to see if it is currently playing.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to check.

functions.name: audio_master_gain
functions.description: With this function you can set the absolute value for the global volume of all sounds and music.

params.name: gain
params.description: Value for the global volume (0 to 1).

functions.name: audio_pause_all
functions.description: With this function you can pause all sounds that are currently playing.

functions.name: audio_pause_sound
functions.description: With this function you can pause any sound that is currently playing.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to pause.

functions.name: audio_play_sound
functions.description: This function plays any Sound Asset in your game.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to play.

params.name: priority
params.description: Set the channel priority for the sound.

params.name: loop
params.description: Sets the sound to loop or not.

params.name: gain
params.description: Sets the gain of the sound played.

params.name: offset
params.description: Sets the start offset (in seconds) of the sound played.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Sets the pitch of the sound played.

params.name: listener_mask
params.description: Sets the listener mask of the sound played.

functions.name: audio_play_sound_at
functions.description: With this function you can play any sound asset at a given position within the audio space.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to play.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position.

params.name: z
params.description: The z position.

params.name: falloff_ref
params.description: The falloff reference relative to the listener (clamp).

params.name: falloff_max
params.description: The maximum falloff distance relative to the listener.

params.name: falloff_factor
params.description: The falloff factor (default 1).

params.name: loop
params.description: Flags the sound as looping or not.

params.name: priority
params.description: Set the channel priority for the sound.

params.name: gain
params.description: Sets the gain of the sound played.

params.name: offset
params.description: Sets the start offset (in seconds) of the sound played.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Sets the pitch of the sound played.

params.name: listener_mask
params.description: Sets the listener mask of the sound played.

functions.signature: audio_play_sound_at(index, x, y, z, falloff_ref, falloff_max, falloff_factor, loop, priority, [gain], [offset], [pitch], [listener_mask])

functions.name: audio_play_sound_ext
functions.description: This function plays any sound asset in your game using any combination of parameters.

params.name: params
params.description: A struct containing a set of playback parameters.

functions.name: audio_sound_get_asset
functions.description: This function returns the Sound Asset that was used to play the given Sound Instance ID. The sound must be active (i.e. currently playing) for this function to return the correct value, otherwise it will throw a fatal error.

params.name: index
params.description: The voice index of the sound.

functions.name: audio_resume_all
functions.description: With this function you can resume all sounds that have been paused previously.

functions.name: audio_resume_sound
functions.description: With this function you can resume any sound that is currently paused (after using the function audio_pause_sound()).

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to resume.

functions.name: audio_set_master_gain
functions.description: With this function you can set the absolute value for the global volume of all sounds and music for a specific listener. The default listener index is 0, but you can use the function audio_get_listener_info() to get the different indices available for the target platform.

params.name: listenerindex
params.description: The index of the listener to set the gain on.

params.name: gain
params.description: Value for the global volume (0 to 1).

functions.name: audio_sound_gain
functions.description: With this function you can fade a sound in or out over a given length of time, or it can be used to set the sound gain instantly.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to set the gain for.

params.name: volume
params.description: Value for the music volume.

params.name: time
params.description: The length for the change in gain in milliseconds.

functions.name: audio_sound_get_gain
functions.description: This function will return the current gain value for the given sound.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to get the gain of.

functions.name: audio_sound_get_listener_mask
functions.description: This function will return the bit-mask data that defines which audio listeners a sound should be played from.

params.name: soundid
params.description: The unique ID of the sound to get the mask of

functions.name: audio_sound_get_pitch
functions.description: This function can be used to get the pitch of a given sound.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to get the pitch of.

functions.name: audio_sound_get_track_position
functions.description: This function will get the position (in seconds) within the sound file for the sound to play from.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to get the play position of.

functions.name: audio_sound_is_playable
functions.description: This function can be used to check if the given sound index can be played currently.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to check.

functions.name: audio_sound_length
functions.description: This function returns the length of the given sound in seconds.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to check.

functions.name: audio_sound_pitch
functions.description: This function changes the pitch of the given sound asset or instance.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to change.

params.name: pitch
params.description: The pitch multiplier (default 1).

functions.name: audio_sound_set_listener_mask
functions.description: This function can be used to set the the bit-mask for a sound so that it will play only from those listeners specified.

params.name: soundid
params.description: The unique ID of the sound to set the mask of

params.name: mask
params.description: The bitmask data to set for the sound

functions.name: audio_sound_set_track_position
functions.description: This function will set the position (in seconds) for the given sound ID or asset.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to change.

params.name: time
params.description: The time (in seconds) to set the start point to.

functions.name: audio_sound_loop
functions.description: This function will set the state of a playing sound's loop section.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to change.

params.name: state
params.description: The state that the loop section should be set to.

functions.name: audio_sound_get_loop
functions.description: This function will return the state of a playing sound's loop section.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound whose loop section state is retrieved.

functions.name: audio_sound_loop_start
functions.description: This function will set the offset (in seconds) of the start of a sound's loop section.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to change.

params.name: time
params.description: The offset (in seconds) to set the start of the loop section to.

functions.name: audio_sound_get_loop_start
functions.description: This function will return the offset (in seconds) of the start of a sound's loop section.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound whose loop-start is retrieved.

functions.name: audio_sound_loop_end
functions.description: This function will set the offset (in seconds) of the end of a sound's loop section.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to change.

params.name: time
params.description: The offset (in seconds) to set the end of the loop section to.

functions.name: audio_sound_get_loop_end
functions.description: This function will return the offset (in seconds) of the end of a sound's loop section.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound whose loop-end is retrieved.

functions.name: audio_stop_all
functions.description: This function will stop all sounds that are currently playing.

functions.name: audio_stop_sound
functions.description: This function will stop the given sound if it is currently playing. This includes all sounds that have been paused using audio_pause_sound or audio_pause_all.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sound to stop.

functions.name: audio_system_is_available
functions.description: This function can be used to check and see if the audio system has been initialised, or if the audio context is running.

functions.name: audio_system_is_initialised
functions.description: This function can be used to check if the audio engine has been initialised, after which all audio functions can be called normally.

functions.name: audio_create_buffer_sound
functions.description: With this function you can create a new sound from the contents of a buffer.

params.name: bufferId
params.description: The ID of the buffer to use.

params.name: bufferFormat
params.description: The format of the data in the buffer (buffer_u8 or buffer_s16).

params.name: bufferRate
params.description: The sample rate of the data in the buffer.

params.name: bufferOffset
params.description: The offset into the buffer to read the sample data from (in bytes).

params.name: bufferLength
params.description: The length of the buffer (the number of bytes of audio data, excluding the header).

params.name: bufferChannels
params.description: The channels to use (audio_mono, audio_stereo or audio_3D).

functions.signature: audio_create_buffer_sound(bufferId, bufferFormat, bufferRate, bufferOffset, bufferLength, bufferChannels)

functions.name: audio_create_play_queue
functions.description: This function prepares a buffer queue for audio.

params.name: queueformat
params.description: The format of the buffer data to use (buffer_u8 or buffer_s16).

params.name: queuerate
params.description: The sample rate of the data in the buffer queue.

params.name: queuechannels
params.description: A constant specifying the channels to use.

functions.name: audio_free_buffer_sound
functions.description: With this function you can free up the pointer index value associated with the sound ID.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the buffered sound to free.

functions.name: audio_free_play_queue
functions.description: This function is used to free up the memory associated with the given audio queue.

params.name: queueindex
params.description: The index of the queue to free.

functions.name: audio_get_recorder_count
functions.description: This function will return the number of audio recording sources (like microphones, etc.) currently available to your game.

functions.name: audio_get_recorder_info
functions.description: This function will return a DS Map with information about the given recorder source index.

params.name: recorder_index
params.description: The index of the recorder source to get the information from.

functions.name: audio_queue_sound
functions.description: This function will add the data from a buffer into the audio queue that you previously created using the function audio_create_play_queue().

params.name: queueindex
params.description: The index of the queue to add to.

params.name: bufferid
params.description: The buffer to add to the queue.

params.name: bufferoffset
params.description: The offset within the source buffer to start from.

params.name: bufferlength
params.description: The length of the buffer (the number of the bytes in the buffer).

functions.name: audio_start_recording
functions.description: This function will start recording audio from the recorder source indexed.

params.name: recorder_index
params.description: The index of the recorder source to use.

functions.name: audio_stop_recording
functions.description: This function will stop recording on the given recorder channel (the channel index is returned when you call the function audio_start_recording()).

params.name: channel_index
params.description: The index of the recorder channel to stop.

functions.name: audio_emitter_create
functions.description: This function creates a new audio emitter and returns the index for it.

functions.name: audio_emitter_exists
functions.description: This function returns whether an audio emitter exists (true) or not (false).

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the emitter to check the existence of.

functions.name: audio_emitter_falloff
functions.description: With this function you can set the fall-off distance for an emitter.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to change.

params.name: falloff_ref
params.description: The falloff reference relative to the listener (clamp).

params.name: falloff_max
params.description: The maximum falloff distance relative to the listener.

params.name: falloff_factor
params.description: The falloff factor (default 1).

functions.name: audio_emitter_free
functions.description: With this function you can remove the given emitter from memory.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to free.

functions.name: audio_emitter_gain
functions.description: This function sets the maximum gain (volume) for the sound.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to change.

params.name: gain
params.description: The maximum gain (default 1).

params.name: time
params.description: The length for the change in gain in milliseconds.

functions.name: audio_emitter_get_gain
functions.description: This function returns the current gain (volume) set for the given audio emitter, normally between 0 and 1, where 0 is silent and 1 is full volume.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to use.

functions.name: audio_emitter_get_listener_mask
functions.description: This function will return the bit-mask data that defines which audio listeners an emitter should play sounds from.

params.name: emitterid
params.description: The unique ID of the emitter to get the mask of

functions.name: audio_emitter_get_pitch
functions.description: This function returns the current pitch value set for the given audio emitter.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to use.

functions.name: audio_emitter_get_vx
functions.description: This function returns the current velocity along the x axis for the given audio emitter.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to use.

functions.name: audio_emitter_get_vy
functions.description: This function returns the current velocity along the y axis for the given audio emitter.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to use.

functions.name: audio_emitter_get_vz
functions.description: This function returns the current velocity along the z axis for the given audio emitter.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to use.

functions.name: audio_emitter_get_x
functions.description: This function returns the current x position of the given audio emitter.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to use.

functions.name: audio_emitter_get_y
functions.description: This function returns the current y position of the given audio emitter.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to use.

functions.name: audio_emitter_get_z
functions.description: This function returns the current z position of the given audio emitter.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to use.

functions.name: audio_emitter_pitch
functions.description: This function can be used to change the pitch of all sounds emitted from the given emitter. It is a pitch multiplier, in that the input value multiplies the current pitch by that amount, so the default value of 1 is no pitch change, while a value of less than 1 will lower the pitch and greater than 1 will raise the pitch.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to change.

params.name: pitch
params.description: The pitch multiplier (default 1).

functions.name: audio_emitter_position
functions.description: With this function you can change the position of an audio emitter within the 3D audio space. The position will affect the sound in different ways depending on where the listener is positioned within the audio space too (the default position is (0, 0, 0)).

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to change.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position.

params.name: z
params.description: The z position.

functions.name: audio_emitter_set_listener_mask
functions.description: This function can be used to set the the bit-mask for an emitter so that all sounds played through the emitter will play only from those listeners specified.

params.name: emitterid
params.description: The unique ID of the emitter to set the mask of

params.name: mask
params.description: The bitmask data to set for the sound

functions.name: audio_emitter_velocity
functions.description: This function can be used to give an emitter Doppler effects and simulate audio motion based on the vector that is resolved from the given relative x, y and z positions.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to change.

params.name: vx
params.description: The x vector value (default 0).

params.name: vy
params.description: The y vector value (default 0).

params.name: vz
params.description: The z vector value (default 0).

functions.name: audio_play_sound_on
functions.description: With this function you can play any sound asset through an emitter, with any changes to the emitter gain, position, pitch or velocity affecting how the user hears the final sound being played.

params.name: emitter
params.description: The index of the emitter to use.

params.name: sound
params.description: The index of the sound to use.

params.name: loop
params.description: Flags the sound as looping or not.

params.name: priority
params.description: Set the channel priority for the sound.

params.name: gain
params.description: Sets the gain of the sound played.

params.name: offset
params.description: Sets the start offset (in seconds) of the sound played.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Sets the pitch of the sound played.

params.name: listener_mask
params.description: Sets the listener mask of the sound played.

functions.name: audio_group_is_loaded
functions.description: This function will check a specific audio group to see if it has been loaded into memory, ready for use.

params.name: groupid
params.description: The index of the audio group to check (as defined in the Audio Groups Window)

functions.name: audio_group_load
functions.description: This function will load all the sounds that are flagged as belonging to the given Audio Group into memory.

params.name: groupid
params.description: The index of the audio group to load (as defined in the Audio Groups Window)

functions.name: audio_group_load_progress
functions.description: This function will check the loading progress for an audio group and return an (approximate) value between 0 and 100.

params.name: groupid
params.description: The index of the audio group to check (as defined in the Audio Groups Window)

functions.name: audio_group_name
functions.description: This function will return a string containing the name of the given audio group for displaying or checking.

params.name: groupid
params.description: The index value constant of the audio group to check (as defined in the Audio Groups Window)

functions.name: audio_group_set_gain
functions.description: With this function you can fade a group of sounds in or out over a given length of time, or it can be used to set the group gain instantly. The time is measured in milliseconds, and the function requires that you input a final level of gain for the group to have reached by the end of that time. This gain can be between 0 (silent) and 1 (full volume) and the scale is linear.

params.name: groupid
params.description: The index of the audio group to stop (as defined in the Audio Groups Window)

params.name: volume
params.description: The final value for the group volume.

params.name: time
params.description: The length of the change in gain in milliseconds.

functions.name: audio_group_get_gain
functions.description: This function will return the group gain of a given audio group.

params.name: groupid
params.description: The index of the audio group to check (as defined in the Audio Groups window)

functions.name: audio_group_stop_all
functions.description: This function will stop all sounds from the given audio group that are currently playing.

params.name: groupid
params.description: The index of the audio group to stop (as defined in the Audio Groups Window)

functions.name: audio_group_unload
functions.description: This function will unload all the sounds that are flagged as belonging to the given Audio Group into memory. Note that any audio currently being played when this function is called will be stopped.

params.name: groupid
params.description: The index of the audio group to unload (as defined in the Audio Groups Window)

functions.name: audio_group_get_assets

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_align_content
functions.description: This function sets the alignment of the content of the node. If wrapping is set to `flexpanel_wrap.wrap` or `flexpanel_wrap.reverse`, any items overflowing along the main axis will be laid out across new lines on the cross axis. The "align content" property controls how those wrapped lines are distributed along the cross axis. You can choose from the following values: * `flexpanel_align.flex_start` (default): Align wrapped lines to the start of the container's cross axis. * `flexpanel_align.flex_end`: Align wrapped lines to the end of the container's cross axis. * `flexpanel_align.stretch`: Stretch wrapped lines to match the height of the container's cross axis. * `flexpanel_align.center`: Align wrapped lines in the center of the container's cross axis. * `flexpanel_align.space_between`: Evenly space wrapped lines across the container's cross axis, distributing remaining space between the lines. * `flexpanel_align.space_around`: Similar to `flexpanel_align.space_between` but distributes the space before the first child and after the last child as well. * `flexpanel_align.space_evenly`: Similar to `flexpanel_align.space_around` but the spacing between the edges and the children, and between each child node, is exactly the same.

params.name: node
params.description: The node to be set.

params.name: align
params.description: The selected alignment.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_align_items
functions.description: This function sets the alignment of the items of the node. This controls how the non-absolute children of a flex container are aligned along its cross axis (i.e. the direction perpendicular to the "flex direction"). You can choose from the following values: * `flexpanel_align.stretch` (default): Stretch children to fit the size of the cross axis. * `flexpanel_align.flex_start`: Align children to the start of the cross axis. * `flexpanel_align.flex_end`: Align children to the end of the cross axis. * `flexpanel_align.center`: Align children to the centre of the cross axis. * `flexpanel_align.baseline`: Align children along a common baseline. Individual children can be set to be the reference baseline for their parents.

params.name: node
params.description: The node to be set.

params.name: align
params.description: The selected alignment.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_align_self
functions.description: This function sets the alignment of the selected node. This is the same as "align items". However, instead of being applied to a container, this is applied directly to a child node, and affects its cross-axis alignment within its container. This property overrides the "align items" value set for its parent container.

params.name: node
params.description: The node to be set.

params.name: align
params.description: The selected alignment.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_aspect_ratio
functions.description: This function sets the node's aspect ratio. This is the aspect ratio that the node must maintain and corresponds to the horizontal axis. For example, an aspect ratio of `1` will result in a square node, `2` will be a 2:1 rectangle where its width is twice as much as its height, `0.5` will make the width half the size of the height.

params.name: node
params.description: The node to set.

params.name: value
params.description: The value

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_display
functions.description: This function sets the display setting of the selected node. The display setting controls which layout mode the node follows. You can choose from the following values: * `flexpanel_display.flex` (default): The default layout behaviour. * `flexpanel_display.none`: Disables the node. This effectively functions as the node being removed from the tree, as it's not included in any calculations.

params.name: node
params.description: The node to be set.

params.name: display
params.description: The selected display.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_flex
functions.description: This function sets the flex value of the selected node. Flex is shorthand for the "flex grow" and "flex shrink" properties. It will act as "flex grow" when the value is positive, and "flex shrink" when it's negative.

params.name: node
params.description: The node to be set

params.name: flex
params.description: The flex value for this

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_flex_wrap
functions.description: This function sets the flex wrap of the selected node. Flex wrap controls what happens when children in the container have overflown on the main axis. By default, they will overflow or shrink depending on their properties. You can choose from the following values: * `flexpanel_wrap.no_wrap` (default): Default behaviour, no wrapping * `flexpanel_wrap.wrap`: Child nodes are wrapped on overflow, with each new line being placed on the cross axis * `flexpanel_wrap.wrap_reverse`: Child nodes are wrapped but the order of the lines is reversed

params.name: node
params.description: The node to be set.

params.name: align
params.description: The selected wrap.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_flex_grow
functions.description: This function sets the flex grow of the selected node. Flex grow controls how the node grows within its flex container depending on the remaining space in the container. It's a positive weight value with a default of 1. For example, having a 400px container with a 40px node and then a node with a "flex grow" value of `1` will give the second node any remaining space within the container. Any values other than 1 determine how a node is sized against other growing nodes in the same container, e.g. the node with a larger value will be given more size.

params.name: node
params.description: The node to be set.

params.name: grow
params.description: The selected grow factor

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_flex_shrink
functions.description: This function sets the flex shrink of the selected node. Flex shrink controls how the node shrinks within its flex container when there is overflow. It's a positive weight value with a default of 1. Any values other than 1 determine how a node is shrinked against other growing nodes in the same container.

params.name: node

params.name: shrink
params.description: The selected shrink factor

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_flex_direction
functions.description: This function sets the flex direction of the selected node. Flex direction is the direction in which non-absolute children of the node are laid out. This direction is known as the main axis, and the direction perpendicular to this is known as the cross axis. You can choose from the following values: * `flexpanel_flex_direction.column` (default): Align children from top to bottom. * `flexpanel_flex_direction.row`: Align children from left to right. * `flexpanel_flex_direction.column_reverse`: Align children from bottom to top. * `flexpanel_flex_direction.row_reverse`: Align children from right to left.

params.name: node
params.description: The node to be set.

params.name: direction
params.description: The selected direction.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_gap

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_position
functions.description: This function sets an inset position on the node. Inset position defines the distance between an edge of the node and the same edge of its parent's node, with positive values moving the node toward the centre, and negative values moving it away from the centre. For example, a `left` value of `20` will place the node's left edge 20 pixels to the right of the parent's left edge. A `right` value of `40` will move the node so its right edge is 40 pixels to the left of its parent's, without resizing the node.

params.name: node
params.description: The node to be set.

params.name: edge
params.description: The selected edge.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_justify_content
functions.description: This function sets the node's contents justification. Justification controls how the non-absolute children of a flex container are aligned along its main axis (i.e. the direction of the flex direction). You can choose from the following values: * `flexpanel_justify.start` (default): Align children to the start of the main axis, as set in "flex direction". * `flexpanel_justify.flex_end`: Align children to the end of the main axis, acting as the opposite of "flex direction". * `flexpanel_justify.center`: Align children to the centre of the main axis. * `flexpanel_justify.space_between`: Align children from the start of the container to the end, inserting space between each child to fill the container. * `flexpanel_justify.space_around`: Similar to `flexpanel_justify.space_between` but distributes the space before the first child and after the last child as well. * `flexpanel_justify.space_evenly`: Similar to `flexpanel_justify.space_around` but the spacing between the edges and the children, and between each child node, is exactly the same.

params.name: node
params.description: The node to be set.

params.name: justify

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_position_type
functions.description: This function sets the node's position type. Position type of a node can be any one of the following strings: * `flexpanel_position_type.relative` (default): This node will participate in the flow of its parent container and will take up space in it. Inset positions (`flexpanel_edge.left`, `flexpanel_edge.top`, etc.) will be relative to the node's position within the flow. * `flexpanel_position_type.absolute`: This node is removed from the flow of its parent and will not take up space. Inset positions will be relative to the Containing Block which may not be its direct parent. * `flexpanel_position_type.static`: The node will behave like `flexpanel_position_type.relative` except it will ignore insets and will not form a Containing Block for its children.

params.description: The value to use

params.name: unit
params.description: The units to use for the value

functions.description: This function sets the width of the selected node. Width refers to the width of the "border box" of the node, which is the collective size of the node's content, padding and border.

params.name: node
params.description: The node whose width should be set.

params.name: width
params.description: The selected width.

params.name: unit
params.description: The units to use for the value

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_set_height
functions.description: This function sets the height of the selected node. Height refers to the height of the "border box" of the node, which is the collective size of the node's content, padding and border.

params.name: node
params.description: The node whose height should be set.

params.name: height
params.description: The selected height.

params.name: unit
params.description: The units to use for the value

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_align_content
functions.description: This function gets the alignment of the content of the node. If "flex wrap" is set to `flexpanel_wrap.wrap` or `flexpanel_wrap.reverse`, any items overflowing along the main axis will be laid out across new lines on the cross axis. The "align content" property controls how those wrapped lines are distributed along the cross axis.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_align_items
functions.description: This function gets the alignment of the items of the node. This controls how the non-absolute children of a flex container are aligned along its cross axis (i.e. the direction perpendicular to the flex direction)

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_align_self
functions.description: This function gets the alignment of the selected node. This is the same as "align items". However, instead of being applied to a container, this is applied directly to a child node, and affects its cross-axis alignment within its container. This property overrides the "align items" value set for its parent container.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_aspect_ratio
functions.description: This function gets the node's aspect ratio. This is the aspect ratio that the node must maintain and corresponds to the horizontal axis. For example, an aspect ratio of `1` will result in a square node, `2` will be a 2:1 rectangle where its width is twice as much as its height, `0.5` will make the width half the size of the height.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_display
functions.description: This function gets the display setting of the selected node. The display setting controls which layout mode the node follows. It can be one of the following values: * `flexpanel_display.flex` (default): The default layout behaviour. * `flexpanel_display.none`: Disables the node. This effectively functions as the node being removed from the tree, as it's not included in any calculations.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_flex
functions.description: This function gets the flex value of the selected node. Flex is shorthand for the "flex grow" and "flex shrink" properties. It will act as "flex grow" when the value is positive, and "flex shrink" when it's negative.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_flex_wrap
functions.description: This function gets the flex wrap of the selected node. Flex wrap controls what happens when children in the container have overflown on the main axis. By default, they will overflow or shrink depending on their properties.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_flex_grow
functions.description: This function gets the flex grow of the selected node. Flex grow controls how the node grows within its flex container depending on the remaining space in the container. It's a positive weight value with a default of 1. For example, having a 400px container with a 40px node and then a node with a "flex grow" value of `1` will give the second node any remaining space within the container.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_flex_shrink
functions.description: This function gets the flex shrink of the selected node. Flex shrink controls how the node shrinks within its flex container when there is overflow. It's a positive weight value with a default of 1.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_flex_basis
functions.description: This function gets the flex basis of the selected node. Flex basis is the default size of an item within its flex container before any flex grow or shrink is applied. For a row container this affects the width, and for a column container this affects the height.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_flex_direction
functions.description: This function gets the flex direction of the selected node. Flex direction is the direction in which non-absolute children of the node are laid out. This direction is known as the main axis, and the direction perpendicular to this is known as the cross axis.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_gap
functions.description: This function gets the gap of the selected node on the selected side. Gap is the added distance between each row and column of the flex container and affects distances between child nodes. You can apply to both axes or apply only to rows or columns.

params.name: node
params.description: The node to be set.

params.name: gutter
params.description: The selected gutter (column/row/all).

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_position
functions.description: This function gets the node's style position. Inset position define the distance between an edge of the node and the same edge of its parent's node, with positive values moving the node toward the centre, and negative values moving it away from the centre. For example, a `left` value of `20` will place the node's left edge 20 pixels to the right of the parent's left edge. A `right` value of `40` will move the node so its right edge is 40 pixels to the left of its parent's, without resizing the node.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

params.name: edge
params.description: The selected edge.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_justify_content
functions.description: This function gets the node's contents justification. Justification controls how the non-absolute children of a flex container are aligned along its main axis (i.e. the direction of the "flex direction").

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_direction
functions.description: This function gets the direction of the selected node. This is the layout direction of the node and its children.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_margin
functions.description: This function gets the margin of the selected node. Margin is the space around the outside of the node. You can define it for all edges or for a specific edge.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

params.name: edge
params.description: The selected edge.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_padding
functions.description: This function gets the padding of the selected node. Padding is the spacing between the inner edges of the node and its children. You can define it for all edges or for a specific edge.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

params.name: edge
params.description: The selected edge.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_border
functions.description: This function gets the border of the selected node. Border acts the same as padding.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

params.name: edge
params.description: The selected edge.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_position_type
functions.description: This function gets the node's position type. Position type of a node can be any one of the following strings: * `flexpanel_position_type.relative` (default): This node will participate in the flow of its parent container and will take up space in it. Inset positions (`flexpanel_edge.left`, `flexpanel_edge.top`, etc.) will be relative to the node's position within the flow. * `flexpanel_position_type.absolute`: This node is removed from the flow of its parent and will not take up space. Inset positions will be relative to the Containing Block which may not be its direct parent. * `flexpanel_position_type.static`: The node will behave like `flexpanel_position_type.relative` except it will ignore insets and will not form a Containing Block for its children.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_min_width
functions.description: This function gets the minimum width the node must maintain.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_max_width
functions.description: This function gets the maximum width the node must maintain.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_min_height
functions.description: This function gets the minimum height the node must maintain.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_max_height
functions.description: This function gets the maximum height the node must maintain.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_width
functions.description: This function gets the width of the selected node. Width refers to the width of the "border box" of the node, which is the collective size of the node's content, padding and border.

params.name: node
