functions.name: flexpanel_node_style_get_height
functions.description: This function gets the height of the selected node. Height refers to the height of the "border box" of the node, which is the collective size of the node's content, padding and border.

params.name: node
params.description: The node.

functions.name: font_add
functions.description: This function can be used to add a font to your game from a font file present in the Included Files. -1 is returned if the function fails for any reason.

params.name: name
params.description: The path of the font file in the Included Files (*.ttf or *.otf).

params.name: size
params.description: The size of the font - points for Web Fonts, pixels for file fonts.

params.name: bold
params.description: Whether the font is bold (true) or not (false).

params.name: italic
params.description: Whether the font is italic (true) or not (false).

params.name: first
params.description: The first character to include (if you're unsure, go for 32).

params.name: last
params.description: The last character to include (if you're unsure, go for 128).

functions.signature: font_add(name, size, bold, italic, first, last)

functions.name: font_add_enable_aa
functions.description: This function can be used to enable or disable anti-aliasing (AA) for fonts added using font_add(). This function needs to be called before you add any fonts.

params.name: enable
params.description: Whether to enable (true) or disable (false) AA for added fonts.

functions.name: font_add_get_enable_aa
functions.description: This function can be used to check whether anti-aliasing (AA) is enabled for fonts added using font_add(). Note that AA is enabled by default, but you can change the AA state for added fonts using the function font_add_enable_aa(), as long as it is called before adding the font.

functions.name: font_add_sprite
functions.description: With this function you can use a "sprite strip" to create a new font asset, where each sub-image would be an individual symbol or letter.

params.name: spr
params.description: The sprite to add a font based on.

params.name: first
params.description: The index of the first available character.

params.name: prop
params.description: Set as proportional font or not.

params.name: sep
params.description: The space to leave between each letter.

functions.name: font_add_sprite_ext
functions.description: With this function you can use a "sprite strip" to create a new font asset, where each sub-image would be an individual symbol or letter.

params.name: spr
params.description: The sprite to add a font based on.

params.name: string_map
params.description: String from which sprite sub-image order is taken.

params.name: prop
params.description: Set as proportional font or not.

params.name: sep
params.description: The space to leave between each letter.

functions.name: font_delete
functions.description: With this function you can delete a font asset from the game.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the font to delete.

functions.name: font_enable_sdf
functions.description: With this function you can enable or disable SDF rendering for the specified font. This only works on fonts added using font_add().

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the font.

params.name: enable
params.description: Whether to enable (true) or disable (false) SDF rendering for the specified font.

functions.name: font_get_sdf_enabled
functions.description: With this function you can determine whether SDF rendering is enabled or disabled for the specified font

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the font.

functions.name: font_sdf_spread
functions.description: With this function you can set the SDF spread value for the specified font. This only works on fonts added using font_add(), and its effect is only visible if the font is using SDF rendering.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the font.

params.name: spread
params.description: The SDF spread value to set for the specified font.

functions.name: font_get_sdf_spread
functions.description: With this function you can query the SDF spread value for the specified font

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the font.

functions.name: font_enable_effects
functions.description: With this function you can enable or disable built-in effects rendering for the specified font. Built-in effects will only have an effect with SDF-enabled fonts.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the font.

params.name: enable
params.description: Whether to enable (true) or disable (false) effects rendering for the specified font.

params.name: params
params.description: A struct containing any initial values for the font's effect parameters.

functions.name: font_exists
functions.description: This function returns whether a font with the specified index exists or not. You can check font indices as defined from the Asset Browser, or fonts that have been added using functions like font_add().

params.name: ind
params.description: Index of the font to check.

functions.name: font_get_bold
functions.description: With this function you can check any font asset to see if it has the bold flag or not.

params.name: ind
params.description: Index of the font to check.

functions.name: font_get_fontname
functions.description: With this function you can get the actual system name of the selected font asset. This function returns a string and not an index, and the name returned will depend on the font being used.

params.name: ind
params.description: Index of the font to check.

functions.name: font_get_info
functions.description: This function is used to retrieve information for the given font.

params.name: font
params.description: The font for which information should be retrieved.

functions.name: font_get_italic
functions.description: With this function you can check any font asset to see if it has the italic flag or not.

params.name: ind
params.description: Index of the font to check.

functions.name: font_get_last
functions.description: This function can be used to find the last character (as an UTF-8 value) that was used when your font asset was added to your game.

params.name: ind
params.description: Index of the font to check.

functions.name: font_get_name
functions.description: This function can be used to get the name (as a string) that was given to the font when it was added as an asset to the GameMaker Asset Browser.

params.name: ind
params.description: Index of the font to check.

functions.name: font_get_size
functions.description: With this function you can get the size of any font asset, which is the point value shown by the font asset dialogue.

params.name: ind
params.description: Index of the font to get the size of.

functions.name: font_get_texture
functions.description: This function returns a special pointer for the font texture page.

params.name: font
params.description: The index of the font to use.

functions.name: font_get_uvs
functions.description: This function returns an array with the UV coordinates for the font texture on the texture page, filling in the array with the following values: [0] = left [1] = top [2] = right [3] = bottom

params.name: font
params.description: The index of the font to use.

functions.name: font_replace_sprite
functions.description: With this function you can use a "sprite strip" to replace a previously created sprite font asset, where each sub-image would be an individual symbol or letter.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the font that shall be replaced (i.e. all references to this asset past this function will refer to the new font, not the original).

params.name: spr
params.description: The sprite to add a font based on.

params.name: first
params.description: The index of the first available character.

params.name: prop
params.description: Whether white space around each letter should be removed (if false, the created font will be monospaced, otherwise it'll be like most regular fonts).

params.name: sep
params.description: The space between each letter, 0 meaning the right of one letter just touches the left of the next one.

functions.name: font_replace_sprite_ext
functions.description: This function will replace a sprite font that you created previously using the function font_add_sprite_ext(). It uses a "sprite strip", where each sub-image is an individual symbol or letter, and the images are mapped to letters based on the argument "string_map" of the function.

params.name: font
params.description: The font to replace.

params.name: spr
params.description: The sprite to add a font based on.

params.name: string_map
params.description: String from which sprite sub-image order is taken.

params.name: prop
params.description: Set as proportional font or not.

params.name: sep
params.description: The space to leave between each letter.

functions.name: font_set_cache_size
functions.description: This function sets how many blended copies of the given font can be cached before old ones are overwritten.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the font to change the cache size of.

params.name: max
params.description: The maximum number of cached copies of the font that can be stored.

functions.name: alarm_get
functions.description: This function can be used to get the current value of the given alarm. This is an alternative method to getting the alarm array value directly.

params.name: index
params.description: The alarm index to get, from 0 to 11.

functions.name: alarm_set
functions.description: This function can be used to set an alarm. This is an alternative method to setting the alarm array directly.

params.name: index
params.description: The alarm index to set, from 0 to 11.

params.name: value
params.description: The value (an integer) to set the alarm to.

functions.name: instance_change
functions.description: You can use this function to change one instance of an object into another instance of a different object, and while doing so decide whether to perform the initial instance's Destroy and Clean Up Events and the new instance's Create Event.

params.name: obj
params.description: The new object the calling object will change into.

params.name: perf
params.description: Whether to perform that new object's create and destroy events (true) or not (false).

functions.name: instance_copy
functions.description: With this function you can "clone" an instance as this will create a new version of the instance running the code at its same position.

params.name: perf
params.description: Whether to perform the new instance's Create event (true) or not (false).

functions.name: instance_create_depth
functions.description: With this function you can create a new instance of the specified object at any given point within the room and at the depth specified.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position the object will be created at

params.name: y
params.description: The y position the object will be created at

params.name: depth
params.description: The depth to assign the created instance to

params.name: obj
params.description: The object index of the object to create an instance of

params.name: var_struct
params.description: A structure that contains variables that are copied into the new instance before the Create Event is called

functions.name: instance_create_layer
functions.description: With this function you can create a new instance of the specified object at any given point within the room and on the layer specified. The layer can be identified using the layer ID value (as returned by the function layer_create()) or by the name of the layer (as a string, for example "instance_layer") as defined in the Room Editor.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position the object will be created at

params.name: y
params.description: The y position the object will be created at

params.name: layer_id
params.description: The layer ID (or name) to assign the created instance to

params.name: obj
params.description: The object index of the object to create an instance of

params.name: var_struct
params.description: A structure that contains variables that are copied into the new instance before the Create Event is called

functions.name: instance_destroy
functions.description: You call this function whenever you wish to destroy an instance, normally triggering a Destroy Event and also a Clean Up Event.

params.name: id
params.description: The instance ID or object_index to destroy (optional, default is the calling instance)

params.name: execute_event_flag
params.description: Set to true or false to perform the destroy event or not (optional, default is true)

functions.name: instance_exists
functions.description: This function checks if any instance of the given Object handle exists in the room, or whether the given specific Instance handle exists in the room.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object or instance to check for the existence of.

functions.name: instance_find
functions.description: All instances have a unique identifier (id) which can be used to modify and manipulate them while a game is running, but you may not always know what the id for a specific instance is and so this function can help as you can use it to iterate through all of them to find what you need.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object to find the nth instance of

params.name: n
params.description: The number of the instance to find.

functions.name: instance_furthest
functions.description: This function will check all the instances of the given object to see which is furthest from the given x/y point.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position to check.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position to check.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object to check for instances of.

functions.name: instance_id_get
functions.description: With this function you can get the unique ID value of any instance from the currently active instance list.

params.name: index
params.description: The index within the instance list from 0 - (instance count - 1).

functions.name: instance_nearest
functions.description: This function will check all the instances of the given object to see which is nearest to the given x/y point.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position to check.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position to check.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object to check for instances of.

functions.name: instance_number
functions.description: With this function you can find out how many active instances of the specified object exists in the room.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object to total the number of instances of.

functions.name: instance_place
functions.description: With this function you can check a position for a collision with another instance or all instances of an object using the collision mask of the instance that runs the code for the check.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position to check for instances.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position to check for instances.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object to check for instances of.

functions.name: instance_place_list
functions.description: With this function you can check a position for a collision with all instances of an object using the collision mask of the instance that runs the code for the check.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position to check for instances.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position to check for instances.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object to check for instances of.

params.name: list
params.description: The DS list to use to store the IDs of colliding instances.

params.name: ordered
params.description: Whether the list should be ordered by distance (true) or not (false).

functions.name: instance_position
functions.description: With this function you can check a position for a collision with another instance or all instances of an object.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position to check for instances.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position to check for instances.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object to check for instances of.

functions.name: instance_position_list
functions.description: With this function you can check a position for a collision with all instances of another object.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position to check for instances.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position to check for instances.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object to check for instances of.

params.name: list
params.description: The DS list to use to store the IDs of colliding instances.

params.name: ordered
params.description: Whether the list should be ordered by distance (true) or not (false).

functions.name: instance_activate_all
functions.description: With this function you can tell GameMaker to activate all instances that have been previously deactivated in a room. Note that activation is not instantaneous, and an instance that has been activated in this way will not be considered to be active until the end of the event in which the function was called.

params.name: collision_space
params.description: The collision space in which to consider instances, defaults to the collision space the calling instance is in.

functions.name: instance_activate_layer
functions.description: With this function you can activate a layer that has been deactivated previously. Note that activation is not instantaneous, and an instance that has been activated in this way will not be considered to be active until the end of the event in which the function was called.

params.name: layer_id
params.description: The layer ID string (or value) to be used

functions.name: instance_activate_object
functions.description: With this function you can activate a single instance or all instances of a specific object from all those that have been deactivated previously. Note that if you have deactivated an instance or object that has been flagged as Persistent, then you will need to reactivate it again with this function before changing room, otherwise it will not be carried over and will be discarded instead. Note too that activation is not instantaneous, and an instance that has been activated in this way will not be considered to be active until the end of the event in which the function was called.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object or instance to activate (the keyword all can also be used).

params.name: collision_space
params.description: The collision space in which to consider instances, defaults to the collision space the calling instance is in.

functions.name: instance_activate_region
functions.description: With this function you can define a region within the room to activate instances that have previously been deactivated. The region can either be flagged as "inside" or "outside".

params.name: left
params.description: The x coordinate of the left of the rectangular region to activate.

params.name: top
params.description: The y coordinate of the top of the rectangular region to activate.

params.name: width
params.description: The width of the region to activate.

params.name: height
params.description: The height of the region to activate.

params.name: inside
params.description: Whether to activate instances on the inside of the region (true) or the outside (false).

params.name: collision_space
params.description: The collision space in which to consider instances, defaults to the collision space the calling instance is in.

functions.name: instance_deactivate_all
functions.description: This function will deactivate all instances that are in the room at the moment that the code is run. Note that deactivation is not instantaneous, and an instance that has been deactivated in this way will not be considered to be inactive until the end of the event in which the function was called.

params.name: notme
params.description: Whether to keep the calling instance activated (true) or not (false).

params.name: collision_space
params.description: The collision space in which to consider instances, defaults to the collision space the calling instance is in.

functions.name: instance_deactivate_layer
functions.description: With this function you can deactivate all instances assigned to a specific layer. Note that deactivation is not instantaneous, and an instance that has been deactivated in this way will not be considered to be inactive until the end of the event in which the function was called.

params.name: layer
params.description: The layer ID string (or value) to be used

functions.name: instance_deactivate_object
functions.description: With this function you can deactivate a single instance or all instances of a specific object from all those that have been activated previously. Note that deactivation is not instantaneous, and an instance that has been deactivated in this way will not be considered to be inactive until the end of the event in which the function was called.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object or instance to deactivate (the keyword all can also be used).

params.name: collision_space
params.description: The collision space in which to consider instances, defaults to the collision space the calling instance is in.

functions.name: instance_deactivate_region
functions.description: With this function you can define a region within the room to deactivate instances that have previously been activated. The region can either be flagged as "inside" or "outside".

params.name: left
params.description: The x coordinate of the left of the rectangular region to deactivate.

params.name: top
params.description: The y coordinate of the top of the rectangular region to deactivate.

params.name: width
params.description: The width of the region to deactivate.

params.name: height
params.description: The height of the region to deactivate.

params.name: inside
params.description: Whether to deactivate instances on the inside of the region (true) or the outside (false).

params.name: notme
params.description: Whether to exclude the calling instance from deactivation (true) or not (false).

params.name: collision_space
params.description: The collision space in which to consider instances, defaults to the collision space the calling instance is in.

functions.signature: instance_deactivate_region(left, top, width, height, inside, notme, [collision_space])

functions.name: object_exists
functions.description: This function returns whether an object with the specified index exists or not.

params.name: obj
params.description: The index of the object to check.

functions.name: object_get_mask
functions.description: This function will tell you whether the object you are checking has a mask index or not, and if it does then it will return the index of that mask, or -1 if it does not.

params.name: obj
params.description: The index of the object to check

functions.name: object_get_name
functions.description: This function will return the name as a string of the specified object.

params.name: obj
params.description: The index of the object to check.

functions.name: object_get_parent
functions.description: This function will get you the object_index of any parent that has been assigned to the specified object, or else return -100 to show that the object has no parent assigned to it, or -1 if the object being checked does not exist.

params.name: obj
params.description: The index of the object to check

functions.name: object_get_persistent
functions.description: This function will tell you whether the object you are checking has been flagged as "persistent" or not. A persistent object is one that will cause any instances of it to be carried through from room to room unless they are explicitly destroyed.

params.name: obj
params.description: The index of the object to check.

functions.name: object_get_physics
functions.description: This function will tell you whether the object you are checking has been flagged as "physics-enabled".

params.name: obj
params.description: The index of the object to check.

functions.name: object_get_solid
functions.description: This function will tell you whether the object you are checking has been flagged as "solid" or not. A solid object generates a special collision event when using the traditional collision system (i.e.: the physics world is off).

params.name: obj
params.description: The index of the object to check.

functions.name: object_get_sprite
functions.description: This function will tell you whether the object you are checking has a sprite or not, and if it does then it will return the index of that sprite, or -1 if it does not.

params.name: obj
params.description: The index of the object to check

functions.name: object_get_visible
functions.description: This function will tell you whether the object you are checking has been flagged as "visible" (runs its draw event) or not (does not run its draw event).

params.name: obj
params.description: The index of the object to check.

functions.name: object_is_ancestor
functions.description: This function can be used to check an object and see if it is an ancestor or not of another object.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object that is being checked as the child.

params.name: par
params.description: The object that is being checked as the ancestor (parent).

functions.name: object_set_mask
functions.description: With this function you can set the mask_index of a specific object. You can set this to -1 to remove a mask sprite and so default to the mask defined for the sprite of the object (or no masks if no sprite has been chosen).

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the object to change.

params.name: spr
params.description: The new sprite to use as the object's mask.

functions.name: object_set_persistent
functions.description: With this function you can set the persistence of a specific object. A persistent object is "carried over" from room to room and maintains its properties at all times.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the object to change.

params.name: pers
params.description: Whether the object should be flagged as persistent (true) or not (false).

functions.name: object_set_solid
functions.description: With this function you can flag a specific object as being solid or not. This means that all instances of this object that are created after solid has been changed will be created with this new state, while instances that are already in the room may not be affected.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the object to change.

params.name: solid
params.description: The new solidity of the object (true=solid, false=not solid).

functions.name: object_set_sprite
functions.description: With this function you can set the sprite index of a specific object. This means that all instances of this object that are created after the sprite_index has been changed will be created with this new sprite_index, while instances that are already in the room may not be affected.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the object to change.

params.name: spr
params.description: The sprite to assign to the object.

functions.name: object_set_visible
functions.description: With this function you can flag a specific object as being visible or not. This means that all instances of this object that are created after visible has been changed will be created with this new state, while instances that are already in the room may not be affected.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the object to change.

params.name: vis
params.description: The new visibility of the object (true=visible, false=invisible).

functions.name: event_inherited
functions.description: This function will call the current event of the parent object of the instance.

functions.name: event_perform
functions.description: This function will perform the specified event, with the designated argument, for the instance running the code.

params.name: type
params.description: The type of event to perform.

params.name: numb
params.description: The specific event constant or value, if one is necessary (otherwise, just use 0).

functions.name: event_perform_async
functions.description: This function is used to perform any one of the Asynchronous Events provided in GameMaker.

params.name: type
params.description: The type of event to perform.

params.name: ds_map
params.description: The DS map to use as async_load in the called event.

functions.name: event_perform_object
functions.description: This function works the same as event_perform() except that this time you can specify events from another object.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object that should have its event triggered.

params.name: type
params.description: The type of event to perform.

params.name: numb
params.description: The specific event, if one is necessary (otherwise, just use 0).

functions.name: event_user
functions.description: With this function you tell the instance to run the actions or code that has been placed within one of the 16 user-defined events. These events can only be called in this way, or using the event_perform function.

params.name: numb
params.description: The number of event to call, between 0 and 15.

functions.name: path_end
functions.description: This function ends the current path that the instance is following, as set when the function path_start was called.

functions.name: path_get_closed
functions.description: This function can be used to return whether the path is flagged as closed (true) or open (false), i.e. whether the path loops or if it has a definitive beginning and end.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to check.

functions.name: path_get_kind
functions.description: This function can be used to find out whether the given path is smooth (true) or not (false).

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to check.

functions.name: path_get_length
functions.description: You can use this function to get the exact length of a path in pixels. this is not an approximate length from point to point, but rather an exact length along the shape of the path, even when the path is smooth with a high curved precision.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to measure.

functions.name: path_get_name
functions.description: This function will return the name of the path that is referenced as a string.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to check.

functions.name: path_get_number
functions.description: This function can be used to return the number of points on a path.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to check.

functions.name: path_get_point_speed
functions.description: With this function you can get the speed of the point (as defined in the Path Editor or when you dynamically add a path point using path_add_point()) expressed as a percentage.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to check.

params.name: n
params.description: The point identity to check.

functions.name: path_get_point_x
functions.description: This function will return the x position (in room coordinates) of the point that you input for the path that you index. If the point is outside of the range of the path (i.e.: a path has 8 points and you ask for the x position of point 10) then a value of 0 will be returned.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to check.

params.name: n
params.description: The point identity to check.

functions.name: path_get_point_y
functions.description: This function will return the y position (in room coordinates) of the point that you input for the path that you index. If the point is outside of the range of the path (i.e.: a path has 8 points and you ask for the y position of point 10) then a value of 0 will be returned.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to check.

params.name: n
params.description: The point identity to check.

functions.name: path_get_precision
functions.description: This function returns precision with which the given path has been "smoothed", and will be an integer value from 1 to 8. Although you can get (and set) this value for a straight-line path it will have no influence over how an instance uses the path as it is only relevant when the path kind is set to "smooth".

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to check.

functions.name: path_get_speed
functions.description: This function returns the speed factor of any given position on a path. The position should be a value between 0 and 1 (you can use path_position if you need the current position of the instance).

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to check.

params.name: pos
params.description: How far through the path to check. Between 0 (start) and 1 (end), can be decimal.

functions.name: path_get_x
functions.description: With this function you can get the x coordinate of a position on any given path.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to check.

params.name: pos
params.description: How far through the path to check. Between 0 (start) and 1 (end).

functions.name: path_get_y
functions.description: With this function you can get the y coordinate of a position on any given path.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to check.

params.name: pos
params.description: How far through the path to check. Between 0 (start) and 1 (end).

functions.name: path_start
functions.description: This function tells the calling instance to start the given path. The path started by the instance is stored in the variable path_index.

params.name: path
params.description: The path index to start.

params.name: speed
params.description: The speed of which to follow the path in pixels per step, negative meaning going backwards.

params.name: endaction
params.description: What to do when the end of the path is reached.

params.name: absolute
params.description: Whether the calling instance should follow the absolute path as it is in the editor (true) or a relative path to its current position (false).

functions.name: path_add
functions.description: With this function you can create a path in GameMaker without using the path editor.

functions.name: path_add_point
functions.description: With this function you can add a point to the specified path and set its speed factor.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to add the point to.

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate of the new point.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate of the new point.

params.name: speed
params.description: The speed factor of the point (default value is 100).

functions.name: path_append
functions.description: With this function you can append one path onto another one, effectively joining them together.

params.name: index
params.description: The new index of the path.

params.name: path
params.description: The index of the path that will be appended to "index".

functions.name: path_assign
functions.description: With this function you can copy the path data from one path to another. The path being copied to will be cleared first (should it have any path points) and be completely overwritten by the path being copied from.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to be overwritten.

params.name: path
params.description: The index of the path that will overwrite "index".

functions.name: path_change_point
functions.description: With this function you can change the position and/or the speed factor of any point previously defined for a path).

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to change a point of.

params.name: n
params.description: The defining point to change the attributes of.

params.name: x
params.description: The new x coordinate (relative to the path) of the point.

params.name: y
params.description: The new y coordinate (relative to the path) of the point.

params.name: speed
params.description: The new speed factor of the point.

functions.name: path_clear_points
functions.description: With this function you can remove all point definitions from a path, effectively making an "empty" path.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to clear.

functions.name: path_delete
functions.description: You can use this code to remove a path from memory.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to delete.

functions.name: path_delete_point
functions.description: With this function you can remove a point from the specified path.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to delete a point from.

params.name: n
params.description: The defining point to delete.

functions.name: path_duplicate
functions.description: This function takes a path and copies it into a new path.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the existing path to duplicate.

functions.name: path_exists
functions.description: This function returns whether a path with the given index exists or not.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to check for.

functions.name: path_flip
functions.description: This function takes all the path points and flips them along the horizontal axis, changing the actual path asset.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to flip.

functions.name: path_insert_point
functions.description: With this function you can insert a new point into a path. The point will be added into the path before the point "n" that is specified in the function.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to insert the point into.

params.name: n
params.description: The defining point to insert the new point BEFORE.

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate (relative to the path) of the new point.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate (relative to the path) of the new point.

params.name: speed
params.description: The speed factor of the point.

functions.name: path_mirror
functions.description: This function takes all the path points and mirrors them along the vertical axis, changing the actual path asset.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to mirror.

functions.name: path_rescale
functions.description: This function can be used to re-scale the given path along both (or either) the vertical and horizontal axis, basically moving each of the path points to a new position corresponding to this scale around the centre of the path.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to scale.

params.name: xscale
params.description: What to multiply the current horizontal scale by. Default scale is 1.

params.name: yscale
params.description: What to multiply the current vertical scale by. Default scale is 1.

functions.name: path_reverse
functions.description: With this function you can reverse the order in which the individual path points are numbered, so, for example, if the path has 5 points, point 0 would become point 4, point 1 would be point 3 and point 2 would not be changed. The actual position of the points remains the same, only the order in which they are processed is changed.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to change.

functions.name: path_rotate
functions.description: You can use this function to rotate a given path around its center.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to flip.

params.name: angle
params.description: The angle of rotation degrees.

functions.name: path_set_closed
functions.description: This function can be used to flag a given path as being open (false) or closed (true). A closed path has its start point connected to its end point, forming a loop, and an open path has a definitive, unconnected start and finish.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to change.

params.name: closed
params.description: Whether the path is closed (true) or not (false).

functions.name: path_set_kind
functions.description: This function can be used to set the kind of path that you wish the specified asset to be. This can be either a straight line path (set to 0) or a smoothed path (set to 1) which takes into account the path precision.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to change.

params.name: val
params.description: The kind of the path, 0 for straight or 1 for smooth.

functions.name: path_set_precision
functions.description: With this function you can change the "smoothness" of a path. This value must be between 1 and 8, with a low value creating straighter edges with sharper curves between points, while a higher value will round the points and make the path a lot more "curvy".

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to change.

params.name: prec
params.description: The precision of the path. Must be an integer between 1 and 8.

functions.name: path_shift
functions.description: With this function you can shift a path along the horizontal and vertical axis.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the path to change.

params.name: xshift
params.description: The number of horizontal pixels to shift the path. Negative=left, positive=right.

params.name: yshift
params.description: The number of vertical pixels to shift the path. Negative=up, positive=down.

functions.name: room_add
functions.description: This function will create a new, empty, room and add it to your game, returning its index to be stored in a variable for all further codes that deal with this room. Note that each room is permanently added to the game until the executable is closed, i.e.: rooms added through code cannot be deleted again.

functions.name: room_assign
functions.description: This function copies one room to another, removing all instances, tiles, etc., from the room that is being copied to and replaces them completely with the new room's contents.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the room to be copied to.

params.name: source
params.description: The index of the room to be copied from.

functions.name: room_duplicate
functions.description: This will duplicate a given room and return the duplicate's index to be used in all further calls to reference the new room.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the original room to be duplicated.

functions.name: room_exists
functions.description: With this function you can check and see whether the room you specify exists or not.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the room to check.

functions.name: room_get_camera
functions.description: With this function you can get the unique index ID of the camera assigned to a specific view in a room other than the current one.

params.name: rm
params.description: The index of the room to get the view camera of

params.name: vind
params.description: The index of the viewport to get the camera of

functions.name: room_get_name
functions.description: This function can be used to return the name of the specified room as a string.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the room to check the name of.

functions.name: room_get_info
functions.description: This function can be used to get all the information on a room. It returns a struct that contains data that has been requested, a room can be very large so this can take a long time to complete, and optionally some data can be omitted to speed it up. NOTE: Tilemap data is an array of all the tilemap indices stored as a one dimensional array of width * height, where an x, y entry is indexed as (y*width)+x

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the room.

params.name: views
params.description: Add room view information to the struct (defaults to true)

params.name: instances
params.description: Add instance information to the struct (defaults to true)

params.name: layers
params.description: Add room layer information to the struct (defaults to true)

params.name: layer_elements
params.description: Add layer element information to the struct (defaults to true), NOTE: you must have layers enabled to get any layer_elements

params.name: tilemap_data
params.description: Add tilemap data information to the struct (defaults to true), NOTE: you must have layers and layer_elements enabled to get any tilemap_data (if present)

params.name: live
params.description: if you request the current room then if this is true (default is false) it will report the live data for the current room, otherwise it is the data from the WAD

functions.name: room_get_viewport
functions.description: With this function you can retrieve the details of a viewport in a room other than the current one.

params.name: rm
params.description: The index of the room to get viewport data from

params.name: vind
params.description: The index of the viewport to get

functions.name: room_goto
functions.description: This function permits you to go to any room in your game project, whether created using code or in the Asset Browser. This function will also trigger the Room End event.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the room to go to.

functions.name: room_goto_next
functions.description: With this function you can make your game go to the next room as listed in the Room Manager at the time the game was compiled. If this room does not exist, an error will be thrown and the game will be forced to close.

functions.name: room_goto_previous
functions.description: With this function you can make your game go to the previous room as listed in the Room Manager at the time the game was compiled. If this room does not exist, an error will be thrown and the game will be forced to close. This function will also trigger the Room End event.

functions.name: room_instance_add
functions.description: With this function you can add an instance to any room other than the current one and at any position within that room.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the room to add an object instance to.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position of the new instance.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position of the new instance.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object to add an instance of.

functions.name: room_instance_clear
functions.description: This function will clear a room of all instances (no destroy events shall be called for the instances that are being removed). Note that calling this function on a room asset created in the Asset Browser will permanently clear the room of instances, and even calling game_restart() will not return the room to its original state (only ending the game and opening it again will start with the room in its original state again).

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the room to clear all instances in.

functions.name: room_next
functions.description: With this function you can retrieve the index of the room after the room input into the function.

params.name: numb
params.description: The index of the room to get the next one after.

functions.name: room_previous
functions.description: With this function you can retrieve the index of the room before the room input into the function.

params.name: numb
params.description: The index of the room to get the one before from.

functions.name: room_restart
functions.description: This function will restart the current room, as if it had just been entered. Note that the room will not restart until the end of the event where the function was called, so any code after this has been called will still run if in the same event. This function will also trigger the Room End event.

functions.name: room_set_camera
functions.description: With this function you can assign a camera to a specific viewport in a room other than the current one.

params.name: rm
params.description: The index of the room to set the view camera of

params.name: vind
params.description: The index of the viewport to assign the camera to

params.name: camera
params.description: The index of the camera to assign

functions.name: room_set_height
functions.description: With this function you can change (or set) the height of any room in your game except the current one.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the room to set the height of.

params.name: h
params.description: The new height of the room in pixels.

functions.name: room_set_persistent
functions.description: With this function you can change (or set) the persistence of any room in your game except the current one. A persistent room will maintain the state of all instances within that room if the player leaves and then returns, a non-persistent room will be reset to the initial state every time.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the room to set the persistence of.

params.name: val
params.description: Whether the room shall be persistent (true) or not (false).

functions.name: room_set_viewport
functions.description: With this function you can set the viewport properties for any room in your game except the current one.

params.name: rm
params.description: The index of the room to set

params.name: vind
params.description: The index of the viewport to set

params.name: vis
params.description: The visibility of the viewport (true is visible, false is invisible)

params.name: xport
params.description: The x position for the viewport in the room

params.name: yport
params.description: The y position of the viewport in the room

params.name: wport
params.description: The width (in pixels) of the viewport

params.name: hport
params.description: The height (in pixels) of the viewport

functions.signature: room_set_viewport(rm, vind, vis, xport, yport, wport, hport)

functions.name: room_set_view_enabled
functions.description: With this function you can enable (true) or disable (false) the view of any room within your game except the current one.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the room to set.

params.name: val
params.description: Whether to enable (true) or disable (false) views in the given room.

functions.name: room_set_width
functions.description: With this function you can change (or set) the width of any room in your game except the current one.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the room to set the width of.

params.name: w
params.description: The new width of the room in pixels.

functions.name: layer_background_alpha
functions.description: This function controls the alpha (transparency) of the background sprite.

params.name: background_element_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the background element to change

params.name: alpha
params.description: The alpha for background sprite, from 0 to 1 (default is 1)

functions.name: layer_background_blend
functions.description: This function controls the blending (or "tinting") of the background sprite and the default value is -1 (which represents the constant c_white, which can also be used). Any other value (including internal colour constants like c_red, or c_aqua) will blend the specified colour with the original sprite.

params.name: background_element_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the background element to change

params.name: blend
params.description: The colour to blend with the background sprite (default is c_white)

functions.name: layer_background_create
functions.description: With this function you can assign a sprite asset to a layer to be used as a background in your project.

params.name: layer_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the layer to target (or the layer name as a string)

params.name: sprite
params.description: The sprite index to be used

functions.name: layer_background_destroy
functions.description: This function will destroy the given background element.

params.name: background_element_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the background to be destroyed

functions.name: layer_background_exists
functions.description: You can use this function to check and see if a background element exists on any given layer.

params.name: layer_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the layer to target (or the layer name as a string)

params.name: background_element_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the background element to check

functions.name: layer_background_get_alpha
functions.description: This function can be used to get the alpha value of the background element.

params.name: background_element_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the background element to get the information from

functions.name: layer_background_get_blend
functions.description: This function can be used to get the blend colour of the background element.

params.name: background_element_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the background element to get the information from

functions.name: layer_background_get_htiled
functions.description: This function can be used to find out if the background element is tiled horizontally or not.

params.name: background_element_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the background element to get the information from

functions.name: layer_background_get_id
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the unique ID value of the background element on a layer.

params.name: layer_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the layer to target

functions.name: layer_background_get_index
functions.description: This function can be used to get the current image index value of the background element.

params.name: background_element_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the background element to get the information from

functions.name: layer_background_get_speed
functions.description: This function can be used to get the current speed multiplier value of the background element. Default value is 1.

params.name: background_element_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the background element to get the information from

functions.name: layer_background_get_sprite
functions.description: This function can be used to get the current sprite index value of the background element. If the element has no sprite assigned, the function will return -1.

params.name: background_element_id

functions.name: layer_tilemap_create
functions.description: With this function you can assign a tile-set asset to a layer to be used as a tile map in your project. It is worth noting that you cannot place tiles at negative positions within the tile map, so all tiles must be placed within the cell spaces 0 to width - 1, 0 to height - 1.

params.name: layer_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the layer to target (or the layer name as a string)

params.name: x
params.description: The x position of the tile map in the room

params.name: y
params.description: The y position of the tile map in the room

params.name: tileset
params.description: The tile set index to be used

params.name: width
params.description: The width tile map (in cells)

params.name: height
params.description: The height of the tile map (in cells)

functions.signature: layer_tilemap_create(layer_id, x, y, tileset, width, height)

functions.name: layer_tilemap_destroy
functions.description: This function will destroy the given tile map element. Note that this does not remove the layer, only the tile map from it, and if the tile map is one that has been added in the room editor, then the next time you leave the room and then return, the tile map will be recreated again. However if the room is persistent, the tile map will be removed unless room persistence is switched off again.

params.name: tilemap_element_id
params.description: The unique ID value of the tile map to be destroyed

functions.name: layer_tilemap_exists
functions.description: You can use this function to check and see if a tile map element exists on any given layer.
