functions.name: skeleton_collision_draw_set
functions.description: With this function, you can toggle on (true) or off (false) drawing the collision data for the current skeletal animation sprite being used by the instance. If this is switched on, the bounding box and the precise collision mask will be drawn as outlines around the sprite.

params.name: flag
params.description: Set to true to turn on drawing, and false to turn it off.

functions.name: skeleton_get_bounds
functions.description: This function will return an array of values associated with any given bounding box for the currently assigned skeleton animation sprite.

params.name: index
params.description: The bounding box index to get the values of.

functions.name: skeleton_get_minmax
functions.description: This function will return an array with the total bounding box value for all the individual bounding boxes assigned to a skeleton animation sprite. The returned array will have 4 elements: [0] - the minimum x position for all bounding boxes [1] - the minimum y position for all bounding boxes [2] - the maximum x position for all bounding boxes [3] - the maximum y position for all bounding boxes

functions.name: skeleton_get_num_bounds
functions.description: This function will return the number of bounding boxes associated with the skeleton animation sprite assigned to the instance running the code. This can then be used along with the function skeleton_get_bounds() to retrieve data about each of the bounding boxes.

functions.name: skeleton_skin_create
functions.description: Creates a new skin by combining one or more skins defined in the sprite. This can be used (for example) to combine multiple skins defining different pieces of clothing or accessories on a character sprite.

params.name: skin_name
params.description: The name of the skin to create.

params.name: base_skins
params.description: Array of skin names defined in the sprite to combine.

functions.name: skeleton_skin_get
functions.description: With skeletal animation sprites, you can assign separate textures (called "skins") to the animation, thereby using one animation for multiple different things. This function will return the name of the skin (as a string) that is currently assigned to the skeletal animation sprite your instance is using.

functions.name: skeleton_skin_list
functions.description: With this function you can populate a (pre-created) DS list with all the names of the skins included as part of the skeletal animation sprite. The names will be strings and can then be used in the other skeleton animation skin functions for these types of sprite.

params.name: sprite
params.description: The sprite index of the Spine skeletal animation to get the list from.

params.name: list
params.description: The ID of the DS list to populate with the animation names.

functions.name: skeleton_skin_set
functions.description: This function sets the skin used to draw a skeletal animation sprite.

params.name: skinname
params.description: The name (a string) of the skin to use (or a reference returned by the skeleton_skin_create() function).

functions.name: skeleton_find_slot
functions.description: With this function you can find which slots are at a specified room-space position in the Spine sprite associated with the current instance. Note that the list is always sorted in descending order starting from the top-most slot.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position in the room to check.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position in the room to check.

params.name: list
params.description: The ID of the DS list to populate with the DS maps.

functions.name: skeleton_slot_alpha_get
functions.description: With this function you can get an attachment slot alpha value.

params.name: slot
params.description: The slot name to check, a string

functions.name: skeleton_slot_colour_get
functions.description: With this function you can get an attachment slot colour.

params.name: slot
params.description: The slot name to check, a string

functions.name: skeleton_slot_colour_set
functions.description: With this function you can set an attachment slot colour and alpha so all sprites attached to it will be drawn with these blend values. Keep in mind that the instance's sprite can have a blend colour and alpha setting (image_blend and image_alpha), as can the attachment (see the function skeleton_attachment_create_colour()), and so the final colour and alpha that the assigned attachment sprite for the slot will have will be a composite of all these values.

params.name: slot
params.description: The slot name to set, a string

params.name: colour
params.description: The colour to set, either an integer, a constant, or a hex value.

params.name: alpha
params.description: The alpha to set from 0 to 1.

functions.name: skeleton_slot_data
functions.description: With this function you can populate a (pre-created) DS list with data for each of the available attachment slots that an animation contains. This data is returned in the forum of a DS map.

params.name: sprite
params.description: The sprite index of the Spine skeletal animation to get the data from.

params.name: list
params.description: The ID of the DS list to populate with the DS maps.

functions.name: skeleton_slot_data_instance
functions.description: With this function you can populate a (pre-created) DS list with data for each of the available attachment slots for the Spine sprite associated with the current instance (including any attachment modifications). This data is returned in the forum of a DS map.

params.name: list
params.description: The ID of the DS list to populate with the DS maps.

functions.name: skeleton_slot_list
functions.description: With this function you can populate a (pre-created) DS list with all the names of the slots created as part of the skeletal animation sprite. The names will be strings and can then be used in the other skeleton animation slot functions for these types of sprite.

params.name: sprite
params.description: The sprite index of the Spine skeletal animation to get the list from.

params.name: list
params.description: The ID of the DS list to populate with the bone names.

functions.name: sprite_get_bbox_bottom
functions.description: This function returns the relative position of the bottom of the sprite bounding box. This value is given as a relative value based on the upper left corner of the base sprite asset being (0, 0). it is the same value as can be found in the sprite editor for the collision mask properties.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to check.

functions.name: sprite_get_bbox_left
functions.description: This function returns the relative position of the left of the sprite bounding box. This value is given as a relative value based on the upper left corner of the base sprite asset being (0, 0). it is the same value as can be found in the sprite editor for the collision mask properties.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to check.

functions.name: sprite_get_bbox_mode
functions.description: This function will return the current "mode" for the bounding box calculations.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to check.

functions.name: sprite_get_bbox_right
functions.description: This function returns the relative position of the right of the sprite bounding box. This value is given as a relative value based on the upper left corner of the base sprite asset being (0, 0). it is the same value as can be found in the sprite editor for the collision mask properties.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to check.

functions.name: sprite_get_bbox_top
functions.description: This function returns the relative position of the top of the sprite bounding box. This value is given as a relative value based on the upper left corner of the base sprite asset being (0, 0). it is the same value as can be found in the sprite editor for the collision mask properties.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to check.

functions.name: sprite_get_height
functions.description: With this function you can find the height of the base sprite asset, with no transforms, in pixels.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to find the height of.

functions.name: sprite_get_info
functions.description: This function is used to retrieve information for the given sprite.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to get the information for.

functions.name: sprite_get_convex_hull
functions.description: This function is used to generate the points of a convex hull for the given sprite. The function returns an array of reals defining the points of the convex hull.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to generate the convex hull of.

params.name: max_pts
params.description: Use this parameter to specify the maximum number of points that can be returned. (If you are intending to generate a physics polygon shape from the points the maximum is 32)

params.name: subimg
params.description: Use this parameter to specify a specific sprite sub-index to use (defaults to 0)

functions.name: sprite_get_name
functions.description: This function will return the name as a string of the specified sprite.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to get the name of.

functions.name: sprite_get_nineslice
functions.description: This function returns the Nine Slice struct for a sprite, containing all its Nine Slice properties as set in the Sprite Editor or using sprite_set_nineslice().

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite from which the Nine Slice struct will be retrieved

functions.name: sprite_get_number
functions.description: A sprite has to have at least one sub-image and this function will return just how many it has.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite.

functions.name: sprite_get_speed
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the sprite speed as defined for the sprite asset in the Sprite Editor. Note that the return value will be different depending on the type of speed that was applied in the Sprite Editor, either Frames Per Second, or Frames Per Game Frame.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to get the speed of

functions.name: sprite_get_speed_type
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the sprite animation type as defined for the sprite asset in the Sprite Editor.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to get the animation type of

functions.name: sprite_get_texture
functions.description: This function returns a special pointer for the sprite texture page. This value can then be used in other draw functions, particularly in the 2D primitive functions, as well as the Shader functions.

params.name: spr
params.description: The index of the sprite to use.

params.name: subimg
params.description: The sub-image of the sprite to use.

functions.name: sprite_get_tpe
functions.description: This function will return a special value that relates to the position of the given sprite and sub-image on the texture page used by your game.

params.name: sprite
params.description: The index of the sprite to find the texture page entry of.

params.name: index
params.description: The image index of the sprite.

functions.name: sprite_get_uvs
functions.description: This function returns an array with the UV coordinates and other data for the texture of the sprite sub-image on the texture page. The function returns an array with the following 8 elements: [0] = left [1] = top [2] = right [3] = bottom [4] = amount of pixels the asset compiler has trimmed from the sprite's left side [5] = amount of pixels the asset compiler has trimmed from the sprite's top side [6] = normalised percentage of pixel data from the original sprite's width that has been saved to the texture page [7] = normalised percentage of pixel data from the original sprite's height that has been saved to the texture page

params.name: sprite
params.description: The index of the sprite to use.

params.name: subimage
params.description: The sub-image of the sprite to use.

functions.name: sprite_get_width
functions.description: With this function you can find the width of the base asset sprite, with no transforms, in pixels.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to find the width of.

functions.name: sprite_get_xoffset
functions.description: This function returns the x offset of the origin of the given sprite.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to find the xoffset of.

functions.name: sprite_get_yoffset
functions.description: This function returns the y offset of the origin of the given sprite.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to find the yoffset of.

functions.name: sprite_add
functions.description: With this function you can add an image as a sprite, loading it from an external source where the image file to be loaded should always be in either *.png, *.gif, *.jpg/jpeg or *.json format (*json files are used for loading skeleton animation sprites made with Spine). If you use this function with HTML5 or are getting an image from a URL, this function will also generate an Image Loaded asynchronous event.

params.name: fname
params.description: The name (a string file path) of the file to add.

params.name: imgnum
params.description: Use to indicate the number of sub-images (1 for a single image or for a *.gif).

params.name: removeback
params.description: Indicates whether to make all pixels with the background colour (left-bottom pixel) transparent.

params.name: smooth
params.description: Indicates whether to smooth the edges if transparent.

params.name: xorig
params.description: Indicate the x position of the origin in the sprite.

params.name: yorig
params.description: Indicate the y position of the origin in the sprite.

functions.signature: sprite_add(fname, imgnum, removeback, smooth, xorig, yorig)

functions.name: sprite_add_ext
functions.description: With this function you can asynchronously add an image as a sprite, loading it from an external source where the image file to be loaded should always be in either *.png, *.gif, *.jpg/jpeg or *.json format (*json files are used for loading skeleton animation sprites made with Spine). This function will generate an Image Loaded asynchronous event when the sprite has been loaded.

params.name: fname
params.description: The name (a string file path) of the file to add.

params.name: imgnum
params.description: Use to indicate the number of sub-images (1 for a single image or for a *.gif).

params.name: xorig
params.description: Indicate the x position of the origin in the sprite.

params.name: yorig
params.description: Indicate the y position of the origin in the sprite.

params.name: prefetch
params.description: Indicates whether the sprite should be loaded to GPU memory.

functions.name: sprite_add_from_surface
functions.description: This function works in exactly the same way as sprite_create_from_surface() only instead of creating a new sprite from the area of the indexed surface that you select, it adds the defined area of the surface as a new sub-image to a previously created sprite.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to add the new image to.

params.name: surface
params.description: The index of the surface from which the get the image.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position to copy from.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position to copy from.

params.name: w
params.description: The width of the area to be copied (from the x position).

params.name: h
params.description: The height of the area to be copied (from the y position).

params.name: removeback
params.description: Indicates whether to make all pixels with the background colour (left-bottom pixel) transparent.

params.name: smooth
params.description: Indicates whether to smooth the edges.

functions.signature: sprite_add_from_surface(index, surface, x, y, w, h, removeback, smooth)

functions.name: sprite_assign
functions.description: This function takes two previously created (or included) sprite indexes, and copies the image from one to the other. In this way you can copy (or "clone") one sprite into another index. Note that you cannot copy to a game asset. You have to have created the sprite to be copied to previously using the sprite_add() or sprite_duplicate() functions.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to be copied to (i.e.: overwritten).

params.name: sprite
params.description: The sprite to be copied from.

functions.name: sprite_collision_mask
functions.description: With this function you can set the properties of the collision mask that a sprite should have. If you select either automatic (0) or full image (1) as the bounding box mode then the individual bounding box values can be set to 0. However, for a user-defined mask (2) you will have to set these values.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to set the bounding box of.

params.name: sepmasks
params.description: Whether to create collision masks for each sub-image of the sprite (true), or one mask for all (false).

params.name: bboxmode
params.description: What kind of bounding box to use. 0 = automatic, 1 = full image, 2 = user-defined.

params.name: bbleft
params.description: The maximum left position of the bounding box.

params.name: bbtop
params.description: The maximum top position of the bounding box.

params.name: bbright
params.description: The maximum right position of the bounding box.

params.name: bbbottom
params.description: The maximum bottom position of the bounding box.

params.name: kind
params.description: The kind of mask, a constant.

params.name: tolerance
params.description: Indicates the tolerance in the transparency value (0 = no tolerance, 255 = full tolerance).

functions.signature: sprite_collision_mask(ind, sepmasks, bboxmode, bbleft, bbtop, bbright, bbbottom, kind, tolerance)

functions.name: sprite_create_from_surface
functions.description: With this function you can create a sprite from a previously initialised surface (the surface index ID value is returned when you create the surface using surface_create()).

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the surface to create from.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position to copy from.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position to copy from.

params.name: w
params.description: The width of the area to be copied (from the x position).

params.name: h
params.description: The height of the area to be copied (from the y position).

params.name: removeback
params.description: Indicates whether to make all pixels with the background colour (left-bottom pixel) transparent.

params.name: smooth
params.description: Indicates whether to smooth the edges.

params.name: xorig
params.description: Indicates the x position of the origin in the sprite.

params.name: yorig
params.description: Indicates the y position of the origin in the sprite.

functions.signature: sprite_create_from_surface(index, x, y, w, h, removeback, smooth, xorig, yorig)

functions.name: sprite_delete
functions.description: This function will delete a sprite from the game, freeing any memory that was reserved for it. This cannot be used to delete sprites that are included in the game as part of the assets in the Asset Browser.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to be deleted.

functions.name: sprite_duplicate
functions.description: This function will return the index of a newly created sprite that is a duplicate (copy) of the one input as the "index" argument. If the function fails, -1 is returned.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to duplicate.

functions.name: sprite_exists
functions.description: This function returns whether a sprite with the specified index exists or not in the project being run.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to check.

functions.name: sprite_flush
functions.description: With this function you can remove the given texture page for the given sprite from texture memory. Note that the function will return -1 if flush is not supported for the chosen asset, or it will return 0 if all worked correctly.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index (asset name) of the sprite asset to flush

functions.name: sprite_flush_multi
functions.description: This function removes any number of texture pages for the given sprites from texture memory. Note that the function will return -1 if flush is not supported for the chosen resources, or it will return 0 if all worked correctly.

params.name: array
params.description: Array with the sprite indices to flush

functions.name: sprite_merge
functions.description: This function will merge the sprite indexed in argument 1 ("ind2") with that which is indexed in argument 0 ("ind1"). The images themselves are NOT merged together, but rather the image indices are merged, with the sub images from sprite "ind2" appended onto those of sprite "ind1", i.e.: they are added on at the end. Note that if the sprites are different sizes, then the appended sprites are stretched to fit the image size for "ind1".

params.name: ind1
params.description: The index of the sprite to merge.

params.name: ind2
params.description: The index of the sprite that ind1 is to be merged with.

functions.name: sprite_nineslice_create
functions.description: This function is used to create a Nine Slice struct which can be modified and then applied to a sprite.

functions.name: sprite_prefetch
functions.description: This function can be used to prefetch (place into texture memory) a texture page with the given sprite. Note that the function will return -1 if prefetch is not supported for the chosen asset or the target platform is HTML5, or it will return 0 if all worked correctly.

params.name: ind
params.description: The sprite index to fetch

functions.name: sprite_prefetch_multi
functions.description: This function can be used to prefetch (place into texture memory) a number of texture pages that contain the sprites given. Note that the function will return -1 if prefetch is not supported for the chosen asset or the target platform is HTML5, or it will return 0 if all worked correctly.

params.name: array
params.description: Array with the sprite indices to fetch

functions.name: sprite_replace
functions.description: This function works in almost the exact same manner as sprite_add(), only instead of returning the index of the sprite you are importing, it overwrites a previously created sprite index.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to permanently replace.

params.name: fname
params.description: The filename of the image to make the new sprite.

params.name: imgnumb
params.description: The number of frames the sprite will be cut up into horizontally. 1 = one single image / *.gif.

params.name: removeback
params.description: Indicates whether to make all pixels with the background colour (left-bottom pixel) transparent.

params.name: smooth
params.description: Indicates whether to smooth the edges.

params.name: xorig
params.description: The x coordinate of the origin, relative to the sprite's top-left corner.

params.name: yorig
params.description: The y coordinate of the origin, relative to the sprite's top-left corner.

functions.signature: sprite_replace(ind, fname, imgnumb, removeback, smooth, xorig, yorig)

functions.name: sprite_save
functions.description: This function can be used to save any sub-image of a sprite to disc, giving it the specified filename. The sprite must have been added at runtime (you cannot save sprites added through the IDE) and the file must be saved with a *.png extension.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to save.

params.name: subimg
params.description: The sub-image of the sprite to save.

params.name: fname
params.description: The filename for the saved sprite.

functions.name: sprite_save_strip
functions.description: This function will create a strip image from all the sub-images in a sprite, saving it to disc with the specified filename. The sprite must have been added at runtime (you cannot save sprites added through the IDE) and the file must be saved with a *.png extension.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to change the transparency map of.

params.name: filename
params.description: The filename for the saved sprite strip.

functions.name: sprite_set_alpha_from_sprite
functions.description: This function uses the value/saturation of one sprite and multiplies it with the alpha of the target sprite. Ideally the sprite being used to generate the new alpha map should be grey-scale, with the white areas having an equivalent alpha value of 1 (opaque), the black areas being equivalent to alpha 0 (transparent), and the grey areas being an alpha in between 0 and 1.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to change the transparency map of.

params.name: spr
params.description: The index of the sprite to take the transparency map data from.

functions.name: sprite_set_bbox
functions.description: This function can be used to set the bounding box values for a sprite. The positions are absolute values, where the (0, 0) position corresponds to the top-left corner of the sprite, regardless of the offset for the sprite, any "empty" pixels the sprite may have, or where it is being drawn in the room.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to set the bounding box on.

params.name: left
params.description: The left side of the bounding box

params.name: top
params.description: The top of the bounding box.

params.name: right
params.description: The right side of the bounding box

params.name: bottom
params.description: The bottom of the bounding box.

functions.name: sprite_set_bbox_mode
functions.description: This function can be used to set the bounding box mode for a sprite.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to change the mode of.

params.name: mode
params.description: The mode to set (a constant).

functions.name: sprite_set_cache_size
functions.description: This function is used on HTML5 to set how many blended copies of the given sprite to cache before old ones are overwritten (default is 4). This is applied to all sub-images of the sprite.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to change the cache size of.

params.name: max
params.description: The maximum number of cached copies of the sprite that can be stored.

functions.name: sprite_set_cache_size_ext
functions.description: This function is used on HTML5 to set how many blended copies of the given sprite can be cached before old ones are overwritten (default is 4). This is applied to the given sub-image of the sprite.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to change the cache size of.

params.name: index
params.description: The sub-image of ind to change the cache size of.

params.name: max
params.description: The maximum number of cached copies of the sprite that can be stored.

functions.name: sprite_set_nineslice
functions.description: This function is used to apply a Nine Slice struct to a sprite.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to modify

params.name: nineslice
params.description: The Nine Slice struct to apply

functions.name: sprite_set_offset
functions.description: This function can be used to set the x and y origin of a sprite, and takes relative values based on the (0, 0) position being the upper left corner of the sprite.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the sprite to change the offset of.

params.name: xoff
params.description: The x position of the origin.

params.name: yoff
params.description: The y position of the origin.

functions.name: sprite_set_speed
functions.description: This function can be used to set the base animation speed and type for the sprite asset. This is normally set in the Sprite Editor, but there may be moments when you are required to set this manually for a given sprite.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the sprite to get the animation type of

functions.name: tileset_get_name
functions.description: This function will return the name as a string of the specified tile set. This name is the one that has been specified for the tile set in the Asset Browser of the main GameMaker window.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the tile set to get the name of.

functions.name: tileset_get_texture
functions.description: This function returns a special pointer for the tile set texture page. This value can then be used in other draw functions, particularly in the 2D primitive functions, as well as the Shader functions.

params.name: tileset
params.description: The index of the tile set to use.

functions.name: tileset_get_uvs
functions.description: This function returns an array with the UV coordinates and other data for the texture of the given tile set on the texture page. The function returns an array with the following 8 elements: [0] = left [1] = top [2] = right [3] = bottom [4] = amount of pixels the asset compiler has trimmed from the tile set left side [5] = amount of pixels the asset compiler has trimmed from the tile set top side [6] = normalised percentage of pixel data from the original tile set width that has been saved to the texture page [7] = normalised percentage of pixel data from the original tile set height that has been saved to the texture page

params.name: tileset
params.description: The index of the tile set to use.

functions.name: tileset_get_info
functions.description: This function is used to retrieve information about the given tileset.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the tile set to get the name of.

functions.name: timeline_add
functions.description: With this function you can add a new (empty) time line into your game. You should make sure to use the function timeline_delete() whenever you no longer wish it to prevent any possible memory leaks. To add moments to a timeline created in this way, see the function timeline_moment_add_script().

functions.name: timeline_clear
functions.description: With this function you can clear a specific time line of "moments", removing all codes and actions for that time line and leaving it empty.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the time line to clear.

functions.name: timeline_delete
functions.description: This function delete the given time line from your game.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the time line to delete.

functions.name: timeline_exists
functions.description: With this function you can check and see whether a time line exists (returns true) or not (returns false).

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the time line to check for.

functions.name: timeline_get_name
functions.description: This function can be used to get the name of a time line as a string.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the time line to check the name of.

functions.name: timeline_max_moment
functions.description: This function will return the value of the moment in which the timeline performs its final action.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the timeline to get the last moment of.

functions.name: timeline_moment_add_script
functions.description: With this function you can dynamically add a script function to Timelines at any given "moment" within that time line, where a "moment" is the equivalent of one game tick (or step).

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the time line to add a moment to.

params.name: step
params.description: The moment (step) to add to.

params.name: script
params.description: The index of the script function to add into the moment.

functions.name: timeline_moment_clear
functions.description: With this function you can clear a specific moment of any previously defined time line of all codes and actions.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the time line to clear.

params.name: step
params.description: The moment to clear.

functions.name: timeline_size
functions.description: With this function you can get the total number of active moments for a timeline (an "active" moment is one which has GML Code or GML Visual added to it).

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the timeline get the information from.

functions.name: achievement_available
functions.description: This function will return true if the user is currently connected to the internet and the chosen leaderboard and achievement system is available, otherwise it will return false.

functions.name: achievement_get_challenges
functions.description: This function will send a request to the server for information on all current challenges and will trigger a callback Social Asynchronous Event which contains the async_load map populated with the relevant key/value pairs. The id key of this DS Map is used to identify the correct callback (there can be more than one trigger function for any given asynchronous event), and will be paired with the constant achievement_challenge_list_received as well as a number of other key/value pairs for each challenge.

functions.name: achievement_get_pic
functions.description: This function will send a request to the server for the image of a player or a friend and will trigger a callback Social Asynchronous Event which contains the async_load map populated with the relevant key/value pairs. The id key of this DS Map is used to identify the correct callback (there can be more than one trigger function for any given asynchronous event), and will be paired with the constant achievement_pic_loaded as well as a number of other key/value pairs.

params.name: char
params.description: The id of the person to get the image of (either from a friends list or a leaderboard)

functions.name: achievement_increment
functions.description: Games can have achievements with no completion value and so you can use this function to increment those achievement by a given amount. On Android, you send the ID of the achievement as a string (this is the unique achievement ID that got assigned when you set up the achievement), while on all other platforms you supply the defined achievement name as a string, and then you give the actual achievement value to increment by.

params.name: name
params.description: The name/id of the achievement.

params.name: value
params.description: The value to be sent as an increment.

functions.name: achievement_load_friends
functions.description: This function will send a request to the server for information on all the logged in users friends and will trigger a callback Social Asynchronous Event which contains the async_load map populated with the relevant key/value pairs. The id key of this DS Map is used to identify the correct callback (there can be more than one trigger function for any given asynchronous event), and will be paired with the constant achievement_friends_info as well as a number of other key/value pairs for each friend.

functions.name: achievement_load_leaderboard
functions.description: below)

params.name: ident
params.description: The unique ID of the leaderboard as shown on the developer dashboard.

params.name: minindex
params.description: The starting index value to get the leaderboard data from.

params.name: maxindex
params.description: The maximum index value to get the leaderboard data from.

params.name: filter
params.description: Whether to filter the results to those that are on your friends list or to all players

functions.name: achievement_load_progress
functions.description: This function will send a request to the server for information on all available achievements. It will trigger a callback Social Asynchronous Event which contains the async_load map populated with the relevant key/value pairs. The id key of this DS Map is used to identify the correct callback (there can be more than one trigger function for any given asynchronous event), and will be paired with the constant achievement_achievement_info as well as a number of other key/value pairs for each player.

functions.name: achievement_login
functions.description: This function logs the user into appropriate leaderboard and achievement service. If the service is not available, the user is logged into a "pretend" game centre and all achievements and scores are stored on the device so that when the actual service is available, these details can be uploaded. The function will trigger a callback Social Asynchronous Event which contains the async_load map populated with the relevant key/value pairs. The id key of this DS Map is used to identify the correct callback (there can be more than one trigger function for any given asynchronous event), and will be paired with the constant achievement_our_info as well as a number of other key/value pairs for each challenge.

functions.name: achievement_login_status
functions.description: This function is currently only useful for Google Play on the Android platform. It will check to see if the user is already logged into Google services, in which case it will return true, or not, returning false. If it returns true there is no need to call the achievement_login() function.

functions.name: achievement_logout
functions.description: This function logs the user out of the chosen leaderboard and achievement service. This will stop all further achievements and scores from being recorded.

functions.name: achievement_post
functions.description: You can use this function to send your achievements to the chosen leaderboard and achievement service. On Android you will need the the ID of the achievement as a string (this is the unique achievement ID that got assigned when you set up the achievement), while on all other platforms you supply the achievement name as a string, and then you give the percentage that you have completed towards getting the achievement (0 - None, 100 - Completed). The function will trigger a Social Asynchronous Event where the returned async_load DS map will have the following key/value pairs:

params.name: achievement
params.description: The name/ID of the achievement.

params.name: percent
params.description: The percentage of the achievement completed.

functions.name: achievement_post_score
functions.description: You can use this function to send your score to the chosen leaderboard and achievement service. On Android, you send the ID of the score table as a string (this is the unique leaderboard ID that got assigned when you set up the leaderboard), while on all other platforms you supply the defined leaderboard name as a string, and then you give the actual score value. The function will trigger a Social Asynchronous Event where the returned async_load DS map will have the following key/value pairs:

params.name: leaderboard
params.description: The name/ID of the leaderboard.

params.name: score
params.description: The score to be sent.

functions.name: achievement_reset
functions.description: This function will reset all achievements back to their initial values for the game. This function is provided as a debug function and it is not recommended that you permit the end-user to do this in your games.

functions.name: achievement_send_challenge
functions.description: This function will send a challenge across the network to the chosen player. You can get the playerid using the achievement_load_friends() or the achievement_load_leaderboard() functions and you must also supply the challengeid which is the unique value given the challenge when you created it on your iTunes Connect or Google Play dashboard. You must also supply a score, and a short text message as well as set the challenge type. This can be one of the following constants:

params.name: playerid
params.description: The unique ID of the player to challenge.

params.name: challengeid
params.description: The unique challenge ID (as found on the provider dashboard).

params.name: score
params.description: The score to beat.

params.name: type
params.description: the type of challenge to be issued - one of two constants.

params.name: message
params.description: The message to attach to the challenge.

functions.name: achievement_show_achievements
functions.description: This function will open the achievements page for the chosen platform. Please note that this is an asynchronous function, i.e.: your game will continue to run in the background while the achievements page is being shown. As such, you should be careful where you use this and make sure to pause the game or only permit it to be shown in areas of your game where it will not interfere with the game-play.

functions.name: achievement_show_challenge_notifications
functions.description: With this function you can show, or suppress, the various different "toast" pop-up notifications relating to challenges. When the arguments are set to true these messages will appear, informing the player of any local or remote challenges received as well as those challenges that have been completed, while setting them to false will suppress these notifications.

params.name: receive
params.description: Show challenges received pop-up (true) or not (false).

params.name: local
params.description: Show completed local challenges pop-up (true) or not (false).

params.name: remote
params.description: Show completed remote challenges pop-up (true) or not (false).

functions.name: achievement_show_leaderboards
functions.description: This function will open the leaderboards page for the chosen platform. Please note that this is an asynchronous function, i.e.: your game will continue to run in the background while the leaderboards page is being shown. As such, you should be careful where you use this and make sure to pause the game or only permit it to be shown in areas of your game where it will not interfere with the game-play.

functions.name: cloud_file_save
functions.description: This function will commit a file to the chosen cloud service for storage. The function will return a unique id value that should then be used in the appropriate asynchronous event to identify the DS map that is returned as a "call back" from the cloud service. The file should contain all the information that you need to save for your game as you can only store one single "data blob" to the cloud, and running this function again will overwrite any previously stored values (as will using the cloud_string_save() function). The description should be a short string of information that describes the save, e.g.: "Level2, Stage2".

params.name: string
params.description: The file to be uploaded (as a string).

params.name: description
params.description: A brief description of the data being stored.

functions.name: cloud_string_save
functions.description: This function will commit a string to the chosen cloud service for storage. The function will return a unique id value that should then be used in the appropriate asynchronous event to identify the DS map that is returned as a "call back" from the cloud service. The string should contain all the information that you need to save for your game as you can only store one single "data blob" to the cloud, and running this function again will overwrite any previously stored values (as will using the cloud_file_save() function). The description should be a short string of information that describes the save, e.g.: "Level2, Stage2".

params.name: string
params.description: The data string to be uploaded.

params.name: description
params.description: A brief description of the data being stored.

functions.name: cloud_synchronise
functions.description: This function would normally be called at the start of a new game and is used to retrieve the current status of the cloud service at game start up. The function returns a unique id value which would then be used in the Asynchronous Cloud Event to retrieve the relevant information from the DS map that is created.

functions.name: get_integer_async
functions.description: This function opens a window and displays a message as well as a space for the user to input a value. This is an asynchronous function that triggers an asynchronous Dialog event with the event's information held in the variable async_load.

params.name: string
params.description: The message to show in the dialog.

params.name: default
params.description: The default value.

functions.name: get_login_async
functions.description: This function opens a window that asks the user to input a username and password. This is an asynchronous function that triggers an asynchronous Dialog event with the event's information held in the variable async_load.

params.name: username
params.description: The default user name

params.name: password
params.description: The default password

functions.name: get_string_async
functions.description: This function opens a window and displays a message as well as a space for the user to input a string. This is an asynchronous function that triggers an asynchronous Dialog event with the event's information held in the variable async_load.

params.name: string
params.description: The message to show in the dialog.

params.name: default
params.description: The default string.

functions.name: shop_leave_rating
functions.description: This function opens up an OS dependent dialog where you can ask the user to post a rating or comment to a particular page. You can define the text that is to appear in the dialogue, as well as the text you wish to appear on the two buttons and the URL where the comment has to be posted.

params.name: text
params.description: Text that appears on the dialog.

params.name: yes_string
params.description: Text that appears on the "yes" button.

params.name: no_string
params.description: Text that appears on the "no" button.

params.name: url
params.description: The full URL where the comment has to be sent.

functions.name: show_message_async
functions.description: This function opens a window and displays the message you define in the function to the user.This is an asynchronous function that triggers an asynchronous Dialog event with the event's information held in the variable async_load.

params.name: string
params.description: The message to show to the user.

functions.name: show_question_async
functions.description: This function opens a window and displays the question you define in the function to the user.This is an asynchronous function that triggers an asynchronous Dialog event with the event's information held in the variable async_load.

params.name: string
params.description: The question to ask to the user.

functions.name: http_get
functions.description: This function sends a GET request to the specified URL in order to retrieve information.

params.name: url
params.description: The web address of the server that you wish to get information from

functions.name: http_get_connect_timeout
functions.description: This function returns the connection timeout value in milliseconds used for HTTP requests.

functions.name: http_get_file
functions.description: This function connects to the specified URL in order to retrieve information in the form of a file.

params.name: url
params.description: The web address of the server that you wish to get file from

params.name: local_target
params.description: The local storage path to save the file to

functions.name: http_get_request_crossorigin
functions.description: This function can be used to get the cross-origin type set for HTML5 games and will return a string (on all other platforms an empty string "" will be returned).

functions.name: http_post_string
functions.description: This function posts a string using the HTTP POST method.

params.name: url
params.description: The web address of the server that you wish to get information from

params.name: string
params.description: The string you wish to send to the specified URL

functions.name: http_request
functions.description: This function creates a generic HTTP request and sends it.

params.name: url
params.description: The web address of the server that you wish to get information from

params.name: method
params.description: The request method (normally "POST" or "GET", but all methods are supported)

params.name: header_map
params.description: A DS map with the required header fields

params.name: body
params.description: The data to be transmitted following the headers (can be a binary buffer handle)

functions.name: http_set_connect_timeout
functions.description: This function sets the connection timeout used for HTTP requests. Any requests made after a call to this function will use this timeout.

params.name: connect_timeout_ms
params.description: The connect timeout (in milliseconds)

functions.name: http_set_request_crossorigin
functions.description: With this function you can set the cross-origin type to use when loading images from a file (using sprite_add()), or sending custom HTTP requests to servers (e.g. using http_post_string()). The function is exclusively for the HTML5 platform.

params.name: origin_type
params.description: The cross origin type to use

functions.name: push_cancel_local_notification
functions.description: This function cancels the given push notification. You can get the ID for the notification to cancel using the functions push_get_first_local_notification() and push_get_next_local_notification() and the function will return true on success or false otherwise (for example if the notification does not exist or has already been triggered).

params.name: id
params.description: The ID of the notification to cancel.

functions.name: push_get_first_local_notification
functions.description: This function will populate a pre-made DS map with a series of key/value pairs for the first local push notification in the queue to be shown. It returns -1 if there are no notifications queued, or a real value otherwise representing the ID for the notification. This ID can then be used to cancel the notification using the function push_cancel_local_notification().

params.name: map
params.description: The DS Map ID to use.

functions.name: push_get_next_local_notification
functions.description: This function will populate a pre-made DS map with a series of key/value pairs for the next local push notification in the queue to be shown. It returns -1 if there are no further notifications queued, or a real value otherwise representing the ID for the notification. This ID can then be used to cancel the notification using the function push_cancel_local_notification(). You should call the function push_get_first_local_notification() to get the first notification in the queue and then use this function to continue through it.

params.name: map
params.description: The DS Map ID to use.

functions.name: push_local_notification
functions.description: This function can be used to set a local notification to be shown on a given date at a given time. The "fire_time" is the date/time that the notification should be pushed to the user device (you can use the GameMaker Date and Time Functions to get this), and you can give the notification a title and a message text as well as a payload string which will be passed to your game when the users taps the notification.

params.name: fire_time
params.description: The date/time to fire the off the notification

params.name: title
params.description: The notification title (a string)

params.name: message
params.description: The notification message text (a string)

params.name: data
params.description: The data package to send to your game (a string)

functions.name: buffer_async_group_begin
functions.description: This function is called when you want to begin the saving out of multiple buffers to multiple files.

params.name: groupname
params.description: The name of the group (as a string).

functions.name: buffer_async_group_end
functions.description: This function finishes the definition of a buffer async group and starts the saving of the files.

functions.name: buffer_async_group_option
functions.description: This function sets some platform-specific options for the buffer group being saved/loaded.

params.name: option
params.description: The option to set.

params.name: value
params.description: The value to set (can be string or real, depending on the option).

functions.name: buffer_base64_decode
functions.description: This function decodes a base64 encoded string (created using the buffer_base64_encode function) into a new buffer.

params.name: string
params.description: The base64 encoded string to decode

functions.name: buffer_base64_decode_ext
functions.description: This function decodes a base64 encoded string (created using the buffer_base64_encode function) into a buffer.

params.name: buffer

params.name: string
params.description: The base64 encoded string to decode.

params.name: offset

functions.name: buffer_base64_encode
functions.description: This function converts the data in the given buffer into a base64 encoded string.

params.name: buffer

params.name: offset

params.name: size
params.description: The size of the buffer.

functions.name: buffer_compress
functions.description: With this function you can compress part (or all) of a buffer using zlib compression. The function will return a new buffer ID value for the compressed buffer, or a value less than 0 if it has failed for any reason. This function will not alter the original buffer.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to compress.

params.name: offset
params.description: The offset within the buffer to compress (in bytes).

params.name: size
params.description: The size of the buffer area to compress (in bytes).

functions.name: buffer_copy
functions.description: This function can be used to copy a segment (or all) of the data stored in one buffer to another.

params.name: src_buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to copy from.

params.name: src_offset
params.description: The data offset to start copying from (in bytes).

params.name: size
params.description: The size of the data to copy (in bytes).

params.name: dest_buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to copy to.

params.name: dest_offset
params.description: The offset position to copy the data to (in bytes).

functions.name: buffer_copy_stride
functions.description: This function can be used to copy multiple data entries from one buffer to another, with the ability to specify different strides between individual entries in both the source and the destination buffers. The function takes into account the types of both buffers. If a buffer has a fixed size or is not a wrap buffer, the copying process will stop when the read or write position exceeds the buffer's range. Initial read and write positions can be negative, in which case they are computed from the end of given buffer.

params.name: src_buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to copy from.

params.name: src_offset
params.description: The data offset to start copying from (in bytes). If negative, then the offset is computed from the end of the buffer.

params.name: src_size
params.description: The size of a single data entry (in bytes). Must be a non-negative value.

params.name: src_stride
params.description: The number of bytes from the beginning of one entry to the beginning of the following entry in the source buffer. If negative, then the source buffer is traversed backwards.

params.name: src_count
params.description: The number of data entries to copy. Must be a non-negative value.

params.name: dest_buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to copy to.

params.name: dest_offset
params.description: The offset position to copy the data to (in bytes). If negative, then the offset is computed from the end of the buffer.

params.name: dest_stride
params.description: The desired stride between entries when copied to the destination buffer (in bytes). If negative, then the destination buffer is traversed backwards.

functions.signature: buffer_copy_stride(src_buffer, src_offset, src_size, src_stride, src_count, dest_buffer, dest_offset, dest_stride)

functions.name: buffer_copy_from_vertex_buffer
functions.description: This function can be used to copy some (or all) of the vertex data stored in one vertex buffer into a previously created regular buffer. When copying from a vertex buffer into a regular buffer with this function, both buffers must have previously been created (using the vertex_create_buffer() and buffer_create() functions, for example). You can specify the range of vertex data that you wish to copy into the buffer, where the start vertex can be anywhere between 0 and the number of vertices -1, and you can give the number of vertices from that point on to copy. You can use the function vertex_get_number() on the vertex buffer to get the total number of vertices stored. Finally you give the buffer index to copy the vertex data into, as well as a data offset to define the position to copy the vertex data to in the destination buffer.

params.name: vertex_buffer
params.description: The index of the vertex buffer to copy from.

params.name: start_vertex
params.description: The starting vertex.

params.name: num_vertices
params.description: The total number of vertices to use.

params.name: dest_buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to copy to.

params.name: dest_offset
params.description: The offset position to copy the data to (in bytes).

functions.name: buffer_crc32

params.name: buffer

params.name: size

functions.name: buffer_decompress
functions.description: With this function you can decompress a previously compressed buffer using zlib compression. If the decompression has failed (for example, you are supplying a buffer that hasn't been compressed) then the function will instead return a value less than 0.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to decompress.

functions.name: buffer_delete
functions.description: This function deletes a buffer previously created using buffer_create from memory, releasing the resources used to create it and removing any data that it may currently contain.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to delete.

functions.name: buffer_exists
functions.description: This function checks whether the given buffer exists in memory or not. If it does, the function will return true, otherwise it will return false.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to check.

functions.name: buffer_fill
functions.description: This function fills a previously created buffer with a given data type and value.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to fill.

params.name: offset
params.description: The data offset value (in bytes).

params.name: type

params.name: value

params.name: size

functions.name: buffer_get_address
functions.description: With this function you can get a pointer to the raw, aligned buffer address. This is primarily for use with extensions as you can pass this value through to them, allowing them to access the buffer data.

params.name: buffer

functions.name: buffer_get_alignment
functions.description: This function gets the byte alignment of the given buffer.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to check.

functions.name: buffer_get_size
functions.description: This function gets the size in bytes of the given buffer.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the buffer to get the size of.

functions.name: buffer_get_surface
functions.description: With this function you can write information from a surface to a given buffer. The buffer must have been created previously and should be a 1-byte aligned buffer large enough to store data for the surface you are going to write.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to use.

params.name: surface
params.description: The index of the surface to use.

params.name: offset
params.description: The data offset value (in bytes).

functions.name: buffer_get_surface_depth
functions.description: With this function you can write information from a surface's depth buffer to a given buffer. The buffer must have been created previously and should be a 1-byte aligned buffer large enough to store data for the surface you are going to write.

params.name: buffer

params.name: surface
params.description: The index of the surface whose depth buffer to use.

params.name: offset
params.description: The data offset value (in bytes).

functions.name: buffer_get_type
functions.description: This function returns the type of the given buffer.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to check.

functions.name: buffer_load
functions.description: This function is used to load a buffer that was previously saved using the buffer_save() functions, as well as any Included Files or files loaded externally.

params.name: filename
params.description: The name of the file to load from.

functions.name: buffer_load_async

params.name: offset

params.description: The length of the part of the buffer to load (in bytes).

params.name: dest_offset

functions.name: buffer_md5
functions.description: This function takes the input data from a given buffer (or part of the buffer) and returns the 32-character hexadecimal MD5 hash that is unique to that data. In this way you can generate a secure key which can be stored and used to check the integrity of the information being sent to (or received from) an external server (for example).

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to use.

params.name: offset
params.description: The data offset value.

params.name: size
params.description: The size of the buffer.

functions.name: buffer_peek
functions.description: The buffer_peek function reads a piece of data of a certain type from the given buffer at an arbitrary offset position (in bytes). Contrary to buffer_read(), however, this function doesn't use or change the buffer's current "seek" position.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to use.

params.name: offset
params.description: The offset position (in bytes) within the buffer to read the given data from.

params.name: type
params.description: The type of data that is to be read from the buffer.

functions.name: buffer_poke
functions.description: With this function you can write data into a buffer at the specified offset, without changing the seek position. This is different from buffer_write(), which uses the current seek position as the offset and advances that with the amount of bytes written.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to use.

params.name: offset
params.description: The offset position (in bytes) within the buffer to write the given data to.

params.name: type
params.description: The type of data that is to be written to the buffer.

params.name: value
params.description: The data to add to the buffer, in accordance with the type specified.

functions.name: buffer_read
functions.description: This function can be used to read data from a previously created buffer. The return value will depend on the type of data that you are reading, which in itself is defined by one of the BufferDataType constants.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to read from.

params.name: type
params.description: The type of data that is to be read from the buffer.

functions.name: buffer_resize
functions.description: With this function you can resize a given buffer to be the size (in bytes) that you specify.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to change the size of.

params.name: newsize
params.description: The new size of the buffer (in bytes).

functions.name: buffer_save
functions.description: With this function you can save the contents of a buffer to a file, ready to be read back into memory using the buffer_load() function.

params.name: filename
params.description: The name of the file to save as.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to save.

params.name: filename
params.description: The name of the file to save as.

params.name: offset
params.description: The offset within the buffer to save from (in bytes).

functions.name: buffer_save_ext
functions.description: This function saves (part of) the contents of a buffer to a file, ready to be read back into memory using the buffer_load() function.

params.name: buffer

params.description: The offset within the buffer to save from (in bytes).

functions.description: This function moves the seek position of a buffer, setting it relative to the start, end or current seek position (that which was last used when reading or writing data). It also moves automatically when you read from or write to a buffer.

params.name: buffer

params.name: offset

params.name: buffer

functions.name: display_get_dpi_x
functions.description: This function gets the DPI of the device display along the x axis (this value is also dependent on the orientation of the device).

functions.name: display_get_gui_width
functions.description: With this function you can get the width (in pixels) of the GUI as used in the Draw GUI Event.

functions.name: display_get_height
functions.description: This function will return the height of the display (in pixels). Note that on the HTML5 target, this value is the height of the browser window, rather than the physical display size.

functions.name: display_get_orientation
functions.description: This function will return one of two constants GameMaker has to tell you whether the device running the game is being held in landscape or portrait mode. Note that this function may not correctly detect the orientation of the device when used in the HTML5 target module.

functions.name: display_get_sleep_margin
functions.description: This function can be used to get the current sleep margin value used for the render timing of your game, and will return a millisecond value. For more information on display timing, please see display_set_timing_method().

functions.name: display_get_timing_method
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the timing method to be used for rendering your game.

functions.name: display_get_width
functions.description: This function will return the width of the display (in pixels). Note that on the HTML5 target, this value is the width of the browser window, rather than the physical display size.

functions.name: display_mouse_get_x
functions.description: This function will return the mouse x position within the screen. It should be noted that this function only works properly when used on the Windows target. It can be used for HTML5 too, but will only return a value relative to the (0, 0) of the canvas itself, and will not return any value while the mouse is outside of the canvas. For other devices it will return 0, and you should use the device_mouse_raw_x()and device_mouse_raw_y() functions instead.

functions.name: display_mouse_get_y
functions.description: This function will return the mouse y position within the screen. It should be noted that this function only works properly when used on the Windows target. It can be used for HTML5 too, but will only return a value relative to the (0, 0) of the canvas itself, and will not return any value while the mouse is outside of the canvas. For other devices it will return 0, and you should use the device_mouse_raw_x() and device_mouse_raw_y() functions instead.

functions.name: display_mouse_set
functions.description: With this function you can change or set the position of the mouse within the game display.

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate in the display.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate in the display.

functions.name: display_reset
functions.description: This function resets the display settings to those that were set when the game was started and also allows you to change the current level of fullscreen anti-aliasing being used and whether to use vertical synchronisation.

params.name: aa
params.description: The level of anti-aliasing filtering (0, 2, 4 or 8).

params.name: vsync
params.description: Toggle vertical synchronisation to on (true) or off (false).

functions.name: display_set_gui_size
functions.description: This function will only affect things drawn in the Draw GUI Event and can be used to set a specific width and height for all GUI components in that event, and no matter what size of display or window is used to display the GUI, it will be scaled to fit correctly.

params.name: width
params.description: The width of the GUI

params.name: height
params.description: The height of the GUI

functions.name: display_set_sleep_margin
functions.description: This function can be used to set the sleep margin value used for the render timing of your game, and requires a millisecond value.

params.name: milliseconds
params.description: The number of milliseconds for the sleep margin

functions.name: display_set_timing_method
functions.description: This function can be used to set the timing method to be used for rendering your game.

params.name: method
params.description: The timing method to use

functions.name: display_set_ui_visibility
functions.description: This function can be used to show or hide the system UI on Android and iOS only.

params.name: flags
params.description: The Android SYSTEM flags to use (as an integer value).

functions.name: gif_add_surface
functions.description: With this function you can save a frame to a GIF file from a surface. The delay time is calculated in 1/100ths of a second, but note that once the GIF has been created different browsers may interpret the frame delay slightly differently.

params.name: gif_index
params.description: The ID of gif to add the surface data to

params.name: surface
params.description: The ID of the surface to use as the added frame

params.name: delay_time
params.description: The delay time for the frame (in 100ths of a second)

params.name: xoffset
params.description: [Optional] The offset along the X axis of the surface to add from

params.name: yoffset
params.description: [Optional] The offset along the Y axis of the surface to add from

params.name: quantization
params.description: [Optional] The quantization amount from 0 to 3 (0 lowest quality, 3 highest quality, default is 2)

functions.name: gif_open

The function will return the unique ID value used to identify the GIF in subsequent functions, or it will return -1 if the GIF could not be initialized (for example, if the width/height are too big for the memory available).

params.name: width
params.description: The width of the GIF to create

params.name: height
params.description: The height of the GIF to create

params.name: clear_colour
params.description: [Optional] The colour (RGB) to clear the GIF to (defaults to black)

functions.name: gif_save
functions.description: With this function you can save out a GIF animation. Note that GameMaker does not automatically append the .gif file extension, so you should include this as part of the filename string if you wish the saved file to be identified as a GIF. The created GIF will be palletised using the Universal 884 Palette.

params.name: gif_index
params.description: The ID of the GIF to save

params.name: fname
params.description: The filename to use for the GIF

functions.name: gif_save_buffer
functions.description: With this function you can save out a GIF animation. Note that the final GIF data will be palletised using the Universal 884 Palette.

params.name: gif_index
params.description: The ID of the GIF to save

functions.name: screen_save
functions.description: With this function you can save a screenshot of the game as it currently appears in the game window. The file will be saved to the working directory of the game, which in windows is located at <drive>:/Users/YOURUSERNAME/AppData/Local/[Game Name]/ and on Mac it would be ~/Library/Application Support/[Game Name]/. The image captured will be the final render of the application surface of the game, or (if the app surface has been disabled) it will be an image of the whole display or window. It is important to note that the function is designed to be called in the Draw GUI End Event, which should give consistent results across all platforms.

params.name: fname

The selection coordinates are based on the absolute size of the display (or window if not fullscreen), so (0, 0) is always the top-left hand corner of the screen (or window).

params.description: The filename for the screenshot to save

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate of the top left corner of the area of the screen to capture

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate of the top left corner of the area of the screen to capture

params.name: w
params.description: The width of the area of the screen to capture

params.name: h
params.description: The height of the area of the screen to capture

functions.name: camera_apply

params.name: camera_id
params.description: The unique camera ID value returned when you created the camera.

functions.name: camera_copy_transforms

params.name: dest_camera_id
params.description: The unique camera ID value for the camera the values will be copied to.

params.name: src_camera_id
params.description: The unique camera ID value for the camera the values will be copied from.

params.name: y_border

params.name: camera_id

functions.name: camera_get_view_angle

params.name: camera_id

params.name: camera_id

params.name: camera_id
params.description: The unique camera ID value returned when you created the camera
