functions.name: window_center
functions.description: With this function you can centre the game window in the display when the target module is Windows, Ubuntu (Linux) or macOS, or you can centre it in the browser if the target module is HTML5.

functions.name: window_device
functions.description: This function will return the current D3D device pointer, which you can then (for example) pass through to a DLL or Dylib on Windows and macOS.

functions.name: window_post_message
functions.description: This function is for the GX.games target and is used to send a message to the host window containing the game. It takes a string which is sent to the host iframe.

params.name: message
params.description: The message to be passed to the host window

functions.name: window_get_showborder
functions.description: Returns whether the border around the window is shown in windowed mode.

functions.name: window_get_caption
functions.description: This function returns the caption of the window (this is the text that appears on the top of the window, next to its icon).

functions.name: window_get_colour
functions.description: This function returns the background colour of the game window. This colour represents that which will be used for those areas of the game window that are not occupied by any views.

functions.name: window_get_cursor
functions.description: With this function you can get the current cursor being used in the game window.

functions.name: window_get_fullscreen
functions.description: This function returns whether the game window is in fullscreen mode (true) or not (false).

functions.name: window_get_height
functions.description: With this function you can get the current height (in pixels) of the game window.

functions.name: window_get_visible_rects
functions.description: With this function you can find the overlapping region of the rectangle defined by (x1, y1) to (x2, y2) on each of the attached displays. The function will return an array with 8 values per display, where the values [0 ... 3] correspond to the overlapx1, overlapy1, overlapx2, overlapy2 - defining the region of overlap on this display and will be set to 0,0,0,0 if no overlap - and the values [4 ... 7] corresponds to the monitorx1, monitory1, monitorx2, monitory2 - the coordinates of the display in the virtual display space.

params.name: x1
params.description: The left edge of the rectangle to check

params.name: y1
params.description: The top edge of the rectangle to check.

params.name: x2
params.description: The right edge of the rectangle to check

params.name: y2
params.description: The bottom edge of the rectangle to check.

functions.name: window_get_width
functions.description: With this function you can get the current width (in pixels) of the game window.

functions.name: window_get_x
functions.description: With this function you can get the x position (in pixels) within the browser if it is an HTML5 game or within the display if it is a Windows, Ubuntu (Linux) or macOS game.

functions.name: window_get_y
functions.description: With this function you can get the y position (in pixels) within the browser if it is an HTML5 game or within the display if it is a Windows, Ubuntu (Linux) or macOS game.

functions.name: window_handle
functions.description: With this function you can get the internal Windows ID value (the HWND, a pointer).

functions.name: window_has_focus
functions.description: With this function you can poll the window (or tab) state and if it loses focus the function will return false, otherwise it will return true.

functions.name: window_minimise
functions.description: This function minimises the game window. You can restore it with window_restore().

functions.name: window_minimize
functions.description: This function minimizes the game window. You can restore it with window_restore().

functions.name: window_mouse_get_x
functions.description: With this function you can get the x position of the mouse cursor (in pixels) within the browser if it is an HTML5 game or within the display if it is a Windows, Ubuntu (Linux) or macOS game.

functions.name: window_mouse_get_y
functions.description: With this function you can get the y position of the mouse cursor (in pixels) within the browser if it is an HTML5 game or within the display if it is a Windows, Ubuntu (Linux) or macOS game.

functions.name: window_mouse_set
functions.description: With this function you can change or set the position of the mouse within the game window.

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate in the window.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate in the window.

functions.name: window_mouse_set_locked
functions.description: With this function you can enable or disable mouse lock. When enabled, the mouse cursor is hidden and locked at the center of the window. When disabled, the mouse cursor is shown and unlocked. While the cursor is locked, you can still use functions window_mouse_get_delta_x() and window_mouse_get_delta_y() to retrieve how much has it moved since the last frame.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable (true) or disable (false) mouse lock.

functions.name: window_mouse_get_locked
functions.description: Returns whether the mouse cursor was locked using function window_mouse_set_locked.

functions.name: window_mouse_get_delta_x
functions.description: Returns how many pixels the mouse cursor has moved on the x axis since the last frame.

functions.name: window_mouse_get_delta_y
functions.description: Returns how many pixels the mouse cursor has moved on the y axis since the last frame.

functions.name: window_restore
functions.description: This function restores the game window which may have been minimised by the user or using the function window_minimise().

functions.name: window_set_showborder
functions.description: Sets whether the border around the window is shown in windowed mode.

params.name: show
params.description: Whether to show the window border (true) or not (false).

functions.name: window_set_caption
functions.description: With this function you can change or set the windows caption for the room that you are currently in. This caption appears at the top of the window, beside the game icon, when the game is not in full screen mode.

params.name: caption
params.description: The new caption.

functions.name: window_set_colour
functions.description: This function sets the background colour of the game window.

params.name: colour
params.description: The colour to set the region.

functions.name: window_set_cursor
functions.description: With this function you can set the cursor for the game window to any one of the built-in constants.

params.name: cursor
params.description: The cursor to set for the game window.

functions.name: window_set_fullscreen
functions.description: With this function you can set the game window to be full screen (true) or not (false).

params.name: full
params.description: Whether to set the screen to fullscreen (true) or not (false).

functions.name: window_set_max_height
functions.description: This function can be used to set a maximum window height for your game. If you enable the window resize option in the Game Options for the target platform, then the player can resize the game window to any size they wish, however by using this function you can limit the maximum height to the size you specify. If you wish to go back to the default behaviour (i.e.: no minimum), then use a value of -1.

params.name: height
params.description: The maximum height in pixels for the game window.

functions.name: window_set_max_width
functions.description: This function can be used to set a maximum window width for your game. If you enable the window resize option in the Game Options for the target platform, then the player can resize the game window to any size they wish, however by using this function you can limit the maximum width to the size you specify. If you wish to go back to the default behaviour (i.e.: no minimum), then use a value of -1.

params.name: width
params.description: The maximum width in pixels for the game window.

functions.name: window_set_min_height
functions.description: This function can be used to set a minimum window height for your game. If you enable the window resize option in the Game Options for the target platform, then the player can resize the game window to any size they wish, however by using this function you can limit the minimum height to the size you specify. If you wish to go back to the default behaviour (i.e.: no minimum), then use a value of -1.

params.name: height
params.description: The minimum height in pixels for the game window.

functions.name: window_set_min_width
functions.description: This function can be used to set a minimum window width for your game. If you enable the window resize option in the Game Options for the target platform, then the player can resize the game window to any size they wish, however by using this function you can limit the minimum width to the size you specify. If you wish to go back to the default behaviour (i.e.: no minimum), then use a value of -1.

params.name: width
params.description: The minimum width in pixels for the game window.

functions.name: window_set_position
functions.description: With this function you can set the game window to a specific position within the display (on macOS, Linux(Ubuntu) and Windows) or within the browser (HTML5).

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate of where to position the window.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate of where to position the window.

functions.name: window_set_rectangle
functions.description: With this function you can set the position of the game window within the browser (HTML5) or display (Windows, Ubuntu (Linux) or macOS) and set the scale of the window too.

params.name: x
params.description: The new x coordinate of the window.

params.name: y
params.description: The new y coordinate of the window.

params.name: w
params.description: The new width of the window.

params.name: h
params.description: The new height of the window.

functions.name: window_set_size
functions.description: With this function you can change the size of the game window. If you use this function to change the size of the game window, the contents of the window will be scaled to fit with a 1:1 ratio to the background canvas which will keep the image crisp and clear (although scaled if the window is other than the room or view size).

params.name: w
params.description: The new width of the window.

params.name: h
params.description: The new height of the window.

functions.name: window_enable_borderless_fullscreen
functions.description: With this function you can enable borderless fullscreen mode which uses a borderless window when switching to fullscreen rather than making the game take over exclusive use of the display. Note that this will only take effect on the next switch to fullscreen (so if the game is currently running in fullscreen then nothing will immediately change).

params.name: enable
params.description: Whether to enable borderless fullscreen mode (true) or not (false).

functions.name: window_get_borderless_fullscreen
functions.description: This function returns whether fullscreen mode uses a borderless window or whether the game takes exclusive control of the display.

functions.name: window_view_mouse_get_y
functions.description: This function will return the mouse y position relative to the view selected.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the view to compare the mouse position to.

functions.name: ds_grid_resize
functions.description: With this function you can resize the given DS grid to have a different width and/or height. If the grid size is larger than the current grid, the new cells will have a base value of 0, and if the size is smaller then the values held in the cells that are no longer within the new size will be lost. All other cells will be left untouched.

params.description: This index of the grid to resize.

params.name: w
params.description: The new width of the grid.

params.name: h
params.description: The new height of the grid.

params.description: The destination MP grid.

params.name: func
params.description: A predicate function (that is passed the: grid value, cell x and cell y) and should return true (cell is ocupied) or false (cell is empty)

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the grid to write.

functions.name: ds_list_add
functions.description: This function can be used to add a new value (real or string) to the list, which will be added on at the end. The function can take as many further optional arguments as you require, permitting you to add multiple values consecutively to the list in a single call.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the list to add to.
The value to add to the list.

functions.name: ds_list_clear
functions.description: With this function you can clear all data from the given list data structure.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the data structure to clear.

functions.name: ds_list_copy
functions.description: With this function you can copy the contents of one list into another. Both lists must have been created previously and if the list being copied to already has information within it, this list will be cleared first. The end result is two independent lists which contain the same information.

params.name: destination
params.description: The id of the list being copied to.

params.name: source
params.description: The id of the list to be copied from.

functions.name: ds_list_create
functions.description: This function creates a new list data structure and returns a handle to it.

functions.name: ds_list_delete
functions.description: With this function you can remove the value stored at a specific position within the list.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the list to change.

params.name: pos
params.description: Where in the list to delete the value.

functions.name: ds_list_destroy
functions.description: This function will remove the given list data structure from memory, freeing up the resources it was using and removing all values that it contained.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the data structure to remove.

functions.name: ds_list_empty
functions.description: With this function you can check the given DS list to see if it is empty (returns true) or not (returns false).

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the data structure to check.

functions.name: ds_list_find_index
functions.description: With this function you can check the given list for a value and the position within the list for that value will be returned. Note that if there are multiple entries in the list with the same value, the position of any one of them may be returned, and if the value doesn't exist, -1 will be returned.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the list to use.

params.name: val
params.description: The value to find.

functions.name: ds_list_find_value
functions.description: With this function you can check the given list position and the value held within the list for that position will be returned. Note that if you give a position that is outside of the given list size (i.e.: position 11 in a 10 value list) then the function may return undefined or 0.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the list to use.

params.name: pos
params.description: The position to look at, where 0 corresponds to the very beginning of the list and the final position is ds_list_size(id)-1.

functions.name: ds_list_insert
functions.description: This function will add the given value into the list at the given position. if the list contains more values after the given position, their position will be shifted up one to make room making the list larger by one.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the list to add to.

params.name: pos
params.description: The position to add the value, where 0 corresponds to the very beginning of the list and the final position is ds_list_size(id)-1.

params.name: val
params.description: The value to add to the list.

functions.name: ds_list_is_list
functions.description: With this function you can check to see if another DS list is stored at the given position within a DS list.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the list to check.

params.name: pos
params.description: The position within the list to check.

functions.name: ds_list_is_map
functions.description: With this function you can check to see if a DS map is stored at the given position within a DS list.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the list to check.

params.name: pos
params.description: The position within the list to check.

functions.name: ds_list_mark_as_list
functions.description: This function will "mark" (or "flag") a given position within a previously created DS list as holding another DS list, allowing for the correct encoding of the list containing the list into a JSON string with json_encode().

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the list to mark.

params.name: pos
params.description: The position within the list to mark.

functions.name: ds_list_mark_as_map
functions.description: This function will "mark" (or "flag") a given position within a previously created DS list as holding a DS map, allowing for the correct encoding of the list containing the map into a JSON string with json_encode().

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the list to mark.

params.name: pos
params.description: The position within the list to mark.

functions.name: ds_list_read
functions.description: With this function you can recreate a saved DS list (one that has previously been written as a string using ds_list_write()).

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the data structure to read into.

params.name: str
params.description: The string to read from.

params.name: legacy (optional)
params.description: Can be either true or false or omitted completely.

functions.name: ds_list_replace
functions.description: This function will replace the value at the given position by another one.

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the list to change.

params.name: pos
params.description: The position to replace the value, where 0 corresponds to the very beginning of the list and the final position is ds_list_size(id)-1.

params.name: val
params.description: The new value to replace the given value with.

functions.name: ds_list_set

params.name: id
params.description: The id of the data structure to check.

params.description: The id of the list to sort.

params.name: ascend
params.description: Whether the values should be ascending (true) or descending (false) order.

params.description: The id of the data structure to write.

The sprite is specified with the given reference, the width and height of the button specified in pixels (width and height of the sprite is used if not specified). Bits of the sprite can be displayed by specifying the x and y offset along with width and height (if none given then the whole sprite is used). NOTE: if no section is declared a "Default" section will be created.

params.name: dbgref
params.description: reference to the function to call

params.name: dbgrefSprite
params.description: reference to the variable for the sprite index or array of references to variables

params.name: dbgrefSpriteIndex
params.description: reference to the variable for the image index or array of references to variables

params.name: width
params.description: width of button in pixels.

params.name: height
params.description: height of button in pixels.

params.name: xoffset
params.description: xoffset into the sprite in pixels.

params.name: yoffset
params.description: yoffset into the sprite in pixels.

params.name: widthSprite
params.description: width of the sprite in pixels.

params.name: heightSprite
params.description: height of the sprite in pixels.

params.description: Index value to use for array references.

functions.name: show_error
functions.description: This function will show a custom string as an error message. You can also specify whether the game should be aborted after the error, however please note that this only exists for compatibility reasons and showing errors will require the game to be aborted regardless of the value specified in this argument.

params.name: str
params.description: The string to show in the pop-up message.

params.name: abort
params.description: Whether to abort (true) or not (false).

functions.name: show_message
functions.description: This function creates a pop-up message box which displays the given string and a button marked "Ok" to close it.

params.name: str
params.description: The string to show in the pop-up message.

functions.name: show_question
functions.description: This function creates a pop-up message box with two buttons for "Yes" and "No". It returns true or false depending on which one of the two buttons the user presses.

params.name: str
params.description: The string to show in the pop-up question.

functions.name: draw_enable_drawevent
functions.description: With this function you can choose to enable (true) or disable (false) the draw event for all instances in the game, thus giving you control over how and when things are drawn. This can be, for example, useful if you wish to implement a "frame skip" technique.

params.name: enable
params.description: Set to true or false.

functions.name: draw_flush
functions.description: This function flushes the entire draw pipeline.

functions.name: draw_arrow
functions.description: This function will draw an arrow from point (x1, y1) to point (x2, y2). The stem of the arrow is drawn along these points with the actual arrow head being drawn at the end, where the size of the arrowhead is defined by the argument "size" and is calculated as being part of the stem so that the end point is always aligned with the position defined by (x2, y2). The width of the arrow head is calculated automatically in proportion to the length.

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the start of the line.

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the start of the line.

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the end of the line (where the arrowhead ends).

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the end of the line (where the arrowhead ends).

params.name: size
params.description: The length of the arrow in pixels.

params.name: y1

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the right of the button

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the bottom of the button

params.name: up
params.description: Whether the button is up (true) or down (false)

functions.name: draw_circle

params.name: y

params.name: r

params.name: outline

functions.name: draw_circle_colour

params.name: x

params.name: y

functions.name: draw_healthbar
functions.description: With this function you can draw a coloured bar to show a constant value. Although the function uses the word "healthbar" you can use this to display anything you wish as long as the amount to be displayed is a percentage value between 0 and 100 (a percentage of any value can be calculated with the formula (CURRENT_Value / MAXIMUM_value) * 100).

params.name: y1

params.name: x2

params.name: y2

params.name: backcol

params.name: y

params.name: absolute

functions.name: draw_rectangle
functions.description: With this function you can draw either an outline of a rectangle or a filled rectangle where the (x1, y1) position is the top left corner and the (x2, y2) position is the bottom right corner. Please note that the rectangle being drawn may need different values (+/-1 on the x, y, or width or height) to be drawn with the desired dimensions due to differences across the various supported platforms.

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the top left corner of the rectangle.

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the top left corner of the rectangle.

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the bottom right corner of the rectangle.

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the bottom right corner of the rectangle.

params.name: outline
params.description: Whether the rectangle is drawn filled (false) or as a one pixel wide outline (true).

functions.name: draw_rectangle_colour
functions.description: With this function you can draw either an outline of a rectangle or a filled rectangle by defining an area where the (x1, y1) position is the top-left corner and the (x2, y2) position is the bottom-right corner. If it is filled you can define the individual colours for each corner point and if these colours are not the same, you will get a gradient effect from one to the other (the colour settings will override the base colour set with the function draw_set_colour()). Please note that the rectangle being drawn may need different values (+/-1 on the x, y, or width or height) to be drawn with the desired dimensions due to differences across the various supported platforms.

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the left of the rectangle.

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the top of the rectangle.

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the right of the rectangle.

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the bottom of the rectangle.

params.name: col1
params.description: The colour of the top left corner.

params.name: col2
params.description: The colour of the top right corner.

params.name: col3
params.description: The colour of the bottom right corner.

params.name: col4
params.description: The colour of the bottom left corner.

params.name: outline
params.description: Whether the rectangle is an outline (true) or filled in (false).

functions.signature: draw_rectangle_colour(x1, y1, x2, y2, col1, col2, col3, col4, outline)

functions.name: draw_roundrect
functions.description: With this function you can draw either an outline of a rounded rectangle or a filled rounded rectangle where the (x1, y1) position is the top-left corner and the (x2, y2) position is the bottom-right corner. You can define how precise the drawing of the corners is with the function draw_set_circle_precision(), but this function uses a fixed radius for them (should you need to change the corner radius, use the function draw_roundrect_ext()). Please note that the rectangle being drawn may need different values (+/-1 on the x, y, or width or height) to be drawn with the desired dimensions due to differences across the various supported platforms.

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the top left corner of the rounded rectangle (as if it were a normal rectangle).

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the top left corner of the rounded rectangle (as if it were a normal rectangle).

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the bottom right corner of the rounded rectangle (as if it were a normal rectangle).

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the bottom right corner of the rounded rectangle (as if it were a normal rectangle).

params.name: outline
params.description: Whether the rounded rectangle is drawn filled (false) or as a one pixel wide outline (true).

functions.name: draw_roundrect_colour
functions.description: With this function you can draw either an outline of a rounded rectangle or a filled rounded rectangle where the (x1, y1) position is the top-left corner and the (x2, y2) position is the bottom-right corner. If it is filled, you can define the individual colours for the centre and the edges, and if these colours are not the same, you will get a gradient effect from one to the other (the colour settings will override the base colour set with the function draw_set_colour()).You can define how precise the drawing of the corners is with the function draw_set_circle_precision(), but the corners are always drawn with a fixed radius. Should you need to change the corner radius you should use the function draw_roundrect_colour_ext(). Please note that the rectangle being drawn may need different values (+/-1 on the x, y, or width or height) to be drawn with the desired dimensions due to differences across the various supported platforms.

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the left of the rounded rectangle.

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the top of the rounded rectangle.

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the right of the rounded rectangle.

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the bottom of the rounded rectangle.

params.name: col1
params.description: The center colour.

params.name: col2
params.description: The outside edge colour.

params.name: outline
params.description: Whether the rectangle is an outline (true) or filled in (false).

functions.signature: draw_roundrect_colour(x1, y1, x2, y2, col1, col2, outline)

functions.name: draw_roundrect_colour_ext
functions.description: With this function you can draw either an outline of a rounded rectangle or a filled rounded rectangle where the (x1, y1) position is the top left corner and the (x2, y2) position is the bottom right corner. If the rectangle is filled, then the colour arguments will be used to generate a colour gradient from the centre to the edges, where colour 1 is the centre colour and colour 2 the edge colour. You must also supply radius values for the x and y axis (in pixels) and the corners will be rounded by these amounts. You can define how precise the drawing of the corners is with the function draw_set_circle_precision(). Please note that the rectangle being drawn may need different values (+/-1 on the x, y, or width or height) to be drawn with the desired dimensions due to differences across the various supported platforms.

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the left of the rounded rectangle.

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the top of the rounded rectangle.

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the right of the rounded rectangle.

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the bottom of the rounded rectangle.

params.name: xrad
params.description: The radius of the curve along the x axis from the rectangle corners.

params.name: yrad
params.description: The radius of the curve along the y axis from the rectangle corners.

params.name: col1
params.description: The center colour.

params.name: col2
params.description: The outside edge colour.

params.name: outline
params.description: Whether the rectangle is an outline (true) or filled in (false).

functions.signature: draw_roundrect_colour_ext(x1, y1, x2, y2, xrad, yrad, col1, col2, outline)

params.name: y

functions.name: draw_get_alpha
functions.description: This function returns the current value of the draw alpha, which will range between 0 (fully transparent) and 1 (fully opaque). The draw alpha affects the transparency of all draw functions, and can be set with the draw_set_alpha() function.

functions.name: draw_get_colour
functions.description: This function returns the current draw colour which is used for drawing forms, text, primitives and untextured 3D models. This can be set with the draw_set_colour() function.

functions.name: draw_set_alpha
functions.description: With this function you can set the base draw alpha for the game. This value can be set from 0 to 1 with 0 being fully transparent and 1 being fully opaque (the default value), and will affect all further drawing, including backgrounds, sprites, fonts, primitives and 3D.

params.name: alpha
params.description: The alpha to set (between 0 and 1)

functions.name: draw_set_colour
functions.description: With this function you can set the base draw colour for the game. This value will affect all further drawing where appropriate, including fonts, forms, primitives and 3D. If any of those assets are drawn with their own colour value changed, this value will be ignored.

params.name: col
params.description: The colour to set for drawing.

functions.name: make_colour_hsv
functions.description: This function creates a colour based on the hue, saturation and value components.

params.name: hue
params.description: The hue of the colour

params.name: sat
params.description: How saturated the colour is

params.name: val
params.description: How dark the colour is

functions.name: make_colour_rgb
functions.description: This function creates a colour based on the red, green and blue components.

params.name: red
params.description: The red component of the colour

params.name: green
params.description: The green component of the colour

params.name: blue
params.description: The blue component of the colour

functions.name: merge_colour
functions.description: With this function you can take two colours and then merge them together to make a new colour. The amount of each of the component colours can be defined by changing the "amount" argument, where a value of 0 will return the first colour (col1), a value of 1 will return the second colour (col2) and a value in between will return the corresponding mix. For example, a value of 0.5 will mix the two colours equally.

params.name: col1
params.description: The first colour to merge

params.name: col2
params.description: The second colour to merge

params.name: amount
params.description: How much of each colour should be merged. For example, 0 will return col1, 1 will return col2, and 0.5 would return a merge of both colours equally

functions.name: gpu_get_sprite_cull
functions.description: With this function you can check to see whether sprite culling is enabled (returns true) or not (returns false).

functions.name: gpu_get_alphatestenable
functions.description: With this function you can check to see whether alpha testing is enabled (returns true) or not (returns false).

functions.name: gpu_get_alphatestref
functions.description: You can use this function to find the current value for the alpha test reference (default is 0, but you can use gpu_set_alphatestref() to set this value to something other than this).

functions.name: gpu_get_blendenable
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the alpha blending state. If it returns true then alpha blending is enabled, and if it returns false it is disabled. By default this is on and so the function will return true.

functions.name: gpu_get_blendmode
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current blend mode being used for drawing.

functions.name: gpu_get_blendmode_dest
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current destination extended blend mode factor being used for drawing.

functions.name: gpu_get_blendmode_destalpha
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current destination extended blend mode alpha factor.

functions.name: gpu_get_blendmode_ext
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current extended blend mode being used for drawing.

functions.name: gpu_get_blendmode_ext_sepalpha
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current extended blend mode being used for drawing, separating out the blend modes into two parts - the RGB component and the alpha component.

functions.name: gpu_get_blendmode_src
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current source extended blend mode factor being used for drawing.

functions.name: gpu_get_blendmode_srcalpha
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current source extended blend mode alpha factor.

functions.name: gpu_get_blendequation
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current blend equation being used for drawing.

functions.name: gpu_get_blendequation_sepalpha
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current blend and alpha blend equations being used for drawing.

functions.name: gpu_get_colourwriteenable
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current colour write-enable values.

functions.name: gpu_get_cullmode
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the backface culling mode.

functions.name: gpu_get_fog
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the fog settings.

functions.name: gpu_get_state
functions.description: This function will get the current GPU state, returning it as a DS Map. This can then be manipulated or even saved, and you can return this map to the GPU using the function gpu_set_state().

functions.name: gpu_get_stencil_depth_fail
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the stencil operation executed when the stencil test passes but the depth test fails.

functions.name: gpu_get_stencil_enable
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve whether the stencil test is currently enabled (returns true) or not (returns false).

functions.name: gpu_get_stencil_fail
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the stencil operation executed when the stencil test fails.

functions.name: gpu_get_stencil_func
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current stencil test function.

functions.name: gpu_get_stencil_pass
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the stencil operation executed when both stencil and depth test pass.

functions.name: gpu_get_stencil_read_mask
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current stencil test read mask value.

functions.name: gpu_get_stencil_ref
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current stencil test reference value.

functions.name: gpu_get_stencil_write_mask
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the current stencil test write mask value.

functions.name: gpu_get_texfilter
functions.description: With this function you can check to see whether texture filtering (linear interpolation) is enabled (returns true) or not (returns false).

functions.name: gpu_get_texfilter_ext
functions.description: With this function you can check to see whether texture interpolation (linear interpolation) is enabled (returns true) or not (returns false) for a given shader sampler texture.

params.name: sampler_id
params.description: The sampler id from the shader.

functions.name: gpu_get_texrepeat
functions.description: With this function you can check to see whether texture repeating is enabled (returns true) or not (returns false).

functions.name: gpu_get_texrepeat_ext
functions.description: With this function you can check to see whether texture repeating is enabled (returns true) or not (returns false) for a given shader sampler texture.

params.name: sampler_id
params.description: The sampler id from the shader.

functions.name: gpu_get_zfunc
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the z comparison mode.

functions.name: gpu_get_ztestenable
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve whether z-testing is enabled (the function returns true) or not (the function returns false). The default value is that z-testing is disabled, so the function will return false.

functions.name: gpu_get_depth
functions.description: This function returns the current depth (z coordinate) for 2D drawing functions. By default, it will be equal to the current layer's depth, but can be changed using gpu_set_depth.

functions.name: gpu_get_zwriteenable
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve whether z-writing is enabled (the function returns true) or not (the function returns false). The default value is that z-writing is enabled, so the function will return true.

functions.name: gpu_pop_state
functions.description: This function pops the previous GPU state from the stack and applies it. See gpu_push_state() for more information.

functions.name: gpu_push_state
functions.description: With this function you can push the current GPU state onto a stack to be used later. You would generally use this if you want to "save" the current GPU state (things like blend mode, alpha writing, culling, etc., will all be pushed to the stack), then draw something with different settings, and then reset the GPU stack to what it was before (by calling gpu_pop_state()).

functions.name: gpu_set_sprite_cull
functions.description: This function will enable or disable sprite culling for your game (by default this is enabled). By switching sprite culling off you can avoid any problems with for example sprites not being drawn when using custom shaders that alter the position the sprite is drawn at.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable or disable sprite culling (true / false)

functions.name: gpu_set_alphatestenable
functions.description: This function will enable or disable alpha testing for your game (by default this is disabled). By switching alpha testing on you can then use the companion function gpu_set_alphatestref() to set the "cut-off" value at which all alpha values will be set to 0.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable or disable alpha testing (true / false)

functions.name: gpu_set_alphatestref
functions.description: This function will set the reference value for the alpha testing (when it has been enabled using the gpu_set_alphatestenable()). This is the "cut-off" threshold at which pixels with alpha will not be drawn.

params.name: val
params.description: Sets the reference value for alpha testing from 0 to 255 (default value is 0)

functions.name: gpu_set_blendenable
functions.description: This function can be used to toggle alpha blending on and off.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable or disable alpha blending value (true or false).

functions.name: gpu_set_blendmode
functions.description: This function permits you to set the blend mode to one of the basic blend modes in GameMaker.

params.name: mode
params.description: The blend mode to use

functions.name: gpu_set_blendmode_ext
functions.description: This function permits you to create a custom blend mode by setting the different component parts that should be factored together.

params.name: src
params.description: Source blend mode factor.

params.name: dest
params.description: Destination blend mode factor

functions.name: gpu_set_blendmode_ext_sepalpha
functions.description: This function permits you to set the different component parts that should be factored together to create a custom blend mode, selecting different blend mode factors for the RGB components and the alpha component.

params.name: src
params.description: Source blend mode factor for RGB.

params.name: dest
params.description: Destination blend mode factor for RGB.

params.name: alphasrc
params.description: Source blend mode factor Alpha.

params.name: alphadest
params.description: Destination blend mode factor Alpha.

functions.name: gpu_set_blendequation
functions.description: With this function you can change how the final pixel is calculated from the source and destination.

params.name: equation
params.description: The blend equation to use

functions.name: gpu_set_blendequation_sepalpha
functions.description: This function is the same as gpu_set_blendequation(), however it allows you to set two separate equations: the first one is used for the RGB components of the source and destination, and the second one is used for the alpha component.

params.name: equation
params.description: The blend equation to use

params.name: equation_alpha
params.description: The alpha blend equation to use

functions.name: gpu_set_colourwriteenable
functions.description: With this function you can switch on or off the colour channels and the alpha channel for all further drawing.

params.name: red
params.description: Enable/disable the red channel

params.name: green
params.description: Enable/disable the green channel

params.name: blue
params.description: Enable/disable the blue channel

params.name: alpha
params.description: Enable/disable the alpha channel

functions.name: gpu_set_cullmode
functions.description: This function can be used to set the backface culling mode.

params.name: cullmode
params.description: The cull mode to use

functions.name: gpu_set_fog
functions.description: This function can be used to enable or disable fog drawing.

params.name: enableOrArray
params.description: Enable or disable fog OR pass an array of 4 values that contains {enable,colour,start,end} (as returned by gpu_get_fog)

params.name: colour
params.description: The fog colour

params.name: start
params.description: The distance to start applying fog from

params.name: end
params.description: The distance to end the fog

functions.name: gpu_set_scissor
functions.description: This function can be used to set a scissor region that will clip all rendering to the current render target, all coordinates are in render target coordinate system. NOTE: All values are used as integers. NOTE: Each surface and viewport will reset the current scissor region (they are not stacked).

params.name: xOrStruct
params.description: x coord OR a struct that contains {x, y, w, h}

params.name: y
params.description: y coord

params.name: w
params.description: width in render target pixels

params.name: h
params.description: height in render target pixels

functions.name: gpu_get_scissor
functions.description: This function can be used to get the current scissor region, returns a struct that contains {x, y, w, h}.

functions.name: gpu_set_state
functions.description: This function will set the current GPU state using the passed-in DS Map.

params.name: ds_map
params.description: The GPU state to set as a DS Map.

functions.name: gpu_set_stencil_depth_fail
functions.description: This function can be used to set the stencil operation taken when the stencil test passes but the depth test fails.

params.name: stencil_op
params.description: The operation executed when the stencil test passes but the depth test fails.

functions.name: gpu_set_stencil_enable
functions.description: This function can be used to disable or enable the stencil test.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable or disable the stencil test (true or false).

functions.name: gpu_set_stencil_fail
functions.description: This function can be used to set the stencil operation taken when the stencil test fails.

params.name: stencil_op
params.description: The operation executed when the stencil test fails.

functions.name: gpu_set_stencil_func
functions.description: This function can be used to set the stencil test function.

params.name: cmp_func
params.description: The stencil test function.

functions.name: gpu_set_stencil_pass
functions.description: This function can be used to set the stencil operation taken when both the stencil and the depth test pass.

params.name: stencil_op
params.description: The operation executed when both stencil and depth test pass.

functions.name: gpu_set_stencil_read_mask
functions.description: This function can be used to set the stencil test read mask.

params.name: read_mask
params.description: A mask that enables or disables reading of individual bits during stencil test.

functions.name: gpu_set_stencil_ref
functions.description: This function can be used to set the stencil test reference value.

params.name: ref
params.description: The stencil test reference value in range 0 to 255 (inclusive).

functions.name: gpu_set_stencil_write_mask
functions.description: This function can be used to set the stencil test write mask.

params.name: write_mask
params.description: A mask that enables or disables writing of individual bits during stencil test

functions.name: gpu_set_texfilter
functions.description: This function can be used to set the texture filtering (linear interpolation) of all images drawn on the game screen. When enabled (true) all textures (includes sprites) will be smoothed when drawn, meaning that when scaled or moved if there is not a 1:1 pixel ratio then there will be a "smudging" across various pixels which may make images appear blurry. If this is disabled (false) then images will be drawn based on the nearest pixel when scaled or moving which may lead to "blocky" images.

params.name: enable
params.description: Whether to enable or disable texture filtering (default is false, or the value set in the Game Options)

functions.name: gpu_set_texfilter_ext
functions.description: This function can be used to set the linear interpolation for a single sampler "slot" when using Shaders in GameMaker. When this is enabled (true) the sampler texture will be smoothed and if this is disabled (false) then images will be drawn based on the nearest pixel. The default value is that set by the Global Game Options for your game, or that set using the function gpu_set_texfilter().

params.name: sampler_id
params.description: The sampler id from the shader.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable or disable texture filtering (true / false)

functions.name: gpu_set_texrepeat
functions.description: This function can be used to indicate to GameMaker whether textures should repeat (true) or not (false) when used with models and primitives. When enabled the GPU will treat UV coordinates outside of the 0 to 1 range as inside this range (e.g. 1.2, 2.2, 3.2, etc., all become 0.2) which causes texture images to repeat, instead of clamping them between 0 and 1 (no repetition).

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable or disable texture filtering (true / false)

functions.name: gpu_set_texrepeat_ext
functions.description: This function can be used to set whether a single sampler "slot" repeats the given texture when using Shaders in GameMaker. Setting it to true will repeat the texture if the uv coordinates are outside of the 0-1 range, while a setting of false will mean no repeating. Note that for this to work on a single sprite the sprite will need to be marked as being on a "Separate Texture Page" in the Sprite Editor.

params.name: sampler_id
params.description: The sampler id from the shader.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable or disable texture filtering (true / false)

functions.name: gpu_set_zfunc
functions.description: This function can be used to set the z-buffer testing comparison mode (see gpu_set_ztestenable() for more information).

params.name: cmp_func
params.description: The comparison mode to use

functions.name: gpu_set_ztestenable
functions.description: This function can be used to toggle z-buffer testing on or off. When enabled the GPU tests on a per-pixel basis if the source pixel is closer than the destination pixel, which determines whether it is drawn. Note that the default comparison checks if the z value of a pixel is less or equal (cmpfunc_lessequal) than that of the pixel drawn to, but this can be changed using function gpu_set_zfunc().

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable or disable z-buffer testing (true or false).

functions.name: gpu_set_depth
functions.description: This function can be used to change the depth (z coordinate) for 2D drawing functions. By default, the layer's depth will be used. Note that GameMaker will only change the depth when it starts drawing a new layer, so you may want to restore the original value (from gpu_get_depth()) after you're done drawing.

params.name: depth
params.description: New drawing depth.

functions.name: gpu_set_zwriteenable
functions.description: This function can be used to toggle on (true) and off (false) depth ordering using the z-buffer.

params.name: enable
params.description: The comparison mode to use

functions.name: draw_get_lighting
functions.description: This function will return whether lighting is enabled (true) or not (false) for the whole scene.

functions.name: draw_light_define_ambient
functions.description: This function is used to control the ambient light of a scene, which is the light that you have in a scene even without having defined any point or directional light sources.

params.name: col
params.description: The colour to use (either a constant, a real or a hex value).

functions.name: draw_light_define_direction
functions.description: This function is for defining a directional light, where the direction and intensity are set by the values input for the x, y and z unit vector (meaning that they must be between -1 and 1, where 1 or -1 is full intensity, and 0 is no intensity).

params.name: ind
params.description: The index number of the light (arbitrary)

params.name: x
params.description: The x component of the light vector

params.name: y
params.description: The y component of the light vector

params.name: z
params.description: The z component of the light vector

params.name: col
params.description: The colour to use for the light (either a constant, a real or a hex value).

functions.name: draw_light_define_point
functions.description: This function is for defining a positional light, where you can define the x, y and z position of the light, the light range and its colour (which will also affect the perceived intensity of the light as certain colours appear "darker" than others).

params.name: ind
params.description: The index number of the light (arbitrary)

params.name: x
params.description: The x position of the light

params.name: y
params.description: The y position of the light

params.name: z
params.description: The z position of the light

params.name: range
params.description: The light range (in pixels)

params.name: col
params.description: The colour to use for the light (either a constant, a real or a hex value).

functions.signature: draw_light_define_point(ind, x, y, z, range, col)

functions.name: draw_light_enable
functions.description: This function is used to enable a defined light. When you define a positional or a directional light you must assign it an index number which is then used by this function to switch the light on or off. Default is disabled (false).

params.name: ind
params.description: The index number of the light (from 0 to 7)

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable or disable all lighting (true or false)

functions.name: draw_light_get
functions.description: This function will get the specified light parameters as an array with the following 6 elements: * [0] = enabled / disabled (true / false) * [1] = Light Type Constant * [2] = x position * [3] = y position * [4] = z position * [5] = light radius (only for point lights, will be 0 for directional) * [6] = light colour (a real)

params.name: ind
params.description: The index number of the light (from 0 to 7)

functions.name: draw_light_get_ambient
functions.description: This function will return the current colour used for ambient lighting.

functions.name: draw_set_lighting
functions.description: This function is used to enable all lighting effects. Default is disabled (false).

params.name: enable
params.description: enable or disable all lighting (true or false)

functions.name: gpu_get_tex_max_aniso
functions.description: With this function you can get the current maximum level of anisotropy when using the tf_anisotropic filter mode. The returned value will range between 1 and 16.

functions.name: gpu_get_tex_max_aniso_ext
functions.description: With this function you can get the current maximum level of anisotropy when using the tf_anisotropic filter mode on a shader sampler.

params.name: sampler_index
params.description: The index of the shader sampler to get

functions.name: gpu_get_tex_max_mip
functions.description: With this function you can get the currently set maximum mipmap level which is to be used, where a value of 0 is the highest resolution, 1 is to use the first mipmap, 2 is the second, etc.

functions.name: gpu_get_tex_max_mip_ext
functions.description: With this function you can get the currently set maximum mipmap level which is to be used for a given shader sampler. Note that this can be quite useful for avoiding bleeding artifacts when rendering textures, for example, setting the texture page border to 8px and then setting the max mipmap level to 3 will ensure you don't get any bleeding problems at greater render distances.

params.name: sampler_index
params.description: The index of the shader sampler to get

functions.name: gpu_get_tex_min_mip
functions.description: With this function you can get the minimum mipmap level which is currently used, where a value of 0 is the highest resolution, 1 is to use the first mipmap, 2 is the second, etc.

functions.name: gpu_get_tex_min_mip_ext
functions.description: With this function you can get the minimum mipmap level which is currently used for a given shader sampler.

params.name: sampler_index
params.description: The index of the shader sampler to get

functions.name: gpu_get_tex_mip_bias
functions.description: With this function you can retrieve the mipmap bias value, where a value of 0 equals no bias, 1 equals the first mipmap, 2 equals the second mipmap, etc. This controls the rate at which the mip map is swapped and will generally make rendered textures blurrier the higher the value and the greater the "distance" being viewed. Note that this can return negative values too, in which case rendered textures will be sharper over a greater distance the lower the value.

functions.name: gpu_get_tex_mip_bias_ext
functions.description: With this function you can retrieve the mipmap bias value for a given shader sampler. Note that this can return negative values too, in which case shader textures will be sharper over a greater distance the lower the value.

params.name: sampler_index
params.description: The index of the shader sampler to get

functions.name: gpu_get_tex_mip_enable

functions.name: gpu_get_tex_mip_enable_ext
functions.description: With this function you can get whether mipmapping is switched off, switched on for everything or switched on only for texture groups selected in the Texture Group Manager on a shader sampler.

params.name: sampler_index
params.description: The index of the shader sampler to get

functions.name: gpu_get_tex_mip_filter

functions.name: gpu_get_tex_mip_filter_ext

params.name: setting
