functions.name: gpu_set_tex_mip_filter
functions.description: With this function you can set the current mip filter mode to one of the three types supported.

params.name: filter
params.description: The mip filter mode to use (a constant, default: tf_point).

functions.name: gpu_set_tex_mip_filter_ext
functions.description: With this function you can set the mip filter mode for a given shader sampler.

params.name: sampler_index
params.description: The index of the shader sampler to get.

params.name: filter
params.description: The mip filter mode to use (a constant, default: tf_point).

functions.name: effect_clear
functions.description: This will clear all particles that are currently visible in the room which have been made using the effect_create_* functions.

functions.name: effect_create_above
functions.description: With this function you can create a simple effect above all instances of your room (it is actually created at a depth of -15000). If the effect is anything other than ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large.

params.name: kind
params.description: The kind of effect (use one of the constants listed above).

params.name: x
params.description: The x positioning of the effect if relevant.

params.name: y
params.description: The y positioning of the effect if relevant.

params.name: size
params.description: The size of the effect.

params.name: colour
params.description: The colour of the effect.

functions.name: effect_create_below
functions.description: With this function you can create a simple effect below all instances of your room (it is actually created at a depth of 50). If the effect is anything other than ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large.

params.name: kind
params.description: The kind of effect (use one of the constants listed above).

params.name: x
params.description: The x positioning of the effect if relevant.

params.name: y
params.description: The y positioning of the effect if relevant.

params.name: size
params.description: The size of the effect.

params.name: colour
params.description: The colour of the effect.

functions.name: effect_create_layer
functions.description: With this function you can create a simple effect on a specified layer. If the effect is anything other than ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large.

params.name: layer_id
params.description: The layer ID (or name) to assign the created effect to.

params.name: kind
params.description: The kind of effect (use one of the constants listed above).

params.name: x
params.description: The x positioning of the effect if relevant.

params.name: y
params.description: The y positioning of the effect if relevant.

params.name: size
params.description: The size of the effect.

params.name: colour
params.description: The colour of the effect.

functions.signature: effect_create_layer(layer_id, kind, x, y, size, colour)

functions.name: effect_create_depth
functions.description: With this function you can create a simple effect at a specified depth. If the effect is anything other than ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large.

params.name: depth
params.description: The depth to assign the created effect to.

params.name: kind
params.description: The kind of effect (use one of the constants listed above).

params.name: x
params.description: The x positioning of the effect if relevant.

params.name: y
params.description: The y positioning of the effect if relevant.

params.name: size
params.description: The size of the effect.

params.name: colour
params.description: The colour of the effect.

functions.signature: effect_create_depth(depth, kind, x, y, size, colour)

functions.name: part_emitter_burst
functions.description: This function allows you to set an emitter to burst a specific type of particle and is typically used in alarms and destroy events as it is a one off code that creates the number of particles specified all at once following the distribution, shape and position set by the function part_emitter_region(). Should you need the particles to appear every step, you should be using the function part_emitter_stream() instead.

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system that the emitter is in.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the emitter to burst from.

params.name: parttype
params.description: The index (type) of the particles to be created.

params.name: number
params.description: The number of particles to create.

functions.name: part_emitter_clear
functions.description: With this function you can clear the given emitter from the specified particle system back to its default state. This will also stop any particles that are being streamed from the emitter at the time, and if you wish to use the emitter again you will need to set the region position and particle type using the part_emitter_region() function.

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system that the emitter is in.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the emitter to clear.

functions.name: part_emitter_create
functions.description: This function must be used to create a new emitter and assign it to a given particle system. The emitter must be destroyed when no longer being used to prevent memory leaks

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system to create the emitter in.

functions.name: part_emitter_destroy
functions.description: This function will remove the specified emitter from the given system and clear it from memory (this will also stop any particles from being produced by the given emitter, but does NOT remove existing ones from the room). This function should always be called when the given emitter is no longer needed for the system to prevent memory leaks and errors.

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system to destroy the emitter from.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the emitter to destroy.

functions.name: part_emitter_destroy_all
functions.description: This function will remove all defined emitters from the given system and clear them from memory (this will also stop any particles from being produced by the given emitter, but does NOT remove existing ones from the room). This function should always be called when the emitters are no longer needed for the system to prevent memory leaks and errors.

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system to destroy all emitters from.

functions.name: part_emitter_enable
functions.description: With this function you can enable or disable a particle emitter. Disabled particle emitters are not updated nor rendered and they do not spawn new particles.

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system that the emitter is in.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the emitter to enable or disable.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable (true) or disable (false) the particle emitter.

functions.name: part_emitter_exists
functions.description: With this function you can check to see if the given particle emitter indexed exists in the given system or not. Note that if the variable being checked is an uninitialised variable (that a particle emitter would otherwise have its index assigned to) this will throw an error.

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system to check for an emitter.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the emitter to search for.

functions.name: part_emitter_region
functions.description: This function is used to set the position of a particle emitter within the current room.

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system that the emitter is in.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the emitter to set.

params.name: xmin
params.description: The x coordinate of the left side of the region.

params.name: xmax
params.description: The x coordinate of the right side.

params.name: ymin
params.description: The y coordinate of the top of the region.

params.name: ymax
params.description: The y coordinate of the bottom of the region.

params.name: shape
params.description: The shape of the region.

params.name: distribution
params.description: The distribution style of the particles.

functions.signature: part_emitter_region(ps, ind, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, shape, distribution)

functions.name: part_emitter_stream
functions.description: This function allows you to set an emitter to stream a specific type of particle and is typically used in the create event as it is a one-off code that sets the emitter to generate the number of particles specified every step of the game thereafter.

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system that the emitter is in.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the emitter to burst from.

params.name: parttype
params.description: The index (type) of the particles to be created.

params.name: number
params.description: The number of particles to create per step.

functions.name: part_emitter_delay
functions.description: With this function you can configure an emitter's delay before it bursts first particles when it is in a stream mode.

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system that the emitter is in.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the emitter.

params.name: delay_min
params.description: The minimum length of the delay.

params.name: delay_max
params.description: The maximum length of the delay.

params.name: delay_unit
params.description: The units that the delay is measured in.

functions.name: part_emitter_interval
functions.description: With this function you can configure the interval between individual particle bursts when an emitter is in a stream mode.

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system that the emitter is in.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the emitter.

params.name: interval_min
params.description: The minimum length of the interval.

params.name: interval_max
params.description: The maximum length of the interval.

params.name: interval_unit
params.description: The units that the interval is measured in.

functions.name: part_emitter_relative
functions.description: With this function you can enable relative mode for an emitter, which means that the number of particles it burst or streams becomes relative to its area.

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system that the emitter is in.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the emitter.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable (true) or disable (false) relative mode.

functions.name: part_particles_clear
functions.description: With this function you can clear all the particles currently created by the system from the room. It does not reset or remove the particle types themselves, just their visual representation, and if you have any object streaming particles from an emitter, these particles disappear but will begin to appear again the next step after calling this code.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system.

functions.name: part_particles_count
functions.description: With this function you can check to see if a particle system currently has any particles created in the room, and it will return the number of them too.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system.

functions.name: part_particles_create
functions.description: This function is ideal for those effects that do not require any of the functionality offered by particle emitters (for example, to create smoke from a missile, or a simple explosion effect) as it permits you to quickly and easily create particles at any position in the game room. Note that you must have created the particle system and the particle type previously for this function to be used.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system.

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate of where to create the particles.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate of where to create the particles.

params.name: parttype
params.description: The index (type) of the particles to be created.

params.name: number
params.description: The number of particles to create.

functions.name: part_particles_create_colour
functions.description: This function is ideal for those effects that do not require any of the functionality offered by particle emitters (for example, to create smoke from a missile, or a simple explosion effect) as it permits you to quickly and easily create particles at any position in the game room.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system.

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate of where to create the particles.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate of where to create the particles.

params.name: parttype
params.description: The index (type) of the particles to be created.

params.name: colour
params.description: The colour blending for the particles.

params.name: number
params.description: The number of particles to create.

functions.signature: part_particles_create_colour(ind, x, y, parttype, colour, number)

functions.name: part_particles_burst
functions.description: This function allows you to burst all particles defined in a particle system asset at any position in the room.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system.

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate of where to burst the particles.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate of where to burst the particles.

params.name: partsys
params.description: The particle system asset to burst.

functions.name: part_system_automatic_draw
functions.description: This function can be used to switch off the drawing of a particle system so that any updates done to the system (automatic or otherwise) will not be seen.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system to change.

params.name: automatic
params.description: Whether automatic drawing is on (true) or not (false).

functions.name: part_system_automatic_update
functions.description: This function controls whether GameMaker should update the particle system automatically or not, and normally you would not need to use this function as the default value of true (automatic update is on) is what you wish to happen.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system to change.

params.name: automatic
params.description: Whether automatic updating is on (true) or not (false).

functions.name: part_system_clear
functions.description: With this function you can clear the indexed system to its default state, removing all emitters and resetting the depth and position (if they had been changed).

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system to clear.

functions.name: particle_add
functions.description: With this function you can create a new particle system assset from an info struct.

params.name: info
params.description: The info struct to create a new particle system asset from.

functions.name: particle_delete
functions.description: With this function you can delete a particle system asset.

params.name: ind
params.description: The particle system asset to delete.

functions.name: particle_exists
functions.description: With this function you can check to see if a particle system asset with the given index exists or not.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system asset to check for.

functions.name: particle_get_info
functions.description: This function is used to retrieve information for the given particle system asset or instance.

params.name: partsys
params.description: The particle system for which information should be retrieved.

functions.name: part_system_create
functions.description: This function is used to create a new particle system and will return a unique index number that should be stored and used in all further functions relating to that system. The system will be assigned a managed layer and will be set to have a depth of 0. Managed layers are not accessible to the user and used only for internal management when depth is used instead of layers. Normally you would use the function part_system_create_layer() instead of this one.

params.name: partsys
params.description: A particle system asset to create an instance of.

functions.name: part_system_create_layer
functions.description: This function will create a new particle system on a given layer.

params.name: layer
params.description: The layer ID value or string to assign the particle system to (can be any layer type)

params.name: persistent
params.description: Flag the particle system as persistent (set to true) or not (set to false)

params.name: partsys
params.description: A particle system asset to create an instance of.

functions.name: part_system_depth
functions.description: With this function you can set the draw depth for the particle system, much the same as you can set the render depth of different layers within the room, where a low draw depth means that it will appear on top of all things drawn with a higher depth, and a high draw depth placing it below everything with a lower draw depth.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system to change.

params.name: depth
params.description: The depth at which to set the particle system.

functions.name: part_system_destroy
functions.description: With this function you can destroy a given particle system and remove it from memory.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system to destroy.

functions.name: part_system_update
functions.description: This function will advance the given particle system one step in game time and can be used to simulate the particle system behaviour when automatic updating is off, or it can be used to advance a particle system to a specific point all in one step.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system to update.

functions.name: part_system_draw_order
functions.description: With this function you can set the order in which particles in the given particle system are drawn when created on the screen, either old to new or new to old.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system to change.

params.name: oldtonew
params.description: Whether old particles should be drawn behind newer ones (true) or vice versa (false).

functions.name: part_system_exists
functions.description: With this function you can check to see if the given particle system indexed exists in the game or not.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system to check for.

functions.name: part_system_get_layer
functions.description: This function retrieves the layer handle for the given particle system.

params.name: ind
params.description: The particle system ID value to get the layer ID of

functions.name: part_system_layer
functions.description: This function can be used to switch a particle system from its current layer to a new one.

params.name: ps
params.description: The particle system ID

params.name: layer
params.description: The new layer ID

functions.name: part_system_global_space
functions.description: This function can be used to enable global space particles. When enabled, particles keep their position and direction when the particle system is moved or rotated. This is by default disabled.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable (true) or disable (false) global space particles.

functions.name: part_system_get_info
functions.description: This function is used to retrieve information for the given particle system instance.

params.name: partsys
params.description: The particle system for which information should be retrieved.

functions.name: part_system_color
functions.description: This function can be used to change color and alpha with which the particle system is blended.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system to change the color and alpha of.

params.name: color
params.description: The new color with which to blend the particle system. c_white is to display it normally.

params.name: alpha
params.description: The new alpha of the particle system (from 0 to 1 where 0 is transparent and 1 opaque).

functions.name: part_system_colour
functions.description: This function can be used to change colour and alpha with which the particle system is blended.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system to change the colour and alpha of.

params.name: colour
params.description: The new colour with which to blend the particle system. c_white is to display it normally.

params.name: alpha
params.description: The new alpha of the particle system (from 0 to 1 where 0 is transparent and 1 opaque).

functions.name: part_system_position
functions.description: With this function you can set the base position for the particle system relative to the (0, 0) position of the room, meaning that all further particle functions relating to this system will now be drawn relative to the new position.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system to change.

params.name: x
params.description: The new x coordinate of the particle system.

params.name: y
params.description: The new y coordinate of the particle system.

functions.name: part_system_angle
functions.description: This function can be used to change the rotation of the particle system.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle system to change the rotation of.

params.name: angle
params.description: The new rotation of the particle system in degrees.

functions.name: part_type_alpha1
functions.description: This function is used to set a particle type to have a single alpha value (transparency) for the total duration of the lifetime of each individual particle, and this can be from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque).

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: alpha1
params.description: The alpha of the particle.

functions.name: part_type_alpha2
functions.description: This function can be used to set an alpha value (transparency) gradient for each particle created of the given type. The first alpha is that which all particles will start with, and the second alpha is the one on with which the particle will end with, and a smooth gradient change will occur to the alpha over the particle's lifetime from one to the other. This can be from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque).

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: alpha1
params.description: The start alpha of the particle.

params.name: alpha2
params.description: The end alpha of the particle.

functions.name: part_type_alpha3
functions.description: This function can be used to set a three alpha (transparency) value gradient for each particle created of the given type. The first alpha is that which all particles will start with, and the second alpha is the one that will be blended to half way through its lifetime and the third alpha is the one with which the particle will end with. A smooth gradient change will occur through the alphas over the particle's lifetime from one to the other.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: alpha1
params.description: The starting alpha of the particle.

params.name: alpha2
params.description: The halfway point alpha of the particle.

params.name: alpha3
params.description: The ending alpha of the particle.

functions.name: part_type_blend
functions.description: With this function you can make your particles be drawn with an additive blend mode (true) or not (false). Additive blending is a special blend mode that adds the luminosity values of each particle as they overlap, so that light colours will gradually get brighter (until they appear white) as they overlap, and dark colours become more and more transparent with black being almost invisible.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: additive
params.description: Whether the particles should be blended additively (true) or normally (false).

functions.name: part_type_clear
functions.description: With this function you can "reset" a particle, returning all the values for each of the functions relating to the particle (life, colour, alpha, orientation, etc.) to their default values. Note that this function does not remove any particles currently visible in the room from the screen, for that you should be using part_particles_clear().

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to clear.

functions.name: part_type_colour1
functions.description: This function is used to set a particle type to be a single colour for the total duration of the lifetime of each individual particle.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: colour1
params.description: The single colour to make the particle type.

functions.name: part_type_colour2
functions.description: This function can be used to set a two colour gradient for each particle created of the given type. The first colour is that which all particles will start with, and the second colour is the one on which the particle will end with, and a smooth gradient change will occur to the colour over the particle's lifetime from one colour to the other.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: colour1
params.description: The colour the particle will start at.

params.name: colour2
params.description: The colour the particle will end at.

functions.name: part_type_colour3
functions.description: This function can be used to set a three colour gradient for each particle created of the given type. The first colour is that which all particles will start with, and the second colour is the one that will be blended to half way through its lifetime and the third colour is the one with which the particle will end with. A smooth gradient change will occur through the colours over the particle's lifetime from one colour to the other.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: colour1
params.description: The colour the particle will start at.

params.name: colour2
params.description: The colour the particle will be halfway through its lifespan.

params.name: colour3
params.description: The colour the particle will end at.

functions.name: part_type_colour_hsv
functions.description: With this function you can set a hue, saturation and value range for all particles of the given type. In this way you can create particles of the same hue but different saturations, or of different hues but the same value (luminosity), etc. All values must be between 0 and 255.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: hmin
params.description: The minimum the final colour's hue component can be.

params.name: hmax
params.description: The maximum the final colour's hue component can be.

params.name: smin
params.description: The minimum the final colour's saturation component can be.

params.name: smax
params.description: The maximum the final colour's saturation component can be.

params.name: vmin
params.description: The minimum the final colour's value component can be.

params.name: vmax
params.description: The maximum the final colour's value component can be.

functions.signature: part_type_colour_hsv(ind, hmin, hmax, smin, smax, vmin, vmax)

functions.name: part_type_colour_mix
functions.description: With this function you can set the given particle type to be a random blend of two colours.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: colour1
params.description: The first colour the blend will take from.

params.name: colour2
params.description: The second colour the blend will take from.

functions.name: part_type_colour_rgb
functions.description: With this function you can set the mix of red, green and blue colours for all particles created of the given type. All values must be between 0 and 255.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: rmin
params.description: The minimum the final colour's red component can be.

params.name: rmax
params.description: The maximum the final colour's red component can be.

params.name: gmin
params.description: The minimum the final colour's green component can be.

params.name: gmax
params.description: The maximum the final colour's green component can be.

params.name: bmin
params.description: The minimum the final colour's blue component can be.

params.name: bmax
params.description: The maximum the final colour's blue component can be.

functions.signature: part_type_colour_rgb(ind, rmin, rmax, gmin, gmax, bmin, bmax)

functions.name: part_type_create
functions.description: With this function you can create a new particle type and the return value should be stored in a variable for use in all subsequent particle functions.

functions.name: part_type_death
functions.description: This function can be used to make your particle burst another type of particle at the end of its lifetime.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: death_number
params.description: The quantity of the new particle to create at the particle death. If a negative value, it will instead create a fraction chance one is created (e.g. -3 would mean that one is created every 3 or so steps).

params.name: death_type
params.description: The index of the particle type to create.

functions.name: part_type_destroy
functions.description: With this function you can remove the specified particle type from the game. When you use this function, all particles of the given type will disappear from the room and the particle itself is removed form memory, so this function should be used only when you no longer need the particle.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to destroy.

functions.name: part_type_direction
functions.description: This function is used to determine the direction of the particle when it is created and can also be used to make the particle increase or decrease its direction over its lifetime.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: dir_min
params.description: The minimum direction the particle can start at.

params.name: dir_max
params.description: The maximum direction the particle can start at.

params.name: dir_incr
params.description: How much the particle direction should increase or decrease per step.

params.name: dir_wiggle
params.description: How much should randomly be added or subtracted from the particle's direction per step.

functions.name: part_type_exists
functions.description: With this function you can check to see if the given particle type indexed exists in the game or not. Note that if the variable being checked is an uninitialised variable (that a particle type would otherwise have its index assigned to) this will throw an error.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to check for.

functions.name: part_type_gravity
functions.description: This function will set the gravity that is to affect each particle of the given type that is created.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: grav_amount
params.description: Strength of the gravity.

params.name: grav_direction
params.description: The direction of the gravity.

functions.name: part_type_life
functions.description: This is the function that governs how long each individual particle of the indicated type remains on the screen. You provide a minimum and a maximum value (in steps)and each particle lifespan will be a random number of steps from within the specified range. To have all particles with the same lifetime, set the two values to be the same.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: life_min
params.description: The minimum lifespan of the particles.

params.name: life_max
params.description: The maximum lifespan of the particles.

functions.name: part_type_orientation
functions.description: This function is used to determine the orientation of the particle sprite when it is created and can also be used to make the particle orientation increase or decrease over its lifetime. The minimum and maximum orientation values default at 0 but these values can be changed to randomise the orientation following the standard GameMaker directions of 0 degrees being right, 90 degrees being up, 180 degrees being left and 270 degrees being down. If you set them to the same value the particles will all be created with the same orientation.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: ang_min
params.description: The minimum starting angle of the particles.

params.name: ang_max
params.description: The maximum starting angle of the particles.

params.name: ang_incr
params.description: The increase (or decrease if set negative) of the angle in degrees per step.

params.name: ang_wiggle
params.description: The amount the angle wiggles clockwise/counterclockwise per step.

params.name: ang_relative
params.description: Whether to set its angle relative to the direction of the particle's motion (true) or not (false).

functions.signature: part_type_orientation(ind, ang_min, ang_max, ang_incr, ang_wiggle, ang_relative)

functions.name: part_type_scale
functions.description: This function will set the horizontal and vertical scale of the particle before any other size changes are made. This function works on the ratio of the sprite size, so a value of 1 (the default value) is a 1:1 ratio, meaning that 0.5 would be half and 2 double.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: xscale
params.description: The horizontal scaling of the base particle.

params.name: yscale
params.description: The vertical scaling of the base particle.

functions.name: part_type_shape
functions.description: With this function you can set the sprite shape to use for the particle type.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to set.

params.name: shape
params.description: The shape to choose.

functions.name: part_type_size
functions.description: This function is used to determine the size of the particle when it is created and can also be used to make the particle increase or decrease in size over its lifetime.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: size_min
params.description: The minimum size the particle can start at.

params.name: size_max
params.description: The maximum size the particle can start at.

params.name: size_incr
params.description: How much the particle should increase or decrease per step.

params.name: size_wiggle
params.description: How much should randomly be added or subtracted from the particles size per step.

functions.name: part_type_size_x
functions.description: This function is used to configure particle size similarly to part_type_size(), except only for the x axis. You can use function part_type_size_y() to configure the size on the y axis separately as well.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: size_min
params.description: The minimum size the particle can start at on the x axis.

params.name: size_max
params.description: The maximum size the particle can start at on the x axis.

params.name: size_incr
params.description: How much the particle should increase or decrease on the x axis per step.

params.name: size_wiggle
params.description: How much should randomly be added or subtracted from the particles size on the x axis per step.

functions.name: part_type_size_y
functions.description: This function is used to configure particle size similarly to part_type_size(), except only for the y axis. You can use function part_type_size_x() to configure the size on the x axis separately as well.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: size_min
params.description: The minimum size the particle can start at on the y axis.

params.name: size_max
params.description: The maximum size the particle can start at on the y axis.

params.name: size_incr
params.description: How much the particle should increase or decrease on the y axis per step.

params.name: size_wiggle
params.description: How much should randomly be added or subtracted from the particles size on the y axis per step.

functions.name: part_type_speed
functions.description: This function is used to set the movement speed of the particle when it is created and can also be used to make the particle increase or decrease its speed over its lifetime.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: speed_min
params.description: The minimum speed the particle can start at.

params.name: speed_max
params.description: The maximum speed the particle can start at.

params.name: speed_incr
params.description: How much the particle speed should increase or decrease per step.

params.name: speed_wiggle
params.description: How much should randomly be added or subtracted from the particle's speed per step.

functions.name: part_type_sprite
functions.description: This function can be used to set a particle type to use a custom sprite from the game assets. You can choose a random sub-image so that if the sprite is not animated, a different image will be chosen at random to create the sprite, or if the particle is animated it will start the animation at a random point.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: sprite
params.description: The index of the sprite to set the particle type to.

params.name: animate
params.description: Whether to follow the sprite's animation normally (true) or not (false).

params.name: stretch
params.description: Whether to stretch the sprite's animation to match the particle lifespan (true) or not (false).

params.name: random
params.description: Whether to choose a random sub-image (true) or not (false).

functions.name: part_type_subimage
functions.description: This function can be used to set a particle type to use a custom sub-image (frame) of a sprite. If the particle's sprite is animated, then this sub-image will be used as the starting frame of the animation.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: subimg
params.description: The sub-image (frame) of the sprite to use.

functions.name: part_type_step
functions.description: This function can be used to make your particle type stream another type each step until the end of its lifetime. A negative value for the step number will emit a particle with a one in "value" chance. For example, a value of -3 will have a 1:3 chance of emitting a particle each step.

params.name: ind
params.description: The index of the particle type to change.

params.name: step_number
params.description: The quantity of the new particle to create per step.

params.name: step_type
params.description: The index of the particle type to create.

functions.name: vertex_argb

params.name: colour

functions.name: vertex_create_buffer
functions.description: This function creates a new vertex buffer. This is a special grow buffer created by GameMaker which is pre-formatted for use when building primitives (for use with shaders, for example).

functions.name: vertex_create_buffer_ext
functions.description: This function creates a new vertex buffer and sets its initial size in bytes.

params.name: size
params.description: The initial size of the buffer (in bytes).

functions.name: vertex_create_buffer_from_buffer
functions.description: As with the function vertex_create_buffer(), this function will create a new vertex buffer, only now the vertex data it stores is copied from the regular buffer that is specified as the source.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The buffer to create the vertex buffer from.

params.name: format
params.description: The primitive vertex format to use.

functions.name: vertex_create_buffer_from_buffer_ext
functions.description: As with the function vertex_create_buffer(), this function will create a new vertex buffer, only now the vertex data it stores is copied from the regular buffer that is specified as the source. Note that if the number of vertices does not match those being copied you may get corrupted vertex data.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The buffer to create the vertex buffer from.

params.name: format
params.description: The primitive vertex format to use.

params.name: src_offset
params.description: The offset within the the source buffer to copy from.

params.name: vert_num
params.description: The number of vertices the buffer should have.

functions.name: vertex_update_buffer_from_buffer
functions.description: This function updates contents of a vertex buffer using data from a regular buffer. The vertex buffer must not be frozen!

params.name: dest_vbuff
params.description: The vertex buffer to copy to.

params.name: dest_offset
params.description: The offset (in bytes) within the vertex buffer to copy to.

params.name: src_buffer
params.description: The buffer to copy data from.

params.name: src_offset
params.description: The offset (in bytes) within the buffer to copy from.

params.name: src_size
params.description: The size (in bytes) of data to be copied.

functions.name: vertex_update_buffer_from_vertex
functions.description: This function updates contents of a vertex buffer using contents of another vertex buffer. The vertex buffers must not be frozen!

params.name: dest_vbuff
params.description: The destination vertex buffer to copy to.

params.name: dest_vert
params.description: The index of the first vertex within the destination vertex buffer to copy to.

params.name: src_vbuff
params.description: The source vertex buffer to copy vertices from.

params.name: src_vert
params.description: The index of the first vertex to copy from the source vertex buffer.

params.name: src_vert_num
params.description: The number of vertices to copy.

functions.name: vertex_delete_buffer
functions.description: This function can be used to remove a previously created vertex buffer (see vertex_create_buffer()) from system memory.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The buffer to be removed.

functions.name: vertex_end
functions.description: With this function you end the building of the custom primitive.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The buffer to end writing to.

functions.name: vertex_float1
functions.description: This function will add a floating point value to the vertex data. The vertex must have been formatted correctly to accept this using the vertex_format_add_custom() function.

params.name: buffer

params.name: float
params.description: The input value.

functions.name: vertex_float2
functions.description: This function will add two floating point values to the vertex data. The vertex must have been formatted correctly to accept this using the vertex_format_add_custom() function.

params.name: buffer

params.name: float
params.description: The first input value.

params.name: float
params.description: The second input value.

functions.name: vertex_float3
functions.description: This function will add three floating point values to the vertex data. The vertex must have been formatted correctly to accept this using the vertex_format_add_custom() function.

params.name: float
params.description: The second input value.

params.description: The third input value.

functions.name: vertex_float4

params.name: buffer
params.description: The buffer to write the information to.

params.name: float

params.name: float
params.description: The second input value.

params.description: The third input value.

functions.name: vertex_format_add_colour
functions.description: Tell GameMaker to accept colour data as part of the new vertex format being created.

functions.name: vertex_format_add_custom
functions.description: This function permits you to use a custom data type for specific vertex format attributes as part of the new vertex format being created.

params.name: type

params.name: usage
params.description: The use that the data will get.

functions.name: vertex_format_add_normal
functions.description: Tell GameMaker to accept surface normal data (nx, ny and nz) as part of the new vertex format being created.

functions.name: vertex_format_add_position
functions.description: Tell GameMaker to accept 2D positional data (x and y) as part of the new vertex format being created.

functions.name: vertex_format_add_position_3d
functions.description: Tell GameMaker to accept 3D positional data (x, y and z) as part of the new vertex format being created.

functions.name: vertex_format_add_texcoord
functions.description: Tell GameMaker to accept texture position data (u and v) as part of the new vertex format being created.

functions.name: vertex_format_begin
functions.description: This function starts the definition of a new vertex format.

functions.name: vertex_format_delete
functions.description: This function deletes the given vertex format and must be called whenever you are finished using any created vertex formats.

functions.name: vertex_format_end
functions.description: This function ends the vertex format that was started with vertex_format_begin() and returns it.

functions.name: vertex_format_get_info
functions.description: This function is used to retrieve information for the given vertex format.

params.name: format_id
params.description: The vertex format for which information should be retrieved.

functions.name: vertex_format_exists
functions.description: This function will check whether the given vertex format exists in memory or not. If it does, the function will return true, otherwise it will return false.

functions.name: vertex_freeze
functions.description: This function can be used to "freeze" a vertex buffer. This buffer becomes read-only, meaning that if you need to change it, you would have to delete the whole buffer and re-create it. A frozen buffer can be submitted to the shader faster than a normal, dynamic buffer and is recommended for those effects that require an unchanging custom primitive for the duration of a level or the game.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The buffer to freeze.

functions.name: vertex_get_buffer_size
functions.description: This function gets the size of the given vertex buffer in bytes.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The buffer to get the size of.

functions.name: vertex_get_number
functions.description: This function returns the number of vertices defined in the given vertex buffer.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The vertex buffer to check.

functions.description: This function will add surface normal data to the vertex currently being defined for the custom primitive.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The buffer to write the information to.

params.name: nx
params.description: The x component of the surface normal.

params.name: ny
params.description: The y component of the surface normal.

params.name: nz

params.name: y

functions.name: vertex_position_3d

params.description: The buffer to write the information to.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position.

params.name: z
params.description: The z position.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The buffer to use.

params.name: primitive

params.name: texture
params.description: The texture to use (or -1 for no texture).

functions.name: vertex_submit_ext

params.name: primitive

params.name: texture

params.name: offset

params.name: number

params.name: byte

params.name: byte
params.description: The second input value.

params.name: byte
params.description: The third input value.

params.name: byte
params.description: The fourth input value.

functions.name: vertex_buffer_exists
functions.description: This function will check whether the given buffer exists in memory or not. If it does, the function will return true, otherwise it will return false.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The index of the buffer to check.

functions.name: draw_enable_swf_aa
functions.description: With this function you can enable or disable anti-aliasing (AA) for SWF format vector sprites.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable (true) or disable (false) AA for all SWF sprites.

functions.name: draw_get_swf_aa_level
functions.description: This function can be used to get the anti-aliasing (AA) level for SWF format vector sprites.

functions.name: draw_self
functions.description: This function draws the sprite assigned to the instance exactly as it would be drawn if the draw event held no code or actions, and will reflect and changes that have been made to the sprite variables in other events.

functions.name: draw_set_swf_aa_level
functions.description: This function can be used to set the anti-aliasing (AA) level for SWF format vector sprites. This can be a real value from 0 to 1 and will "smooth" the edges of these sprites. Note that to see this effect, you must first have enabled AA using the function draw_enable_swf_aa().

params.name: aa
params.description: The anti-aliasing value to use from 0 to 1.

functions.name: draw_enable_svg_aa
functions.description: With this function you can enable or disable anti-aliasing (AA) for SVG format vector sprites. AA simply smooths the edges of vector images to give them a nicer look. The amount of AA used will depend on the value set using the function draw_set_svg_aa_level(). By default this is disabled.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable (true) or disable (false) AA for all SVG sprites.

functions.name: draw_get_svg_aa_level
functions.description: This function can be used to get the anti-aliasing (AA) level for SVG format vector sprites. The return value will between 0 and 1 and shows how "smooth" the edges of these sprites will be drawn. You can set the AA level using the function draw_set_svg_aa_level().

functions.name: draw_set_svg_aa_level
functions.description: This function can be used to set the anti-aliasing (AA) level for SVG format vector sprites. This can be a real value from 0 to 1 and will "smooth" the edges of these sprites. Note that to see this effect, you must first have enabled AA using the function draw_enable_svg_aa().

params.name: aa
params.description: The anti-aliasing value to use from 0 to 1.

functions.name: vector_sprite_cache_limit
functions.description: This function can be used to set the maximum size of the cache used to accelerate the drawing of SWF and SVG format vector sprites. This can be a value of 0 or greater. A value of 0 will disable the cache. Changing this value will reset the return value of vector_sprite_get_cache_max_used().

params.name: limit
params.description: The cache size in bytes.

functions.name: vector_sprite_cache_prune_fraction
functions.description: This function sets what fraction of the SWF and SVG vector sprite cache is attempted to be cleared each frame. This can be a value between 0.0 and 1.0 (a value of 0.0 will disabled automatic pruning). This will only attempt to clear cache entries that are older than the number of frames specified by vector_sprite_cache_prune_age().

params.name: fraction
params.description: The fraction of the cache size to clear (a value between 0.0 and 1.0).

functions.name: vector_sprite_cache_prune_age
functions.description: This function sets how long entries in the SWF and SVG vector sprite cache must not have been used for before being deleted by the automatic pruning logic. This value is measured in frames and should be 0 or greater.

params.name: frames
params.description: The number of frames a cache entry can be unused for before being considered for deletion.

functions.name: vector_sprite_cache_get_limit
functions.description: This function returns the current maximum size of the SWF and SVG vector sprite cache.

functions.name: vector_sprite_cache_get_prune_fraction
functions.description: This function returns the fraction of the SWF and SVG vector sprite cache that is attempted to be cleared each frame.

functions.name: vector_sprite_cache_get_prune_age
functions.description: This function returns the number of frames an entry in the SWF and SVG vector sprite cache can exist without being used before it is considered for deletion.

functions.name: vector_sprite_cache_get_used
functions.description: This function returns the current amount of memory used by the SWF and SVG vector sprite cache.

functions.name: vector_sprite_cache_get_max_used
functions.description: This function returns the maximum amount of memory which has been used by the SWF and SVG vector sprite cache. This value is reset if the cache size is changed by vector_sprite_get_cache_limit().

functions.name: vector_sprite_cache_get_oldest_entry_age
functions.description: This function returns how long ago the oldest entry in the SWF and SVG vector sprite cache was last used. This can be useful for determining if the cache is set to an appropriate size.

functions.name: draw_sprite

params.description: The index of the sprite to draw.

params.name: subimg

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate of where to draw the sprite.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate of where to draw the sprite.

functions.name: draw_sprite_ext
functions.description: This function will draw the given sprite as in the function draw_sprite() but with additional options to change the scale, blending, rotation and alpha of the sprite being drawn.

params.name: sprite
params.description: The index of the sprite to draw.

params.name: subimg
params.description: The subimg (frame) of the sprite to draw (image_index or -1 correlate to the current frame of animation in the object).

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate of where to draw the sprite.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate of where to draw the sprite.

params.name: xscale
params.description: The horizontal scaling of the sprite, as a multiplier: 1 = normal scaling, 0.5 is half, etc.

params.name: yscale

params.name: rot
params.description: The rotation of the sprite. 0=right way up, 90=rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise, etc.

params.name: colour
params.description: The colour with which to blend the sprite. c_white is to display it normally.

params.name: alpha
params.description: The alpha of the sprite (from 0 to 1 where 0 is transparent and 1 opaque).

functions.signature: draw_sprite_ext(sprite, subimg, x, y, xscale, yscale, rot, colour, alpha)

functions.description: This function combines the function draw_sprite_ext() with the function draw_sprite_part(), adding in some additional blending options so that each corner of the final sprite part can be blended with an individual colour.

params.name: sprite
params.description: The index of the sprite to draw.

params.name: subimg
params.description: The subimg (frame) of the sprite to draw (image_index or -1 correlate to the current frame of animation in the object).

params.name: left
params.description: The x position on the sprite of the top left corner of the area to draw.

params.name: top
params.description: The y position on the sprite of the top left corner of the area to draw.

params.name: width
params.description: The width of the area to draw.

params.name: height
params.description: The height of the area to draw.

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate of where to draw the sprite.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate of where to draw the sprite.

params.name: xscale
params.description: The horizontal scaling of the sprite, as a multiplier: 1 = normal scaling, 0.5 is half, etc.

params.name: yscale
params.description: The vertical scaling of the sprite, as a multiplier: 1 = normal scaling, 0.5 is half, etc.

params.name: rot
params.description: The rotation of the sprite. 0=normal, 90=turned 90 degrees counter-clockwise, etc.

params.name: c1

functions.description: With this function you can draw part of any sprite at a given position within the room.

params.name: subimg
params.description: The subimg (frame) of the sprite to draw (image_index or -1 correlate to the current frame of animation in the object).

params.name: left
params.description: The x position on the sprite of the top left corner of the area to draw.

params.name: top
params.description: The y position on the sprite of the top left corner of the area to draw.
