functions.description: With this function you can delete a whole section of an ini file, which will also remove all key-value pairs that are associated with it.

params.name: section
params.description: The section to delete.

functions.name: ini_section_exists
functions.description: This function checks to see if a section exists in the currently open ini and will return true if it does or false otherwise.

params.name: section
params.description: The section in the open .ini file to check for.

functions.name: ini_write_real
functions.description: You can use this function to write a value (numeric) to an ini data file.

params.name: section
params.description: The section of the .ini to write to.

params.name: key
params.description: The key within the relevant section of the .ini to write to.

params.name: value
params.description: The real value to write to the relevant destination.

functions.name: ini_write_string
functions.description: You can use this function to write a string (text) to an ini data file.

params.name: section
params.description: The section of the .ini to write to.

params.name: key
params.description: The key within the relevant section of the .ini to write to.

params.name: value
params.description: The string to write to the relevant destination.

functions.name: file_text_close
functions.description: Once you have finished working with a given file (whether reading from it or writing to it), you must close the file again using this function, or else you risk losing the information contained within.

params.name: fileid
params.description: The id of the file to close.

functions.name: file_text_eof
functions.description: This function returns true when the end of a given opened text file has been reached or false if not.

params.name: fileid
params.description: The id of the file to check.

functions.name: file_text_eoln
functions.description: With this function you can get GameMaker to check the currently opened file to see if the line being read has finished.

params.name: fileid
params.description: The id of the file to check.

functions.name: file_text_open_append
functions.description: This function opens the text file with the indicated filename for writing (if the file does not exist, it is created), returning the unique id of the file that which should be stored in a variable as it will be used for all further actions to do with that file.

params.name: fname
params.description: The name of the file to append to.

functions.name: file_text_open_from_string
functions.description: This function will create a text file from a string and open it for reading, returning the file "handle" that should be used in all further file function calls to read from this file.

params.name: string
params.description: The string to create the file from.

functions.name: file_text_open_read
functions.description: This function opens the text file with the indicated filename for reading only, returning the unique id of the file that which should be stored in a variable as it will be used for all further actions to do with that file. If the file does not exists then the function will return the value -1.

params.name: fname
params.description: The name of the file to read from.

functions.name: file_text_open_write
functions.description: This function opens the text file with the indicated filename for writing only (if the file does not exist, it is created), returning the unique id of the file that which should be stored in a variable as it will be used for all further actions to do with that file. Note that if the file can't be created (because of an illegal filename, for example) the function will return -1.

params.name: fname
params.description: The name of the file to write to.

functions.name: file_text_readln
functions.description: With this function you can skip the remainder of the current line from a given opened text file and move to the start of the next one. The function will also return the full line as a string, making it an easy way to read complete "chunks" of data for parsing later.

params.name: fileid
params.description: The id of the file to read from.

functions.name: file_text_read_real
functions.description: With this function you can read a real number value from a text file and the function returns that value to be used or stored in a variable.

params.name: fileid
params.description: The id of the file to read from.

functions.name: file_text_read_string
functions.description: With this function you can read a string from a text file and the function returns that value to be used or stored in a variable.

params.name: fileid
params.description: The id of the file to read from.

functions.name: file_text_writeln
functions.description: With this function you can write a new line to an opened text file. In this way you can skip lines or write information on a line by line basis.

params.name: fileid
params.description: The id of the file to edit.

functions.name: file_text_write_real
functions.description: With this function you can write a number to the previously opened text file. Note that as the value to be written can be a real number, all decimals will be written with a "." point as separator.

params.name: fileid
params.description: The id of the file to edit.

params.name: val
params.description: The real value to write to the file.

functions.name: file_text_write_string
functions.description: With this function you can write a string to a previously opened text file.

params.name: fileid
params.description: The id of the file to edit.

params.name: str
params.description: The string to write to the file.

functions.name: device_get_tilt_x
functions.description: This function returns a value between -1 and 1 depending upon the angle of "tilt" of the device. The actual correlation between degrees of tilt and the value returned depends on the device and OS that it uses, but generally a value of 1 or -1 is the same as +/-90°.

functions.name: device_get_tilt_y
functions.description: This function returns a value between -1 and 1 depending upon the angle of "tilt" of the device. The actual correlation between degrees of tilt and the value returned depends on the device and OS that it uses, but generally a value of 1 or -1 is the same as +/-90°.

functions.name: device_get_tilt_z
functions.description: This function returns a value between -1 and 1 depending upon the angle of "tilt" of the device. The actual correlation between degrees of tilt and the value returned depends on the device and OS that it uses, but generally a value of 1 or -1 is the same as +/-90°.

functions.name: device_is_keypad_open
functions.description: This does a check of the device for a keypad and if one is available it returns true, otherwise it returns false. Please note that this function is mainly for use with Android devices

functions.name: device_mouse_check_button
functions.description: This function returns true or false depending on whether the given mouse button is being held down on the given device.

params.name: device
params.description: The device (from 0 - n) that is being checked

params.name: button
params.description: The button of the device that is being checked.

functions.name: device_mouse_check_button_pressed
functions.description: This function returns true or false depending on whether the device that you specify has been "touched" (clicked) or not.

params.name: device
params.description: The device (from 0 - n) that is being checked.

params.name: button
params.description: The button of the device that is being checked.

functions.name: device_mouse_check_button_released
functions.description: This function returns true or false depending on whether the device touch that you specify has been released or not.

params.name: device
params.description: The device (from 0 - n) that is being checked.

params.name: button
params.description: The button of the device that is being checked.

functions.name: device_mouse_dbclick_enable
functions.description: This function can be used to set the device to detect a double tap of the mb_left (left mouse button) as an mb_right (right mouse button) tap or not. By default this is set to true, meaning that every time the user taps the device screen twice quickly and consecutively, the return value is the same as if the right mouse button had been clicked. When this is on, the first tap will be detected as mb_left, and the second as mb_right, so make sure that any code you use takes this into account.

params.name: bool
params.description: Set double-click detection on (true) or off (false).

functions.name: device_mouse_raw_x
functions.description: This function returns the raw x position of a touch on the device. What this means is that it returns the actual device definition of the x position that is being touched, not the GameMaker one, and as such will ignore things like view position and scaling. Note that the maximum number of touches that can be detected will depend very much on the device being used and the OS it runs.

params.name: device
params.description: The device (from 0 - n) that is being checked.

functions.name: device_mouse_raw_y
functions.description: This function returns raw y position of the touch on a device. What this means is that it returns the actual device definition of the y position that is being touched, not the GameMaker one, and as such will ignore things like view position and scaling. Note that the maximum number of device touches that can be detected will depend very much on the device being used and the OS it runs.

params.name: device
params.description: The device (from 0 - n) that is being checked.

functions.name: device_mouse_x
functions.description: This function returns the x position of a touch on the device. If you are running this on a the HTML5 or PC and Mac modules then this value is updated constantly, as long as the device (usually a mouse) is plugged in, however for mobile devices, this will only be updated while the screen is being touched.

params.name: device
params.description: The device (from 0 - n) that is being checked.

functions.name: device_mouse_x_to_gui
functions.description: This function returns the x position of the touch on the device in relation to the GUI layer. If you are running this on a the HTML5 or PC and Mac modules then this value is updated constantly, as long as the device (usually a mouse) is plugged in, however for mobile devices, this will only be updated while the screen is being touched. Note that the maximum number of touches that can be detected will depend very much on the device being used and the OS it runs. Also note that on HTML5 only "device 0" will function correctly and other devices may give wrong values.

params.name: device
params.description: The device (from 0 - n) that is being checked.

functions.name: device_mouse_y
functions.description: This function returns the y position of a touch on the device. If you are running this on a the HTML5 or PC and Mac modules then this value is updated constantly, as long as the device (usually a mouse) is plugged in, however for mobile devices, this will only be updated while the screen is being touched. Note that the maximum number of touches that can be detected will depend very much on the device being used and the OS it runs. Also note that on HTML5 only "device 0" will function correctly and other devices may give wrong values.

params.name: device
params.description: The device (from 0 - n) that is being checked.

functions.name: device_mouse_y_to_gui
functions.description: This function returns the y position of the touch on the device in relation to the GUI layer.

params.name: device
params.description: The device (from 0 - n) that is being checked.

functions.name: gamepad_axis_count
functions.description: This function will return the number of "axis" controls on the device being checked. These controls are the analogue direction "thumbsticks" on most controllers.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

functions.name: gamepad_enumerate
functions.description: Currently only functional on Android, this function will enumerate gamepads to detect any newly added gamepads and remove any recently removed ones without the need for BLUETOOTH_CONNECT permission.

functions.name: gamepad_axis_value
functions.description: You can use this function to get the value of the different axes from a given gamepad slot. The returned value will be between -1 and 1 for each of the available horizontal and vertical axes.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

params.name: axisindex
params.description: The axis index to check.

functions.name: gamepad_button_check
functions.description: This function will return true or false depending on whether the given gamepad button is detected as being held down or not.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

params.name: button
params.description: Which gamepad button constant to check for.

functions.name: gamepad_button_check_pressed
functions.description: This function will return true or false depending on whether the given gamepad button is detected as having been pressed or not.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

params.name: button
params.description: Which gamepad button constant to check for.

functions.name: gamepad_button_check_released
functions.description: This function will return true or false depending on whether the given gamepad button is detected as having been released or not.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

params.name: button
params.description: Which gamepad button constant to check for.

functions.name: gamepad_button_count
functions.description: This function will return the total number of buttons available for the gamepad connected to the given device "slot".

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

functions.name: gamepad_button_value
functions.description: With this function you can get the current value of an analogue button, from 0 to 1, where 0 is no pressure and 1 is full pressure.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

params.name: button
params.description: Which gamepad button constant to check for.

functions.name: gamepad_get_axis_deadzone
functions.description: This function can be used to get the "dead zone" value of the joystick axis. The function will return a value between 0 to 1, where value reflects the threshold under which the joystick axis is considered to be at 0.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

functions.name: gamepad_get_button_threshold
functions.description: This function can be used to detect the current threshold setting of the analogue buttons for a given device. The default threshold for all analogue buttons is 0.5, with the range being from 0 to 1. The threshold defines at what point the button is considered as being "pressed" for games that require them to act as a digital button.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

functions.name: gamepad_get_description
functions.description: This function will return a string with the description of the given gamepad. This string is hardware dependent and the returned value will depend on the gamepad plugged into the device "slot" that is being checked.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad "slot" to get the name of.

functions.name: gamepad_get_device_count
functions.description: This function will tell you one of two things; either the number of game pads connected, or the number of available "slots" for game pads to be connected to.

functions.name: gamepad_get_guid
functions.description: With this function you can retrieve the GUID for the gamepad connected to the given slot index.

params.name: index
params.description: Which gamepad "slot" index to check

functions.name: gamepad_get_mapping
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the mapping string for the gamepad.

params.name: index
params.description: Which gamepad index "slot" to get the mapping from.

functions.name: gamepad_get_option
functions.description: This function can be used to retrieve the given option value. The available option string will depend on the platform that the project is being run on.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

params.name: option_name
params.description: The name of the option to get the value from

functions.name: gamepad_hat_count
functions.description: This function will return the total number of hats available for the gamepad connected to the given device "slot". Hats generally refer to up/down/left/right buttons. Note that on the Windows target, hats are only available on DirectInput controllers (so, from slot 4 upwards).

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

functions.name: gamepad_hat_value
functions.description: With this function you can get the current value of a gamepad "hat".

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

params.name: hatindex
params.description: Which gamepad hat (or hats) to check for.

functions.name: gamepad_is_connected
functions.description: This function will return whether a gamepad is connected to the given "slot" (returns true) or not (returns false). Note that there may be a slight delay between the user connecting the gamepad and GameMaker detecting it as being connected (this is especially the case when dealing with Bluetooth connected controllers).

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad "slot" to check.

functions.name: gamepad_is_supported
functions.description: With this function you can find out whether the target platform supports game pads (returns true) or not (returns false).

functions.name: gamepad_remove_mapping
functions.description: This function can be used to remove the current device mapping from the given gamepad slot index. Once called, the slot index will need to be remapped using the gamepad_test_mapping() function if you want to be able to be able to use the gamepad constants to detect input correctly (direct input can always be retrieved using the gamepad_axis/button/hat_count() and gamepad_axis/button/hat_value() functions together).

params.name: index
params.description: Which gamepad index "slot" to remove the mapping from.

functions.name: gamepad_set_axis_deadzone
functions.description: This function can be used to set the "dead zone" of the joystick axis. You specify the device slot to set, and then set a value from 0 to 1 and if the input amount is lower than the given value, the joystick axis is considered to be at 0. Note that this is a global setting that will affect all axes of all joysticks connected to the device slot specified.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

params.name: deadzone
params.description: The dead zone value from 0 to 1.

functions.name: gamepad_set_button_threshold
functions.description: This function can be used to set the current threshold setting of the analogue buttons for a given device. The default threshold for all analogue buttons is 0.5, with the range being from 0 to 1. The threshold defines at what point the button is considered as being "pressed" for games that require them to act as a digital button. Note that this function will affect the check, pressed and released states for analogue buttons, but will not affect the value returned by the function gamepad_button_check(), which will always return the raw value for the button.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

params.name: threshold
params.description: The new threshold value (from 0 - 1, default 0.5).

functions.name: gamepad_set_colour
functions.description: This function can be used to set the colour of the LEDs within a PlayStation controller. You specify the device slot to set, and then give a colour, which can be any of the colour constants, a colour value created using the specific colour functions or a HEX value(like $FFFFFFF).

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to set.

params.name: colour
params.description: The colour to use.

functions.name: gamepad_set_option
functions.description: This function can be used to set any of the available gamepad options. The available option string will depend on the platform that the project is being run on.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to set.

params.name: option_name
params.description: The name of the option to set

params.name: value
params.description: The value to set the option to (can be boolean, real, integer or string)

functions.name: gamepad_set_vibration
functions.description: With this function you can set the vibration of the gamepad motors, with either motor using a value from 0 (no vibration) to 1 (full vibration). Note that there is no time limit on this function, so you will need to use a variable or an alarm to switch off the vibration (set motors to 0) after a given time has passed, otherwise the gamepad will continue to vibrate indefinitely.

params.name: device
params.description: Which gamepad device "slot" to check.

params.name: left_motor
params.description: The amount of vibration from the left motor from 0 to 1.

params.name: right_motor
params.description: The amount of vibration from the right motor from 0 to 1.

functions.name: gamepad_test_mapping
functions.description: This function can be used to set the gamepad mapping on those targets that permit it.

params.name: index
params.description: Which gamepad index "slot" to set.

params.name: value
params.description: The map string to use.

functions.name: gesture_double_tap_distance
functions.description: This function is used to set the distance within which you have to touch/click the screen again after a single tap in order to trigger a Double Tap Gesture. The distance is measured in inches and has a default value of 0.1.

params.name: distance
params.description: The distance (in inches) to set for double tap gesture event detection.

functions.name: gesture_double_tap_time
functions.description: This function is used to set the time it takes between two touches/clicks to trigger a Double Tap Gesture event. The time is measured in seconds and has a default value of 0.16.

params.name: time
params.description: The time (in seconds) to set for double tap gesture event detection.

functions.name: gesture_drag_distance
functions.description: This function is used to set the distance it takes for a Dragging Gesture event to be triggered by the movement of a touch or click. The distance is measured in inches and has a default value of 0.1.

params.name: distance
params.description: The distance (in inches) to set for drag gesture event detection.

functions.name: gesture_drag_time
functions.description: This function is used to set the time it takes for a Drag Gesture event to be triggered by a touch or click. This time will also affect how the Tap Event is triggered as a touch/click and release before this time is up will be considered a Tap. The time is measured in seconds and has a default value of 0.16.

params.name: time
params.description: The time (in seconds) to set for drag gesture event detection.

functions.name: gesture_flick_speed
functions.description: This function is used to set the speed required for a Flick Gesture event to be triggered when a touch or click is released. The speed is measured in inches per second and has a default value of 2.0.

params.name: speed
params.description: The speed (in inches per second) to set for flick gesture event detection.

functions.name: gesture_get_double_tap_distance
functions.description: This function is used to get the distance within which you have to touch/click the screen again after a single tap in order to trigger a Double Tap Gesture. The distance is measured in inches and has a default value of 0.1.

functions.name: gesture_get_double_tap_time
functions.description: This function is used to get the time it takes between two touches/clicks to trigger a Double Tap Gesture event. The time is measured in seconds and has a default value of 0.16.

functions.name: gesture_get_drag_distance
functions.description: This function is used to get the distance it takes for a Dragging Gesture event to be triggered by the movement of a touch or click. The distance is measured in inches and has a default value of 0.1.

functions.name: gesture_get_drag_time
functions.description: This function is used to get the time it takes for a Drag Start Gesture event to be triggered by a touch or click. This time will also affect how the Tap Event is triggered as a touch/click and release before this time is up will be considered a Tap. The time is measured in seconds and has a default value of 0.16.

functions.name: gesture_get_flick_speed
functions.description: This function is used to get the speed required for a Flick Gesture event to be triggered when a touch or click is released. The speed is measured in inches per second and has a default value of 2.0.

functions.name: gesture_get_pinch_angle_away
functions.description: This function is used to get the angle within which a touch must be moving away from another touch before a Pinch Out Gesture may potentially be started. The angle is measured in degrees and has a default value of 45°.

functions.name: gesture_get_pinch_angle_towards
functions.description: This function is used to get the angle within which a touch must be moving towards another touch before a Pinch In Gesture may potentially be started. The angle is measured in degrees and has a default value of 45°.

functions.name: gesture_get_pinch_distance
functions.description: This function is used to get the distance within which you have to touch/click the screen and move with two fingers before you trigger a Pinch Gesture. The distance is measured in inches and has a default value of 0.1.

functions.name: gesture_get_rotate_time
functions.description: This function is used to get the angle which a pair of touches must exceed in order to trigger a Rotate Start Gesture. The angle is measured in degrees and has a default value of 5°.

functions.name: gesture_get_tap_count
functions.description: This function is used to check whether tap counting is enabled or disabled. You can enable or disable tap counting using the function gesture_tap_count().

functions.name: gesture_pinch_angle_away
functions.description: This function is used to set the angle within which a touch must be moving away from another touch before a Pinch Out Gesture may potentially be started. The angle is measured in degrees and has a default value of 45°.

functions.name: gesture_pinch_angle_towards
functions.description: This function is used to set the angle within which a touch must be moving towards another touch before a Pinch In Gesture may potentially be started. The angle is measured in degrees and has a default value of 45°.

functions.name: gesture_pinch_distance
functions.description: This function is used to set the distance within which you have to touch/click the screen and move with two fingers before you trigger a Pinch Gesture. The distance is measured in inches and has a default value of 0.1.

functions.name: gesture_rotate_angle
functions.description: This function is used to set the angle which a pair of touches must exceed in order to trigger a Rotate Start Gesture. The angle is measured in degrees and has a default value of 5°.

functions.name: gesture_rotate_time
functions.description: This function is used to set the time within which a pair of touches must be rotating in a consistent direction for a Rotate Start Gesture to be triggered. The time is measured in seconds and has a default value of 0.16s.

functions.name: gesture_tap_count
functions.description: This function is used to set whether tap counting is enabled or disabled. When set to true tap counting is enabled, and when set to false it is disabled, although you can check which state it is in using the function gesture_get_tap_count(). Note that this is enabled by default.

params.name: enable
params.description: Enable (set to true) or disable (set to false) tap counting.

functions.name: io_clear
functions.description: This function will clear the current keyboard and mouse states.

functions.name: keyboard_check
functions.description: With this function you can check to see if a key is held down or not. Unlike the keyboard_check_pressed() or keyboard_check_released() functions which are only triggered once when the key is pressed or released, this function is triggered every step that the key is held down for.

params.name: key
params.description: The key to check the down state of.

functions.name: keyboard_check_direct
functions.description: This function will return true if the key with the particular keycode is pressed, or false if it is not, by checking the hardware directly.

params.name: key
params.description: The key to check the down state of.

functions.name: keyboard_check_pressed
functions.description: With this function you can check to see if a key has been pressed or not. Unlike the keyboard_check() function, this function will only run once for every time the key is pressed down, so for it to trigger again, the key must be first released and then pressed again.

params.name: key
params.description: The key to check the pressed state of.

functions.name: keyboard_check_released
functions.description: With this function you can check to see if a key has been released or not. Unlike the keyboard_check() function, this function will only run once for every time the key is lifted, so for it to trigger again, the key must be first pressed and then released again.

params.name: key
params.description: The key to check the released state of.

functions.name: keyboard_clear
functions.description: With this function you can clear the current keyboard state, which essentially means that if the key is being held down, it will no longer be recognised until it is released again (which won't trigger the Keyboard Key Released event either on this occasion) and pressed again.

params.name: key
params.description: The key to clear.

functions.name: keyboard_get_map
functions.description: Sometimes you may wish to get the ASCII code for a mapped key (to see if it is already mapped, for example) which is what this function returns.

params.name: key
params.description: This is the key that you wish to get the mapped value from

functions.name: keyboard_get_numlock
functions.description: You can use this function to find the status of the keypad number lock with true being returned for on, and false returned for off.

functions.name: keyboard_key_press
functions.description: With this function you can simulate the press of any key on the keyboard.

params.name: key
params.description: The key to simulate a press of.

functions.name: keyboard_key_release
functions.description: With this function you can simulate the release of any key on the keyboard.

params.name: key
params.description: The key to simulate a release of.

functions.name: keyboard_set_map
functions.description: This function maps a keyboard key to another one using the keycode value so that any input from either key will be interpreted as the same.

params.name: key1
params.description: This is the key that key2 is to be mapped to

params.name: key2
params.description: This is the key that is to be mapped

functions.name: keyboard_set_numlock
functions.description: You can use this function to switch the keypad number-lock on or off (set to true for on, and false for off).

params.name: value
params.description: Set this to true for "on" and false for "off"

functions.name: keyboard_unset_map
functions.description: With this function you can clear all re-mapped keys so that they return to their default state, i.e.: all keys to map to themselves.

functions.name: mouse_check_button
functions.description: This function will return true if the mouse button being checked is held down or false if it is not.

params.name: numb
params.description: Which mouse button constant to check for.

functions.name: mouse_check_button_pressed
functions.description: This function will return true if the mouse button being checked has been pressed or false if it has not. This function will only be triggered once for any mouse button when it is first pressed and to trigger it again the button will need to have been released and pressed again. Note that it will be considered triggered for the duration of the step, and for all instances that have any mouse events or that use this same function.

params.name: numb
params.description: Which mouse button constant to check for.

functions.name: mouse_check_button_released
functions.description: This function will return true if the mouse button being checked has been released or false if it has not. This function will only be triggered once for any mouse button when it is released and to trigger it again the button will need to have been pressed and released again.

params.name: numb
params.description: Which mouse button constant to check for.

functions.name: mouse_clear
functions.description: This function will clear the current state of the given mouse button. This means that checks for it being held down will not return true until the player releases the button and presses it again (but the release state will still be detected if the clear is done while the mouse button is being held down).

params.name: button
params.description: Which mouse button constant to check for.

functions.name: mouse_wheel_down
functions.description: This function returns true if the mouse wheel is being rotated downwards and false otherwise.

functions.name: mouse_wheel_up
functions.description: This function returns true if the mouse wheel is being rotated upwards and false otherwise.

functions.name: keyboard_virtual_height
functions.description: This function will return the current height in pixels of the virtual keyboard, based on the size of the display. If the keyboard is not visible, 0 will be returned.

functions.name: keyboard_virtual_hide
functions.description: This function can be used to hide the virtual keyboard on the device running the game. Calling this function will generate a System Asynchronous Event.

functions.name: keyboard_virtual_show
functions.description: This function can be used to show the virtual keyboard on the device running the game.

params.name: keyboard_type
params.description: Determines the keyset available on the virtual keyboard.

params.name: return_key_type
params.description: Determines what is shown on the return/action key of the virtual keyboard.

params.name: autocapitalization_type
params.description: Determines how/if the words typed via the virtual keyboard will be autocapitalized.

params.name: predictive_text_enabled
params.description: Set to true/false to enable/disable predictive text input.

functions.name: keyboard_virtual_status
functions.description: This function can be used to get the status of the virtual keyboard on the device running the game. The function will return true if the OS virtual keyboard is visible/being shown or false if it is hidden/hiding.

functions.name: keyboard_virtual_set_position
functions.description: This Windows only function can be used to set the position of the virtual keyboard on the device running the game. The coordinates passed in are in display coordinates (use application_get_position() to find the game's position in this space).

params.name: x
params.description: x coordinate of the requested position.

params.name: y
params.description: y coordinate of the requested position.

functions.name: virtual_key_add
functions.description: This function adds a virtual key that covers a portion of the screen area, mapping "touches" of this area to a keyboard key.

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate (left side) of the virtual key on the screen

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate (top side) of the virtual key on the screen

params.name: w
params.description: The width of the virtual key

params.name: h
params.description: The height of the virtual key

params.name: keycode
params.description: Which keyboard key event should be triggered by touching this area

functions.name: virtual_key_delete
functions.description: This function deletes a previously added virtual key.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the virtual key to delete.

functions.name: virtual_key_hide
functions.description: This function hides the coloured rectangle that's drawn to represent the given virtual key on the screen.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the virtual key to hide.

functions.name: virtual_key_show
functions.description: This function draws a coloured rectangle to represent the given virtual key on the screen.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the virtual key to show.

functions.name: gc_collect
functions.description: With this function you can trigger the garbage collector, forcing it to run at the end of the current frame (step). It is worth noting that the garbage collector does not need to be active for this to work.

functions.name: gc_enable
functions.description: With this function you can enable or disable the garbage collector. Calling the function with true as the argument enables it and using false disables it (not recommended). It is enabled by default.

params.name: enable
params.description: enable (true) or disable (false) the garbage collector.

functions.name: gc_get_stats
functions.description: With this function you can retrieve information about the current state of the garbage collector.

functions.name: gc_get_target_frame_time
functions.description: With this function you can retrieve the current target frame value for the garbage collector. The value returned is in microseconds (where 1,000,000 microseconds equals one second) and the default target frame time is 100 microseconds. If you wish to change this value then you should use the function gc_target_frame_time().

functions.name: gc_is_enabled
functions.description: With this function you can check to see if the garbage collector is enabled or not.

functions.name: gc_target_frame_time
functions.description: With this function you can indicate to the garbage collector that it should aim to spend no more than the time specified running each frame. The function takes a time value specified in microseconds (where 1,000,000 microseconds equals one second) and the default target frame time is 100 microseconds.

params.name: time
params.description: The target time - in microseconds - that the garbage collector should work each frame

functions.name: weak_ref_create
functions.description: With this function you can check the weak reference to a struct to see if it is still "alive" or not. Note that if you supply a value that is not a weak reference, the function will return undefined.

params.name: struct_to_track
params.description: The struct that you want to create a weak reference for

functions.name: weak_ref_any_alive
functions.description: With this function you can check the weak reference to various structs to see if it they are still "alive" or not. Note that if you supply an array where any of the values are not a weak references, the function will return undefined.

params.name: weak_ref
params.description: The weak reference to the struct you want to check.

params.name: index
params.description: OPTIONAL! The index into the array to start checking from

params.name: length
params.description: OPTIONAL! The number of positions from the given index to check

functions.name: game_end
functions.description: With this function you can end the game (and the Game End Event will be triggered). This will not happen instantaneously, but rather at the end of the current step, so any code you have in the same step after this function has been called will still run.

params.name: return_code
params.description: The return code of the application, will default to 0.

functions.name: game_get_speed
functions.description: This function can be used to get the game speed as either the number of game frames to run per second or as the number of microseconds per game frame. Note that this is not the actual running speed FPS value (for that use the fps_real variable) but rather the number of game frames (FPS) that the game will attempt to maintain each second, or the length of each game frame in microseconds that the game will try to maintain (MPF).

params.name: type
params.description: The type of method used to get the game speed.

functions.name: game_load
functions.description: This is a legacy function that can be used to load a game that has been previously saved using game_save(). Note that it will restore the version of the game that was used to create the save, so any updates made after it will not be visible. For more info, read the page on game_save().

params.name: filename
params.description: The name of the file to load.

functions.name: game_load_buffer
functions.description: With this function you can load a game state that has been saved previously. The game is loaded from a previously created "grow" buffer and the buffer must have had a game state saved to it using game_save_buffer() function.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The buffer id to load from.

functions.name: game_restart
functions.description: With this function you can restart the game. This is essentially the same as running the game for the first time and so the Game Start Event will be triggered, as well as the Game End Event.

functions.name: game_save
functions.description: This is a legacy function that can be used to save the current state of the game, and is not recommended for use anymore. Use the File functions instead to create a custom save system where you only save and load specific game data.

params.name: filename
params.description: The name of the file to save the game to.

functions.name: game_save_buffer
functions.description: This is a variant of the game_save() function, so please read its page first as it contains important information related to its use and to this function's use as well.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The buffer id to save to.

functions.name: game_set_speed
functions.description: This function can be used to set the game speed. You can set this in one of two ways: as game frames per second (FPS) or as microseconds per game frame (MPF).

params.name: speed
params.description: The new game speed (as either FPS or MPF).

params.name: type
params.description: The type of method used to set the game speed.

functions.name: game_change
functions.description: This function allows you to close the currently running title and launch another title, it will only work in VM and on certain platforms it will only work in a package build and not in run/debug.

params.name: working_directory
params.description: The directory in which the new game will launch.

params.name: launch_parameters
params.description: Command line parameters to be passed to the new game.

functions.name: highscore_add
functions.description: With this function you can add a name and a score to the internal global high score list. There is no need to check the value to see if it is high enough to enter into the score list as GameMaker will only store those values that are greater than the tenth position stored.

params.name: str
params.description: The string (name) to attribute the score to

params.name: numb
params.description: The number (score) to add.

functions.name: highscore_value
functions.description: With this function you can retrieve the score value that has been stored in the high score list at the given position. If no score has been entered, the function will return 0.

params.name: place
params.description: The place on the table (1-10).

functions.name: highscore_name
functions.description: With this function you can retrieve the name string that has been stored in the high score list at the given position. If no name has been entered, the string "Unknown" will be returned.

params.name: place
params.description: The place on the table (1-10).

functions.name: angle_difference
functions.description: This function returns the smallest difference between the two specified angles, where the difference is calculated from the source angle towards the destination angle.

params.name: ang1
params.description: The destination or target angle (in degrees)

params.name: ang2
params.description: The source angle (in degrees)

functions.name: arccos
functions.description: This function returns the inverse cosine (in radians) of x, in that if cos(val)=n, arccos(n)=val, and the resulting number will be between 0 and pi.

params.name: x
params.description: The angle (in radians) to return the inverse cosine of.

functions.name: arcsin
functions.description: This function returns the inverse sine (in radians) of x, in that if sin(x)=n, arcsin(n)=x, and the resulting number will be between -pi/2 and pi/2.

params.name: x
params.description: The value to return the inverse sine of.

functions.name: arctan
functions.description: This function returns the inverse tangent (in radians) of x.

params.name: x
params.description: The angle (in radians) to return the inverse tangent of.

functions.name: arctan2
functions.description: This function returns the inverse tangent (in radians) of a value given as a ratio y/x, where y = opposite side of triangle and x = adjacent side of triangle. Unlike arctan(), the function arctan2() is valid for all angles and so may be used to convert a vector to an angle without risking division by zero, and it also returns a result in the correct quadrant.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate to calculate.

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate to calculate.

functions.name: cos
functions.description: This function returns the cosine of an angle in radians. In a right-angled triangle the cosine is defined as cos(val) = adjacent / hypotenuse, where val is one of the three angles.

params.name: val
params.description: The angle (in radians) to return the cosine of.

functions.name: darccos
functions.description: This function returns the inverse cosine (in degrees) of x, in that if dcos(val)=n, darccos(n)=val, and the resulting number will be between 0 and 180.

params.name: x
params.description: The value to return the inverse cosine of.

functions.name: darcsin
functions.description: This function returns the inverse sine (in degrees) of x, in that if dsin(x)=n, darcsin(n)=x, and the resulting number will be between -90 and 90.

params.name: val
params.description: The value to return the inverse sine of.

functions.name: darctan
functions.description: This function returns the inverse tangent (in degrees) of x. This will accept any number as, unlike dtan(), darctan() asymptotes are on the y axis so it just means you'll never get returned a number greater than 90 or less than -90.

params.name: val
params.description: The value to return the inverse tangent of.

functions.name: darctan2
functions.description: This function returns the inverse tangent (in degrees) of a value given as y/x, where y = Opposite side of triangle and x = Adjacent side of triangle. Unlike darctan(), the function darctan2() is valid for all angles and so may be used to convert a vector to an angle without risking division by zero, and it also returns a result in the correct quadrant.

params.name: y
params.description: The y coordinate to calculate.

params.name: x
params.description: The x coordinate to calculate.

functions.name: dcos
functions.description: This function returns the cosine of an angle in degrees. In a right-angled triangle the cosine is defined as cos(val) = adjacent / hypotenuse, where val is one of the three angles.

params.name: val
params.description: The angle (in degrees) to return the cosine of.

functions.name: degtorad
functions.description: This function converts an angle in degrees to an angle in radians. This function translates degrees into radians using the formula: angle_radians = angle_degrees * pi / 180;

params.name: deg
params.description: The degrees to convert.

functions.name: distance_to_object
functions.description: This function calculates the distance from the edge of the bounding box of the calling instance to the nearest edge of the nearest instance of the object specified.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object to check for.

functions.name: sphere_is_visible
functions.description: This function checks a sphere of radius r at position x,y,z against the current view frustum. Returns true if the sphere intersects or is contained in the view frustum and false if the sphere is completely outside the view frustum.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position to check.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position to check.

params.name: z
params.description: The z position to check.

params.name: r
params.description: The radius of the sphere to check.

functions.name: distance_to_point
functions.description: This function calculates the distance from the edge of the bounding box of the calling instance to the specified (x , y) position in the room, with the return value being in pixels.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position to check.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position to check.

functions.name: dot_product
functions.description: This function returns the dot product of two 2D vectors specified as (x1, y1) and (x2, y2).

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the first vector.

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the first vector.

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the second vector.

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the second vector.

functions.name: dot_product_3d
functions.description: This function returns the dot product of two 3D vectors specified as (x1, y1, z1) and (x2, y2, z2).

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the first vector.

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the first vector.

params.name: z1
params.description: The z coordinate of the first vector.

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the second vector.

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the second vector.

params.name: z2
params.description: The z coordinate of the second vector.

functions.signature: dot_product_3d(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2)

functions.name: dot_product_3d_normalised
functions.description: This function returns the normalised dot product of two 3D vectors, specified as (x1, y1, z1) and (x2, y2, z2).

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the first vector.

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the first vector.

params.name: z1
params.description: The z coordinate of the first vector.

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the second vector.

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the second vector.

params.name: z2
params.description: The z coordinate of the second vector.

functions.signature: dot_product_3d_normalised(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2)

functions.name: dot_product_normalised
functions.description: This function returns the normalised dot product of two 2D vectors specified as (x1, y1) and (x2, y2).

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the first vector.

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the first vector.

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the second vector.

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the second vector.

functions.name: dsin
functions.description: This function returns the sine of an angle in degrees. In a right-angled triangle the sine is defined as sin(val) = opposite / hypotenuse, where val is one of the three angles.

params.name: val
params.description: The angle (in degrees) to return the sine of.

functions.name: dtan
functions.description: This function returns the tangent of an angle in degrees. In a right-angled triangle the tangent is defined as tan(val) = opposite / adjacent, where val is one of the three angles.

params.name: val
params.description: The angle (in degrees) to return the tangent of.

functions.name: lengthdir_x
functions.description: This function is used to get the x component of a position "len" pixels from the starting point and in direction "dir".

params.name: len
params.description: The length away of the point to return.

params.name: dir
params.description: The direction of the point to return.

functions.name: lengthdir_y
functions.description: This function is used to get the y component of a position "len" pixels from the starting point and in direction "dir".

params.name: len
params.description: The length away of the point to return.

params.name: dir
params.description: The direction of the point to return.

functions.name: point_direction
functions.description: This function returns the direction of a vector formed by the specified components (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) in relation to the fixed x/y coordinates of the room.

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the first component of the vector

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the first component of the vector

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the second component of the vector

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the second component of the vector

functions.name: point_distance
functions.description: This function returns the length of a vector formed by the specified components (x1, y1) and (x2, y2).

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the first component of the vector

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the first component of the vector

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the second component of the vector

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the second component of the vector

functions.name: point_distance_3d
functions.description: This function returns the length of a vector formed by the specified components (x1, y1, z1) and (x2, y2, z2).

params.name: x1
params.description: The x coordinate of the first component of the vector

params.name: y1
params.description: The y coordinate of the first component of the vector

params.name: z1
params.description: The z coordinate of the first component of the vector

params.name: x2
params.description: The x coordinate of the second component of the vector

params.name: y2
params.description: The y coordinate of the second component of the vector

params.name: z2
params.description: The z coordinate of the second component of the vector

functions.signature: point_distance_3d(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2)

functions.name: radtodeg
functions.description: This function converts an angle in radians to an angle in degrees. The function translates radians into degrees using the formula: angle_degrees = angle_radians * 180 / pi;

params.name: rad
params.description: The radians to convert.

functions.name: sin
functions.description: This function returns the sine of an angle in radians. In a right-angled triangle the sine is defined as sin(val) = opposite / hypotenuse, where val is one of the three angles.

params.name: val
params.description: The angle (in radians) to return the sine of.

functions.name: tan
functions.description: This function returns the tangent of an angle in radians. In a right-angled triangle the tangent is defined as tan(val) = opposite / adjacent, where val is one of the three angles.

params.name: val
params.description: The angle (in radians) to return the tangent of.

functions.name: date_compare_date
functions.description: With this function you can check two dates to see which one is the earlier or later than the other. The function returns -1 if date1 is earlier, 0 if both dates are the same, and 1 if date1 is later.

params.name: date1
params.description: The first date.

params.name: date2
params.description: The date to compare it to.

functions.name: date_compare_datetime
functions.description: With this function you can check two dates and times to see which one is the earlier or later than the other. The function returns -1 if date1 is earlier, 1 if date1 is later and 0 if they are the same.

params.name: date1
params.description: The first datetime.

params.name: date2
params.description: The datetime to compare it to.

functions.name: date_compare_time
functions.description: With this function you can check two dates and times to see which one has the time component earlier or later than the other. The function returns -1 if datetime1 is earlier, 1 if datetime1 is later and 0 if they are the same, and it ignores the date, so literally just which of the times is further through its given day.

params.name: datetime1
params.description: The first datetime.

params.name: datetime2
params.description: The datetime to compare the first one to.

functions.name: date_create_datetime
functions.description: This function will create a datetime value from the components given as the arguments.

params.name: year
params.description: The year to set.

params.name: month
params.description: The month to set.

params.name: day
params.description: The day to set.

params.name: hour
params.description: The hour to set.

params.name: minute
params.description: The minute to set.

params.name: second
params.description: The second to set.

functions.signature: date_create_datetime(year, month, day, hour, minute, second)

functions.name: date_current_datetime
functions.description: Returns the date-time value of the current moment. The time returned is based on the default time zone for the system (i.e.: local time).

functions.name: date_datetime_string
functions.description: With this function you can create a string containing the given datetime, formatted for the system or device that is running the game when the function is called.

params.name: date
params.description: The date to use.

functions.name: date_date_of
functions.description: Returns the date value of the given datetime.

params.name: date
params.description: The datetime to extract the date from.

functions.name: date_date_string
functions.description: With this function you can create a string containing the given date, formatted as day/month/year.

params.name: date
params.description: The date to use.

functions.name: date_days_in_month
functions.description: With this function you can get the number of days that the given month has, either 28, 29, 30 or 31.

params.name: date
params.description: The date to use.

functions.name: date_days_in_year
functions.description: With this function you can get the number of days that the given year has, returning 365 for a normal year, and 366 for a leap year.

params.name: date
params.description: The date to use.

functions.name: date_day_span
functions.description: With this function you can get the number of days between two dates. This value is always positive, and incomplete days will be returned as a fraction.

params.name: date1
params.description: The first datetime.

params.name: date2
params.description: The datetime to compare it to.

functions.name: date_get_day
functions.description: This function returns the day (from 1 to 31) of the given datetime.

params.name: date
params.description: The date to check.

functions.name: date_get_day_of_year
functions.description: This function returns the day (from 1 to 366) within the year of the given datetime.

params.name: date
params.description: The date to check.

functions.name: date_get_hour
functions.description: This function returns the hour of the given datetime value.

params.name: date
params.description: The datetime to check.

functions.name: date_get_hour_of_year
functions.description: This function returns the hour of the given datetime value within the year (from the total number of hours for the year, taking into account leap years).

params.name: date
params.description: The datetime to check.

functions.name: date_get_minute
functions.description: This function returns the minute of the given datetime value.

params.name: date
params.description: The datetime to check.

functions.name: date_get_minute_of_year
functions.description: This function returns the minute of the given datetime value within the year (from the total number of minutes for the year, taking into account leap years).

params.name: date
params.description: The date to check.

functions.name: date_get_month
functions.description: This function returns the month of the given datetime value.

params.name: date
params.description: The datetime to check.

functions.name: date_get_second
functions.description: This function returns the second of the given datetime value.

params.name: date
params.description: The datetime to check.

functions.name: date_get_second_of_year
functions.description: This function returns the second of the given datetime value within the year (from the total number of seconds for the year, taking into account leap years).

params.name: date
params.description: The date to check.

functions.name: date_get_timezone
functions.description: This function gets the base time zone being used for all the rest of the date and time functions, which can be either local (as set by the system) or UTC.

functions.name: date_get_week
functions.description: This function returns the week of the given datetime value within the year.

params.name: date
params.description: The datetime to check.

functions.name: date_get_weekday
functions.description: This function returns the week day value of the given datetime. This will be a value from 0 to 6.

params.name: date
params.description: The date to check.

functions.name: date_get_year
functions.description: This function returns the year of the given datetime.

params.name: date
params.description: The datetime to check.

functions.name: date_hour_span
functions.description: With this function you can get the number of hours between two dates. This value is always positive, and incomplete hours will be returned as a fraction.

params.name: date1
params.description: The first datetime.

params.name: date2
params.description: The datetime to compare the first one to.

functions.name: date_inc_day
functions.description: With this function you can increment a given datetime value by a specific number of days, and it will return the new datetime value.

params.name: date
params.description: The datetime to add to.

params.name: amount
params.description: The number of days (must be an integer) to add.

functions.name: date_inc_hour
functions.description: With this function you can increment a given datetime value by a specific number of hours, and it will return the new datetime value.

params.name: date
params.description: The datetime to add to.

params.name: amount
params.description: The number of hours (must be an integer) to add.

functions.name: date_inc_minute
functions.description: With this function you can increment a given datetime value by a specific number of minutes, and it will return the new datetime value.

params.name: date
params.description: The datetime to add to.

params.name: amount
params.description: The number of minutes (must be an integer) to add.

functions.name: date_inc_month
functions.description: With this function you can increment a given datetime value by a specific number of months, and it will return the new datetime value.

params.name: date
params.description: The datetime to add to.

params.name: amount

functions.description: This function uses the instance collision mask (decided by the sprite properties or the mask index of the calling instance) to mark cells as forbidden or not in an MP grid, where forbidden cells cannot be crossed by any of the pathfinding functions. You can specify in the function whether to consider precise collisions or not and the forbidden cells marked will change depending on this setting.

params.name: speed
params.description: The added speed.

params.description: The new direction.

params.name: speed
params.description: The new speed.`

functions.name: move_bounce_all
functions.description: With this function you can command an instance to bounce off all instances within the room, with the only exception being those that have no sprite or mask index assigned to them. You can also tell it to use precise collision checking when enabled, but be aware that this requires all instances to have precise masks enabled and will greatly slow down your game when many instances are involved due to the amount of processing that has to be done.

params.name: adv
params.description: Whether to enable advanced bouncing (true) or not (false).

functions.name: move_bounce_solid
functions.description: With this function you can command an instance to bounce off only those instances marked as solid within the room. You can also tell it to use precise collision checking when enabled, but be aware that this requires all instances to have precise masks enabled and will greatly slow down your game when many instances are involved due to the amount of processing that has to be done.

params.name: adv
params.description: Whether to enable advanced bouncing (true) or not (false).

functions.name: move_contact_all
functions.description: This function will move the instance running the code a set number of pixels in the specified direction until it meets any other instance with a valid mask. You can use -1 or 0 for the maxdist being a default 1000px, i.e.: GameMaker will move the instance continually up 1000 pixels until it is out of collision.

params.name: dir
params.description: The direction to move in.

params.name: maxdist
params.description: The maximum distance the object can travel (-1 or 0 a default value of 1000 pixels).

functions.name: move_contact_solid
functions.description: This function will move the instance running the code a set number of pixels in the specified direction until it meets an instance with solid flagged as true. You can use -1 or 0 for the maxdist being a default 1000px, i.e.: GameMaker will move the instance continually up 1000 pixels until it is out of collision.

params.name: dir
params.description: The direction to move in.

params.name: maxdist
params.description: The maximum distance the object can travel (-1 or 0 a default value of 1000 pixels).

functions.name: move_outside_all
functions.description: With this function you can tell an instance to move out of a collision in any direction and any number of pixels each step, with a value of -1 or 0 for the maxdist being a default 1000px, i.e.: GameMaker will move the instance continually up 1000 pixels until it is out of collision.

params.name: dir
params.description: The direction to move in.

params.name: maxdist
params.description: The maximum distance the object can travel (-1 or 0 a default value of 1000 pixels).

functions.name: move_and_collide
functions.description: With this function you can tell an instance to move in a direction, resolving collisions on the way and specify a direction in which the instance will attempt to move to get past obstacles, thus allowing traversal of slopes or small steps. Returns an array of instances that it has collided with.

params.name: dx
params.description: The x component of direction to move in.

params.name: dy
params.description: The y component of direction to move in.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object to check for collisions with.

params.name: num_iterations
params.description: The number of steps the motion will be broken down into to resolve collisions, defaults to 4

params.name: xoff
params.description: The x component of direction to move to attempt to avoid obstacles. If not specified the perpendicular to the direction of movement is used.

params.name: yoff
params.description: The y component of direction to move to attempt to avoid obstacles. If not specified the perpendicular to the direction of movement is used.

params.name: max_x_distance
params.description: The maximum distance in the x direction the instance will move. If less than or equal to 0 no clamping is performed.

params.name: max_y_distance
params.description: The maximum distance in the y direction the instance will move. If less than or equal to 0 no clamping is performed.

functions.name: move_outside_solid
functions.description: With this function you can tell an instance to move out of a collision with any instance flagged as solid in any direction and any number of pixels each step, with a value of -1 or 0 for the maxdist being a default 1000px, i.e.: GameMaker will move the instance continually up 1000 pixels until it is out of collision.

params.name: dir
params.description: The direction to move in.

params.name: maxdist
params.description: The maximum distance the object can travel (-1 or 0 a default value of 1000 pixels).

functions.name: move_random
functions.description: With this function you can set the instance to a position anywhere in the room, but aligned to an "invisible" grid. So a value of 32 for the hsnap and vsnap will set the instance to a random position that is aligned to a grid of 32x32 squares (you can set these values to 1 to get a position anywhere in the room).

params.name: hsnap
params.description: The horizontal snapping (the size in pixels between "cells").

params.name: vsnap
params.description: The vertical snapping (the size in pixels between "cells").

params.name: hsnap
params.description: The horizontal snapping (the size in pixels between "cells").

params.name: vsnap
params.description: The vertical snapping (the size in pixels between "cells").

params.name: y
params.description: The y position of the point to move towards.

params.name: sp
params.description: The speed to move at in pixels per step.

functions.name: move_wrap
functions.description: This function will automatically "wrap" an instance that has left the room on either the horizontal or vertical (or both) axis. You can specify a margin outside the edges of the room for this to occur, and when the instance has travelled outside of that margin GameMaker will automatically wrap it back into the room at the other side.

params.name: hor
params.description: Whether to wrap horizontally (true) or not (false).

params.name: vert
params.description: Whether to wrap vertically (true) or not (false).

params.name: margin
params.description: How far outside the room, in pixels, the object must be to initiate wrapping.

params.name: vsnap

functions.name: network_connect
functions.description: With this function you can send a request to connect to a server. The function takes the socket id to connect through and requires you to give the IP address to connect to as well as the port to connect through, and if the connection fails a value of less than 0 will be returned. This connection uses a special protocol that ensures only GameMaker games connect to each other, however if you need to connect to a server that is not a GameMaker game, you can use network_connect_raw().

params.name: socket
params.description: The id of the socket to use.

params.name: url
params.description: The URL or IP to connect to.

functions.name: network_connect_async
functions.description: With this function you can send a request to connect to a server. The function takes the socket id to connect through and requires you to give the IP address to connect to as well as the port to connect through, and if the connection fails a value of less than 0 will be returned. The connection uses a special protocol that ensures only GameMaker games connect to each other, however if you need to connect to a server that is not a GameMaker game, you can use network_connect_raw_async().

functions.name: network_set_timeout
functions.description: With this function you can set the timeout for reading and writing data to/from a server through the given socket. Note that the timeout does not generate any type of event, so you will need to deal with timeouts yourself using alarms (for example).

functions.name: environment_get_variable
functions.description: This function returns the value of the environment variable with the given name.

functions.name: external_call
functions.description: If you have created an external function call to a dll or dylib using external_define(), you can use this function to then call it. You supply the name of the previously defined function as well as each of the arguments it requires (each argument must be of the correct type, either real or string) and the function returns the result of the external call.

functions.name: external_define

params.name: name

params.name: calltype

params.name: restype

functions.name: gml_pragma
functions.description: This function affects how the given target compiles your code and should be called with the different commands to further optimise the final compilation of your project. These commands are effectively pre-processed before the game is compiled and so the function can be placed anywhere in your project and it will still be processed before the game is fully compiled.

params.name: command
params.description: A string with one of the supported commands.
Optional argument or arguments for the given command.

functions.name: gml_release_mode

params.name: flag
params.description: Either true to set release mode or false for general development.

functions.name: os_check_permission
functions.description: With this function you can check to see if a specific permission has been granted to the game by the user. The function returns one of os_permission_granted, os_permission_denied, os_permission_denied_dont_request. See Android documentation for the permissions that can be requested.

params.name: permission
params.description: The permission to request

functions.name: os_get_config
functions.description: This function returns the name (as a string) of the currently selected configuration for your game.

functions.name: os_get_info
functions.description: This function returns a DS Map with detailed information about the OS that the game is running on. The exact information returned will depend on the OS and the device.

functions.name: os_get_language
functions.description: This function returns a string with the two letter Language Code for the OS that is running the game, as set by the ISO639 standard. If the information is not available, the function will return an empty string "", or "en" for "English" language.

functions.name: os_get_region
functions.description: This function returns a string with the two or three letter Regional Code for the OS that is running the game, as set by the ISO3166-1 standard. If the information is not available, it will hold simply an empty string "".

functions.name: os_is_network_connected
functions.description: With this function you can check if your device currently has an internet connection. Depending on the value of the attempt_connection argument and the OS, it may attempt to make a connection before returning a value.

params.name: attempt_connection
params.description: OPTIONAL! Set this parameter to a value other than network_connect_none to attempt an OS level connection when called.

functions.name: os_is_paused
functions.description: You can use this function to check if the device the game is running on is paused or not.

functions.name: os_lock_orientation

params.name: flag
params.description: Set to true or false to enable or disable orientation locking.

functions.name: os_set_orientation_lock

params.name: portrait_enable
params.description: true if portait orientation is allowed, false otherwise

functions.name: os_powersave_enable
functions.description: With this function you can turn on or off the power saving features of the device. This is important as certain games (for example those that use the tilt functions) may not generate events that the OS can interpret as being user input and so shut down the screen or exit the game. By setting this function to false you can disable the power saving features and ensure that the screen (and game) are always functioning.

params.name: flag
params.description: Set to true or false to enable or disable powersave functions.

functions.name: parameter_count

functions.name: scheduler_resolution_get

params.name: milliseconds
params.description: The new resolution value (in milliseconds) or -1 for default

functions.name: physics_debug

functions.name: physics_raycast
functions.description: This function checks the physics fixtures of the objects given against the ray specified, it will return an array of structures that will give the hitPointX, hitPointY (the room coordinates of the intersection), normalX, normalY (the normal of the intersection), fraction (the normalised distance down the ray of the intersection)

params.name: xStart
params.description: x position of the start of the ray.

params.name: yStart
params.description: y position of the start of the ray.

params.name: xEnd
params.description: x position of the start of the ray.

params.name: yEnd
params.description: y position of the start of the ray.

params.name: ids
params.description: instance or object id (or an array of instance or object ids) to check the ray against, these should have physics fixtures

params.name: all_hits
params.description: set to true if you want all hits returned, false if you want the closest hit only - defaults to false

params.name: max_fraction
params.description: proportion of the ray to check, defaults to 1.0, can be set to be smaller or larger

functions.name: physics_mass_properties

params.name: inertia

params.description: The object index or instance ID to check for, or one of the keywords all or other

functions.name: physics_fixture_add_point

Note that for a polygon shape, the points are relative to the origin of the fixture, with the (0, 0) position of the x/y axis being the centre, and the subsequent coordinates being calculated as usual in GameMaker with down/right being +x,+y and up/left being -x,-y.

params.name: fixture

params.name: xpos

Also note that using this function on a variable storing an array, a data structure, or a struct will convert the contents of these variables into a string which can then be output to the console or saved to a file for debugging. You are also able to use a format string with "{x}" placeholders (i.e. {0},{1},...) where 'X' is the argument number after the format string (starting at 0).

functions.name: string_char_at
